PAITE: Huan, Labanin a dawnga, Jakob kiangah, tanute kei tanu ahi ua, naupangte kei naupangte ahi ua, gante kei gante ahi ua, na muh tengteng keia vek ahi uh: tuniin hiai ka tanute tungah leh a ta neihte uh tungah bang ka hih thei dia?
ENGLISH: Laban answered Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine: and what can I do this day to these my daughters, or to their children whom they have borne?

PAITE: Kisain, kei leh nang thu I khung ding; huai kei leh nang kalah theihna hi hen, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Now come, let us make a covenant, you and I; and let it be for a witness between me and you.”

PAITE: Huchiin, Jakobin suang a laa, suangphuh dingin a phuta.
ENGLISH: Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.

PAITE: Huan, Jakobin a unaute kiangah, suang la khawm un, a chi a; huan, suang a la ua, achiang ua: huan, suangchian khawm kiangah an a ne uh.
ENGLISH: Jacob said to his relatives, “Gather stones.” They took stones, and made a heap. They ate there by the heap.

PAITE: Huan, Labanin huai suang chian khawm, Jegarsahadutha, a chi a; Jakobin bel Galeed, a chi hi.
ENGLISH: Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, “Jegar Sahadutha” means “Witness Heap” in Aramaic. but Jacob called it Galeed. “Galeed” means “Witness Heap” in Hebrew.

PAITE: Huan, Labanin, hiai suang chian khawm tuiin kei leh nang kikalah theihna ahi, a chi a. Huaijiakin a min dingin Galeed chih a hita:
ENGLISH: Laban said, “This heap is witness between me and you this day.” Therefore it was named Galeed

PAITE: Mizpa chih leng ahi, Labanin, kikhen a I om hun chiangin TOUPAN honveng tuaktuak hen,
ENGLISH: and Mizpah, for he said, “Yahweh watch between me and you, when we are absent one from another.

PAITE: Ka tanute na suk gentheiha, ka tanute lou ji dang na neih leh, kuamah i kiangah a om kei na ua, enin, Pathian kei leh nang kal hontheihpihpa ahi, a chi ngala.
ENGLISH: If you afflict my daughters, or if you take wives besides my daughters, no man is with us; behold, God is witness between me and you.”

PAITE: Huan, Laban mahin, hiai suang chian khawm en lechin, keimah leh nangmah kikala hiai suang ka phuh leng enin.
ENGLISH: Laban said to Jacob, “See this heap, and see the pillar, which I have set between me and you.

PAITE: Poi kikhoihsak dingin kei hiai suang khengin na kiang lamah ka hongpai kei ding, chih leh, nang leng hiai suang chian khawm leh hiai suang phuh khengin kei kiang lamah na hongpai kei ding chih, hiai suang chian a theihna hi henla, hiai suangphuh leng a theihna mah hi hen.
ENGLISH: May this heap be a witness, and the pillar be a witness, that I will not pass over this heap to you, and that you will not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.

PAITE: Abraham Pathian, Nahor Pathian, a pa uh Pathianin I kalah thu ngaihtuah hen, a chi nawna. Huan, Jakobin a pa Isaak kihtak louin a kichiamta.
ENGLISH: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” Then Jacob swore by the fear of his father, Isaac.

PAITE: Huan, Jakobin tang ah kithoihna a lana a unaute tanghou ne dingin a sama; huchiin tanghou a ne ua, tang ah a giak chiat uhi.Huan, jingsang in beltakin Laban a thoua, a tute leh a tanute a tawpa, a vualjawla: huan, Laban a paia, amah omna lamah a pai
ENGLISH: Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his relatives to eat bread. They ate bread, and stayed all night in the mountain.

PAITE: Huan, jingsang in beltakin Laban a thoua, a tute leh a tanute a tawpa, a vualjawla: huan, Laban a paia, amah omna lamah a pai
ENGLISH: Early in the morning, Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. Laban departed and returned to his place.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob bel a pai jela, huan, Pathian angelten a na dawn uh.
ENGLISH: Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

PAITE: Huan, Jakobin amau a muhin, hiaite Pathian pawlte ahi uh, achia: huchiin huai mun minin Mahanaim a chi hi.
ENGLISH: When he saw them, Jacob said, “This is God’s army.” He called the name of that place Mahanaim.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob in, Seir gam a, Edom pawn lamah, a u Esau kiangah a maah thangkoute a paisaka.
ENGLISH: Jacob sent messengers in front of him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.

PAITE: A kianguah, ka toupa Esau a kiangah hichiin na gen ding uh, na sikha Jakobin hichiin a chi hi: Laban kiangah mikhual ka hia, tu tanin ka om nilouha:
ENGLISH: He commanded them, saying, “This is what you shall tell my lord, Esau: ‘This is what your servant, Jacob, says. I have lived as a foreigner with Laban, and stayed until now.

PAITE: Bawngtalte, sabengtung leh belamte, sikhapa leh sikhanute khawng ka neia; hichiin na hehpihna ka muh theihna dingin ka toupa hilh dingin mi ka honsawl ahi, a chi a, chiin, amau thu a pia hi.
ENGLISH: I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants. I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in your sight.’”

PAITE: Huan, thangkoute Jakob kiangah a hong kik nawn ua, Na u Esau kiang ka va tung ua, huan, mi za li honpiin hongdawn dingin a hongpai hi, chiin, a gen ua.
ENGLISH: The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau. Not only that, but he comes to meet you, and four hundred men with him.”

PAITE: Huchiin, Jakobin a lau mahmah a, a lungkhamta a: huchiin a kianga mi omte, belam honte, bawng honte, sangawngsaute pawl nihin a khen a;
ENGLISH: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and was distressed. He divided the people who were with him, and the flocks, and the herds, and the camels, into two companies;

PAITE: Esau pawl khat a hongpaia, a thah leh, pawl khat om lai a tai mang thei ding, a
ENGLISH: and he said, “If Esau comes to the one company, and strikes it, then the company which is left will escape.”

PAITE: Huan, Jakob mahin, aw Toupa, na gam lamah leh na tanute kiangah pai nawnta in, huchiin ka honhih hoih ding, honchipa:
ENGLISH: Jacob said, “God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, Yahweh, who said to me, ‘Return to your country, and to your relatives, and I will do you good,’

PAITE: Na sikha tunga hehpihna tengteng na muhsak leh thutak tengteng na muhsak laka, a neupen leng mu tuak ka hi kei hi; hiai Jordan lui ka chiang kia toh ka kana; tuin jaw pawl nih hial ka honghita hi.
ENGLISH: I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to your servant; for with just my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I have become two companies.

PAITE: Hehpihtakin ka u khut akipan, Esau khut akipan, hon humbit in; numei naupang takna honthah lah ka lau ngala.
ENGLISH: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he come and strike me, and the mothers with the children.

PAITE: Nang, ka hon hihhoih ngeingei dinga, na suante tuipi a piaunel sim zohlouh tan hiala tam bangin ka bawl ding na chi a, a chi a.
ENGLISH: You said, ‘I will surely do you good, and make your seed as the sand of the sea, which can’t be numbered because there are so many.’”

PAITE: Huan, huai jan in huailaiah a giakta a; huan, a neih laka kipan a u Esau adingin kipahman a lakhia;
ENGLISH: He lodged there that night, and took from that which he had with him, a present for Esau, his brother:

PAITE: Kelpi zanih, keltal sawmnih, belampi zanih leh belampa sawmnih,
ENGLISH: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

PAITE: Sangawngsau zatlai sawmthum a noute utoh, bawngpi sawmli leh bawngtal sawm, sabengtungpi sawm nih leh sabengtung nou sawm.
ENGLISH: thirty milk camels and their colts, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.

PAITE: Huan, huaite pawl chih a tuam chiatin a sikhate khut ah a kemsaka; huan, a sikhate kiangah, ka maah pai galkah unla, pawl chih kal nei sak jel un, a chi a.
ENGLISH: He delivered them into the hands of his servants, every herd by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass over before me, and put a space between herd and herd.”

PAITE: Huan, a makai pa kiangah, ka u Esauin hontuaha, na kianga, kua na hia? kaw hoh dek na hia? na maa omte kuaa ahi ua? chia a hondot leh,
ENGLISH: He commanded the foremost, saying, “When Esau, my brother, meets you, and asks you, saying, ‘Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these before you?’

PAITE: Na sikha Jakob a ahi uh; ka pu Esau, nanga dia kipahman dinga honkhak ahi: ngaiin, amah hua ka nung uah a om, chiin, thu a pia hi.
ENGLISH: Then you shall say, ‘They are your servant, Jacob’s. It is a present sent to my lord, Esau. Behold, he also is behind us.’”

PAITE: Huan, a zom leh a zom nawn leh, gan hon hawlte tengteng kiangah leng, Esau na muh hun chiang un huchibang mahin na gen ding uh ahi.
ENGLISH: He commanded also the second, and the third, and all that followed the herds, saying, “This is how you shall speak to Esau, when you find him.

PAITE: Huan, ngaiin, na sikha hua ka nung uah a om, chi chiat un, chiin thu a pe chiat hi. Kipahman ka maah pai leh a lung ka damsak ding a, huai nungin a mel ka mu ding; huchiin, a honna kipahpih kha ding, a chi ahi.
ENGLISH: You shall say, ‘Not only that, but behold, your servant, Jacob, is behind us.’” For, he said, “I will appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face. Perhaps he will accept me.”

PAITE: Huchiin, kipahman a maah a pai galkah saka; amah bel, huai janin a pawlte lakah a giak hi.
ENGLISH: So the present passed over before him, and he himself lodged that night in the camp.

PAITE: Huan, janin a thoua, a ji nih leh, a sikhanu nihte leh a ta sawm leh khat te a pi a, Jabbok lui ngahna ah a pita.
ENGLISH: He rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two handmaids, and his eleven sons, and passed over the ford of the Jabbok.

PAITE: Huchiin, a mau a pi a, lui a kan ua, a neih tengteng leng a kansak vek hi.
ENGLISH: He took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that which he had.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob amah kia in a omta; huan, mi khat toh phalvak tan a kibuan buan
ENGLISH: Jacob was left alone, and wrestled with a man there until the breaking of the day.

PAITE: Huan, a zou kei chih a kitheihin a pheipi guhtuah a khoihsak a, huchiin a kibuan lai un Jakob pheipi guhtuah a kilawita hi.
ENGLISH: When he saw that he didn’t prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was strained, as he wrestled.

PAITE: Huan, aman, hon khah in, phalvak ding a hita, a chi a. Huan, aman, na hon vualjawl keileh ka hon khah kei ding, achia.
ENGLISH: The man said, “Let me go, for the day breaks.” Jacob said, “I won’t let you go, unless you bless me.”

PAITE: Huan, aman, a kiangah, na min bang ahia? Achia. Huan, aman, Jakob a chi a
ENGLISH: He said to him, “What is your name?” He said, “Jacob.”

PAITE: Huan, aman, na min Jakob ahi nawn kei ding, Israel a honchi zota ding uh; Pathian leh mihing te na suala, na zouta ngala, achia.
ENGLISH: He said, “Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have fought with God and with men, and have prevailed.”

PAITE: Huan, Jakobin, amah a dawnga, hehpihtakin na min honhilh in, a chi a. Huan, aman, bangjiakin ahia ka min non dot? Achia. Huan, huailaiah a vualjawlta.
ENGLISH: Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.” He said, “Why is it that you ask what my name is?” He blessed him there.

PAITE: Huan, Jakobin huailai mun ding in Peniel a chi a: Pathian a ma chin mahmah ah ka mu a, ka hinna hon hawisak jiakin a chi a.
ENGLISH: Jacob called the name of the place Peniel Peniel means “face of God.” : for, he said, “I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”

PAITE: Huan, Peniel a khen laiin a ni a hongsuak a, amah a hon suna, a pheipi jiakin a bai ta hi.Huaijiakin tutanin Israel suanten pheipi guhtuah a sadual om a ne ngei kei uh: Jakob pheipi guhtuah a sadual lai tak a khoih jiakin.
ENGLISH: The sun rose on him as he passed over Peniel, and he limped because of his thigh.

PAITE: Huaijiakin tutanin Israel suanten pheipi guhtuah a sadual om a ne ngei kei uh: Jakob pheipi guhtuah a sadual lai tak a khoih jiakin.
ENGLISH: Therefore the children of Israel don’t eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew of the hip.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob a daka, hua, ngaiin, Esau a kianga mi zali toh a hongpaia. Huchiin, a tate Lea kiangah te, Rakil kiangah te, sikhanu kiangah te a om khipkhep ua.
ENGLISH: Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children between Leah, Rachel, and the two handmaids.

PAITE: Huan, sikhanute leh a tate uh a makai penin a koiha, Lea leh a tate a zomin a koiha, Rakil leh Joseph bel a nanung penin a koih hi.
ENGLISH: He put the handmaids and their children in front, Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.

PAITE: Huan, amah a ma uah a paia, a u kiang chin a tun masiah sagih vei lei siin chibai a buk hi.
ENGLISH: He himself passed over in front of them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.

PAITE: Huan, Esau amah kipahpih dingin a taia, a poma, a ngawnga kunin, a tawpa: Huan, a kap khawm uhi.
ENGLISH: Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.

PAITE: Huan, Esau a daka, numeite leh naupangte a mua; huchiin, non pite kuate ahi ua? a chi a. Huan, aman, Pathianin hehpihtaka na sikha kianga a piak naupangte ahi uh, a chi a.
ENGLISH: He lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, “Who are these with you?” He said, “The children whom God has graciously given your servant.”

PAITE: Huchiin, sikhanute, amau leh a tate uh toh a hongpai ua, a kun ua, chibai a buk uh.
ENGLISH: Then the handmaids came near with their children, and they bowed themselves.

PAITE: Huan, Lea leng a tate toh a hongpai naia, a kun ua, chibai a buk uh; huan, huai nungin Joseph leh Rakil a hongpai nai ua, a kun ua, chibai a buk sam uhi.
ENGLISH: Leah also and her children came near, and bowed themselves. After them, Joseph came near with Rachel, and they bowed themselves.

PAITE: Huan, Esauin, ka gan hon kituahpih tengpi bangchidan ahia? a chi a. Huan, aman, Ka toupa, na hehpihna ka muh theihna dingin ka chi a ahi, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Esau said, “What do you mean by all this company which I met?” Jacob said, “To find favor in the sight of my lord.”

PAITE: Huan, Esauin, ken leng hau veng e, bawi aw, na neih tengteng nanga hi hen, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Esau said, “I have enough, my brother; let that which you have be yours.”

PAITE: Huan, Jakobin, Hilou e, non hehpih theihna leh, hehpihtakin kon kipahman piakte hon sansak in: Pathian mel mu bangin na mel ka mu a, ka tungah lah na kipak ngala.
ENGLISH: Jacob said, “Please, no, if I have now found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me.

PAITE: Pathianin hon hehpih jiak leh, ka hauh jiakin ka hon thilpiakte sangin, a chi a. Huchiin a kunkun a, a sangta hi.
ENGLISH: Please take the gift that I brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough.” He urged him, and he took it.

PAITE: Huan, Esauin, Kisain, I pai ding, ma kon kaihsak ding, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Esau said, “Let us take our journey, and let us go, and I will go before you.”

PAITE: Huan, aman, a kiangah, naupangte a neu lai dan u leh, belam hon ka kianga omte a nou a hih dan uh, ka toupa, na thei hi; khat lel leng hat lua a a hawl uleh, ganhon tengteng a si mai ding uh.
ENGLISH: Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.

PAITE: Ka toupa, hehpihtakin na sikha maah pai inla: Ken bel Seir tang ah, ka toupa, na kiang ka tun mateng, ka ma a gan pai a pai theih hun bangbang u leh, naupangte pai theih hun bangbangin, awlawl in ka hon masuan jel ding hi a chi a.
ENGLISH: Please let my lord pass over before his servant, and I will lead on gently, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir.”

PAITE: Huan, Esauin, ka kianga om mi khenkhat te hon nutsiat beh leng ake, a chi a. Huan, aman, bang a chi chitchiat a? A chia.
ENGLISH: Esau said, “Let me now leave with you some of the folk who are with me.” He said, “Why? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.”

PAITE: Huchiin, Esau huai ni mahin Seir tang lam juanin a kiknawnta hi.
ENGLISH: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob Sukkoth min ah a paia, amah ading in a lama, a gante ading leng bukta te alama; huaijiakin huailai mun min dingin Sukkoth a chita hi.
ENGLISH: Jacob traveled to Succoth, built himself a house, and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore the name of the place is called Succoth. succoth means shelters or booths.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob Paddan-aram gam akipan a honga, lungmuang takin Sekem khua, Kanan gam a om, a tunga, dainawla ah a puanin a jakta hi.
ENGLISH: Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan Aram; and encamped before the city.

PAITE: Huan, a puanin jak na mun, Sekem pa Hamor tate akipan, dangka ja in a lei.Huailaiah maitam a doha, a min ding El-elohe-Israel a chi.
ENGLISH: He bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.

PAITE: Huailaiah maitam a doha, a min ding El-elohe-Israel a chi.
ENGLISH: He erected an altar there, and called it El Elohe Israel. El Elohe Israel means “God, the God of Israel” or “The God of Israel is mighty.”

PAITE: Huan, Lea tanu Dina, Jakob a neihsak, huai gam nungak te mu dingin a pawtkhia.
ENGLISH: Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

PAITE: Huan, Hiv mi Hamor, huai gam lal tapa Sekemin amah a na mua; a mana, a luppih a, a ninsak hi.
ENGLISH: Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. He took her, lay with her, and humbled her.

PAITE: Huan, a lungsim Jakob tanu Dina tungah a om bikbeka, huai nungak lah a ita, amah kamsiam takin a houpiha.
ENGLISH: His soul joined to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young lady, and spoke kindly to the young lady.

PAITE: Huan, Sekem in a pa Hamor a houpiha, huai nungak ji dingin honnei sakin, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Shechem spoke to his father, Hamor, saying, “Get me this young lady as a wife.”

PAITE: Huan, Jakobin a tanu Dina a ninsak khin chih a ja a; a tate gamlak ah a gan lak uah a om ua: huchiin, a hongtun mateng uh Jakob a dai dide hi.
ENGLISH: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah, his daughter; and his sons were with his livestock in the field. Jacob held his peace until they came.

PAITE: Huan, Sekem pa Hamor Jakob houpih dingin a kiangah a hoha.
ENGLISH: Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to talk with him.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob tapaten a jak tak un gamlak akipanin a hongpaita ua: huan, Jakob tanu luppihin Israelte laka thil gilou haihuaitak, thil hih hetlouh ding, a hih jiakin a lungkham ua, a heh mahmah uh.
ENGLISH: The sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it. The men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had done folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter; a which thing ought not to be done.

PAITE: Huan, Hamorin a mau a houpiha, ka tapa Sekem lungsim na tanu uh tungah a om bikbeka: hehpihtakin ji dingin nei sak ve ua.
ENGLISH: Hamor talked with them, saying, “The soul of my son, Shechem, longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.

PAITE: Huchiin, ki la tuah ve ni e; na tanute uh hon lasak unla, ka tanute uleng lasam un.
ENGLISH: Make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.

PAITE: Huchiin, ka kiang uah na om ding ua; gam leng a kiching gige ding: hiai khawngah om unla, sum sin unla, hiai khawngah kihih inbul un, a chi a.
ENGLISH: You shall dwell with us, and the land will be before you. Live and trade in it, and get possessions in it.”

PAITE: Huan, Sekemin nungak pa leh a sanggampa te kiangah, honhehpih ve ua, ka kianga na gen peuh uh ka honpe ding.
ENGLISH: Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you will tell me I will give.

PAITE: Man leh thilpiak jaw bang zah bang zah ngen le uchin, na chih bangbang un k a honpe ding: abang hileh, nungak pen ji dingin hon neisak phot un, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Ask me a great amount for a dowry, and I will give whatever you ask of me, but give me the young lady as a wife.”

PAITE: Huan, Jakob taten, a sanggamnu uh Dina a nitsak jiakin. Sekem leh a pa Hamor zekhemna in a dawng ua, a gen sam ua, a kiang uah.
ENGLISH: The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit, and spoke, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,

PAITE: Hiai thil zeksumloute kianga ka tanu uh piak pen ka hih theikei ding uh; huailah kou dingin minsiatna ahi ngala:
ENGLISH: and said to them, “We can’t do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.

PAITE: Hichibanga kichiam kiain na thu bang uh pha ka sa ding uh: na lak ua pasal peuhpeuh zeksumin kou bangin om unla;
ENGLISH: Only on this condition will we consent to you. If you will be as we are, that every male of you be circumcised;

PAITE: Huchiin ka tanute uh kon neisak ding uh, kou leng na tanute uh ka nei sam ding uh, huan, na kiang uah ka om ding ua, chi khat hi ding I hi.
ENGLISH: then will we give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.

PAITE: Himahleh, zeksum thu a ka thu uh na zuih kei ding u leh ka tanu uh ka pi ding ua, kapai mai ding uh, a chi ua.
ENGLISH: But if you will not listen to us, to be circumcised, then we will take our sister, Hebrew has, literally, “daughter” and we will be gone.”

PAITE: Huan, a thu un Hamor leh Hamor tapa Sekem a kipaksak hi.
ENGLISH: Their words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.

PAITE: Huchiin, tangval in bel Jakob tanu a deih mahmah jiakin, huai thil sawt hallou in a hih tamai hi: amah a pa inkuante inkuan tengteng laka mite zahtak pen ahi hi.
ENGLISH: The young man didn’t wait to do this thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he was honored above all the house of his father.

PAITE: Huan, Hamor leh a tapa Sekem in a kho kulh kongkhak uh a pha ua, a khuate uh a houpih ua,
ENGLISH: Hamor and Shechem, his son, came to the gate of their city, and talked with the men of their city, saying,

PAITE: Hua jite hon kituahpih takin a om ua; huaijiakin hiai gamah omin, hiai khawng ah sumsin uhen; ngai un, amau dingin gam lah a za hun ngal a; a tanute uh ji dingin nei lehang, i tanute leng neisak sam ni.
ENGLISH: “These men are peaceful with us. Therefore let them live in the land and trade in it. For behold, the land is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.

PAITE: Himahleh chi khat i hong hihna dinga I kianga om hichibanga I chiam kia in hua miten pha a honsakpih ding uhi, zeksum a hih uh bangin I lak ua pasal peuhpeuh zeksum hong hita lehang.
ENGLISH: Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people, if every male among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised.

PAITE: A gante uh, a sum te uh, a sa tengteng uh eia ahi vek kei dia hia? A thu uh pha sakpih mai ve ni, huchiin I kianga om ding uhi, achi ua.
ENGLISH: Won’t their livestock and their possessions and all their animals be ours? Only let us give our consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”

PAITE: Huan, Hamor leh a tapa Sekem thu a kho kulh kongkhak a pawt tengteng in a jui ua; a kho kulh kongkhak a pawt tengteng pasal peuhpeuh, zek a sumsak uhi.
ENGLISH: All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor, and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.

PAITE: Huan, hichi ahia, a ni thum ni in, a gim laitak un, Jakob tapate laka mi nih, Dina sanggampa Simeon leh Levi in a namsau uh tawi tuaktuak in a gukin khua a sualta ua, pasal tengteng a that gam uh.
ENGLISH: It happened on the third day, when they were sore, that two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came upon the unsuspecting city, and killed all the males.

PAITE: Huchiin, Hamor leh a tapa Sekem namsau hiam in a that ua, Sekem in akipan in Dina a pi ua, a pawt uh.
ENGLISH: They killed Hamor and Shechem, his son, with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.

PAITE: Jakob tapaten a mi thah te uh a va pha nawn ua, a tanu uh a nitsak jiak un huai khua a lokta uhi.
ENGLISH: Jacob’s sons came on the dead, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.

PAITE: A belam honte uh, a bawng honte uh, a sabengtung te uh, a khua ua thil omte, a lou ua thil omte a laksak ua:
ENGLISH: They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, that which was in the city, that which was in the field,

PAITE: A sum tengteng u leh, a ta a nau neu chik chik leh a jite tengteng, in sunga om peuhmah a man ua, a lok uhi.
ENGLISH: and all their wealth. They took captive all their little ones and their wives, and took as plunder everything that was in the house.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob in Simeon leh Levi kiangah, nou hiai gam a omte laka, Kanan te leh Periz te lakah, huat non posak ua non lungjing sak mahmah uh: kei tawmchik ka hih jiakin honsual dingin a kikhawm khawm ding ua, hon that mai ding uh; huchiin, hih mangin ka om dinga, kei leh ka inkuanpihte toh, achia.Huan, amau, ka sanggamnu uh kijuak bawl bangin a bawl ding ahi diam? A chi uhi.
ENGLISH: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am few in number. They will gather themselves together against me and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my house.”

PAITE: Huan, amau, ka sanggamnu uh kijuak bawl bangin a bawl ding ahi diam? A chi uhi.
ENGLISH: They said, “Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute?”

PAITE: Huan, Pathianin, Jakob kiangah, thou inla, Bethel ah hohtou in, huailaiah om in: huan, na u Esau kianga kipan a na tai mang laia na kianga kilak Pathian a dingin huailaiah maitam dohin, achia.
ENGLISH: God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and live there. Make there an altar to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother.”

PAITE: Huchiin, Jakob in a inkuanpihte leh a kianga om tengteng kiangah, na lak ua mi dang Pathian omte koih mang unla, ki hih siangthou unla, na puansilh te uh kheng un:
ENGLISH: Then Jacob said to his household, and to all who were with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, purify yourselves, change your garments.

PAITE: I thou ding ua, Bethel ah I paitou ding uh; huchiin, ka lungjin laia hon dawng, ka paina a ka kianga omjel Pathian a dingin maitam ka doh ding hi, achia.
ENGLISH: Let us arise, and go up to Bethel. I will make there an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.”

PAITE: Huchiin, mi dang Pathian a khut ua om tengteng leh a bil ua bilbah a bah tengteng uh Jakob kiangah a pia ua; huan, Jakob in Sekem kho kianga tosaw nuaiah a selta hi.
ENGLISH: They gave to Jacob all the foreign gods which were in their hands, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.

PAITE: Huan, a pai ua: a kim ua khuate un a kihta mahmah ua, Jakob tapate a delh kei uh.
ENGLISH: They traveled, and a terror of God was on the cities that were around them, and they didn’t pursue the sons of Jacob.

PAITE: Huchiin, Jakob Kanan gama Luz khua a tunga, amah leh a kianga om tengteng toh (Luz Bethel ahi).
ENGLISH: So Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.

PAITE: Huan, huaiah maitam a doha, a u kianga kipana a taimang lai in huailaiah Pathian a kianga a kilak jiakin, huai mun El-Bethel a chita hi.
ENGLISH: He built an altar there, and called the place El Beth El; because there God was revealed to him, when he fled from the face of his brother.

PAITE: Huan, Rebeka honnu Debor a si a, Bethel nuaia tosaw nuaiah a vui ua; a tosaw min Allonbakuth a chi uh.
ENGLISH: Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and its name was called Allon Bacuth.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob Paddan-aram gam akipana a hongtun in Pathian a kiangah a kilak nawna, a vualjawla.
ENGLISH: God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him.

PAITE: Pathianin a kiangah, na min Jakob ahi a; na min Jakob ahi nawnta kei ding, na min Israel a hizota ding, achia: huchiin, a min dingin Israel a chita hi.
ENGLISH: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be Jacob any more, but your name will be Israel.” He named him Israel.

PAITE: Huan, Pathian mahin a kiangah, kei Pathian bangkim hihthei ka hi: chi tampi suangin hong pungin; chi chih tham ngial leh chi tuamtuam om khawm leng nangah a hong om ding ua, na khal a kipanin kumpipate leng a hongpawt ding uh;
ENGLISH: God said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings will come out of your body.

PAITE: Huan, Abraham leh Isaak kianga ka gam piak na kiangah ka honpe ding, na om louh nung chianga na suante kiangah leng gam jaw ka pe jel ding, achia.
ENGLISH: The land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give it to you, and to your seed after you will I give the land.”

PAITE: Huan, Pathianin amah a houpih na mun a kipan in Jakob a paitouh santa.
ENGLISH: God went up from him in the place where he spoke with him.

PAITE: Huan, a houpih na mun ah Jakob in banghiam a suana, (suang ahi, a phuh): a tungah thil lat, dawn chi, a buaka, a tungah sathau leng a buak hi.
ENGLISH: Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of stone. He poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob in, Pathian in a houpih na mun min dingin Bethel asa hi.
ENGLISH: Jacob called the name of the place where God spoke with him “Bethel.”

PAITE: Huan, Bethel akipan in a pai ua; huan, Ephrath kho tunna ding gamla tak ahi laia: huan, Rakil in nau a veia, a nak vei mahmah a.
ENGLISH: They traveled from Bethel. There was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and Rachel travailed. She had hard labor.

PAITE: Huan, hichi ahia, a gim laitakin nau dom miin, lau ken: tapa dang na nei dinga hi, achia.
ENGLISH: When she was in hard labor, the midwife said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for now you will have another son.”

PAITE: Huan, hichi ahia, a kha a pawt dek laiin (a sita ngala) a min dingin Ben-oni a sa a: a pan bel Benjamin a sa hi.
ENGLISH: It happened, as her soul was departing (for she died), that she named him Benoni, “Benoni” means “son of my trouble.” but his father named him Benjamin. “Benjamin” means “son of my right hand.”

PAITE: Huchiin, Rakil a sia, Ephrath lampi ah a vui ua (Ephrath khua Bethlehem khua ahi).
ENGLISH: Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath (the same is Bethlehem).

PAITE: Huan, a han tungah Jakob in suang a phuta: huai tutanin Rakil han suangphuh ahi lai hi.
ENGLISH: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave. The same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.

PAITE: Huan, Israel bel a pai jela, Migdol Eder khen lamah a puanin a kaia.
ENGLISH: Israel traveled, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder.

PAITE: Huan, hichi ahia, Israel huai gama om laiin Reuben in a pa mei Bilha a valuppiha: huan, Israel in huai a ja a.
ENGLISH: It happened, while Israel lived in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard of it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob tapate sawm leh nih ahi ua: Lea tapate Reuben (Jakob ta masa) te, Simeon te, Levi te, Juda te, Issakar te, Zebulun te ahi uhi:
ENGLISH: The sons of Leah: Reuben (Jacob’s firstborn), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.

PAITE: Rakil tapate Joseph leh Benjamin ahi ua:
ENGLISH: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

PAITE: Rakil sikhanu Bilha tapate Dan leh Napthali ahi ua:
ENGLISH: The sons of Bilhah (Rachel’s handmaid): Dan and Naphtali.

PAITE: Huan, Lea sikhanu Zilpa tapate Gad leh Aser ahi ua: huaite Jakob tapa, Paddan-aram gama a neihte ahi uh.
ENGLISH: The sons of Zilpah (Leah’s handmaid): Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan Aram.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob Kiriath-arba khua a Abraham leh Isaak omna Mamrea a pa Isaak kiang a tungta. (Kiriath-arba khua Hebron ahi).
ENGLISH: Jacob came to Isaac his father, to Mamre, to Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac lived as foreigners.

PAITE: Huan, Isaak damsung kum ja leh kum sawm giat ahi.Huan, Isaakin a kha a khah a, upapi tek kuna damin a si a, a chipihte kiangah piin a om samta: huan, a tapa Esau leh Jakob in a vuita uhi.
ENGLISH: The days of Isaac were one hundred eighty years.

PAITE: Huan, Isaakin a kha a khah a, upapi tek kuna damin a si a, a chipihte kiangah piin a om samta: huan, a tapa Esau leh Jakob in a vuita uhi.
ENGLISH: Isaac gave up the spirit, and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Esau suante ahi uh (Esau Edom ahi).
ENGLISH: Now this is the history of the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).

PAITE: Esauin a jite Kanan gama nungakte laka a neih ahi; Hit mi Elon tanu Ada leh, Hiv mi Zibeon tanu, Ana Tanu Oholibamte ahi uh;
ENGLISH: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon, the Hittite; and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the Hivite;

PAITE: Ismael tanu, Nebaioth sanggamnu Basemath toh.
ENGLISH: and Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth.

PAITE: Huan, Ada in Eliphaz Esau a neihsaka; Basemath in Reuel a neia;
ENGLISH: Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz. Basemath bore Reuel.

PAITE: Oholibam in Jeus leh Jalam leh Korah a neia; huaite Esau tapa, Kanan gama a neihte ahi uh.
ENGLISH: Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

PAITE: Huan, Esauin a jite leh, a tapate leh, a tanute leh, a in a mi tengteng leh, a gante leh, a sa tengteng leh, a sum tengteng, Kanan gama a muhte a paipih, a nau Jakob kianga kipan gamdang ah a pai mangta hi.
ENGLISH: Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the members of his household, with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions, which he had gathered in the land of Canaan, and went into a land away from his brother Jacob.

PAITE: A thilneihte uh a thupi lua a, a om khawm theikei uhi; a gante jiakin mikhual a a omna gam un lah a chinta kei hi.
ENGLISH: For their substance was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their travels couldn’t bear them because of their livestock.

PAITE: Huchiin, Esau tangah a omta: Esau tuh Edom ahi.
ENGLISH: Esau lived in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Seir tang a Edom te suangpa Esau suante ahi uh:
ENGLISH: This is the history of the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in the hill country of Seir:

PAITE: Hiaite Esau tapate minte ahi: Eliphaz Esau ji Ada tapa Reuel Esau ji Basemath ta.
ENGLISH: these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau; and Reuel, the son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

PAITE: Huan, Eliphaz tapate Tamante Omarte, Zephote, Gatamte, Kenazte ahi uh.
ENGLISH: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.

PAITE: Huan, Timna tuh Esau tapa Eliphaz mei ahia; aman Eliphaz Amalek a neihsaka: Huaite Esau ji Ada suante ahi uh.
ENGLISH: Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, Esau’s son; and she bore to Eliphaz Amalek. These are the sons of Adah, Esau’s wife.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Reuel tapate ahi uh; Nahath leh Zerahte, Samma leh Mizzate: huaite Esau ji Basemath suante ahi uh.
ENGLISH: These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Zibeon tanu Ana tanu Esau ji Oholibam tapate ahi uh: aman Esau Jeus leh Jalam leh Koran a neihsak hi.
ENGLISH: These were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s wife: she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

PAITE: Hiaite Esau tapate laka heutute ahi uh: Esau ta chil Eliphaz tapate; heutu Temante, heutu Omarte, heutu Zephote, heutu Kenazte,
ENGLISH: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,

PAITE: Heutu Korah te, heutu Gatamte, heutu Amalek te: huaite Edom gam a Eliphaz akipana pawt heutute ahi uh; huaite Ada suante ahi uh.
ENGLISH: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek: these are the chiefs who came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Esau tapa Reuel suante ahi uh; heutu Nahath te, heutu Zerahte, heutu Samma te, Heutu Mizzate: huaite Edom gam a Reuel akipana pawt heutute ahi uh; huaite Esau ji Basemath suante ahi uhi.
ENGLISH: These are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah: these are the chiefs who came of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Esau ji Oholibam suante ahi uh; heutu Jeus te, heutu Jalam te, heutu Korah te: huaite heutu Ana tanu Esau ji Oholibam suante ahi uh.
ENGLISH: These are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah: these are the chiefs who came of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau’s wife.

PAITE: Huaite Esau tapate ahi uh, huaite a lak ua heutute ahi uh: Esau tuh Edom ahi.
ENGLISH: These are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these are their chiefs.

PAITE: Hiaite Hor mi Seir tapa huai gama omte ahi uh; Lotan te, Sobal te, Zibeon te, Ana te, Dison te, Ezer te, Disan te,
ENGLISH: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

PAITE: Huaite Edom gama Seir ta Horta laka kipana pawt heutute ahi uh.
ENGLISH: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs who came of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.

PAITE: Huan, Lotan tate Hor leh Hemam ahi uh. Lotan sanggamnu Timna ahi.
ENGLISH: The children of Lotan were Hori and Heman. Lotan’s sister was Timna.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Sobal tate ahi uh; Alvan te, Manahath te, Ebalt e, Sepho te, Onam te.
ENGLISH: These are the children of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Zibeon tate ahi uh; Aia leh Ana: hiai Ana ahi, apa Zibeon sabengtungte a khah laia gamdaia tui sa khuk te mukhepa.
ENGLISH: These are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness, as he fed the donkeys of Zibeon his father.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite Dison tate ahi uh; Dison leh Ana tanu Oholibam.
ENGLISH: These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.

PAITE: Hiaite Disan tate ahi uh; Uz leh Aran.
ENGLISH: These are the children of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.

PAITE: Hiaite Horte laka kipana pawt heutute ahi uh; heutu Lotan te, heutu Sobal te, heutu Zibeon te, heutu Ana te,
ENGLISH: These are the children of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

PAITE: Heutu Dison te, heutu Ezer te, heutu Disan te: huaite Seir gama a heutu uh dan banga Horte laka kipana pawt a heutute ahi uh.
ENGLISH: These are the children of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

PAITE: Hiaite, kumpipa kuamah in Israel suante tunga vai a hawm ma ua, Edom gama vaihawm kumpipate ahi uhi.
ENGLISH: These are the chiefs who came of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,

PAITE: Huan. Beor tapa Velin Edom gama vai a hawma; a khopi min Dinhaba ahi.
ENGLISH: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, and chief Dishan: these are the chiefs who came of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.

PAITE: Huan, Vel a si a, Bozra khua a mi Zerah tapa Jobab in a sikin vai a hawm ta.
ENGLISH: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel.

PAITE: Huan, Jobab a si a, Timante gam a mi Husam-in a sikin vai a hawm ta a.
ENGLISH: Bela, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom. The name of his city was Dinhabah.

PAITE: Huan, Husam a si a, Bedad tapa Hadad, tapa Hadad, Moab pawn a Midiante that pan, a sikin vai a hawma: a khopi min Avith ahi.
ENGLISH: Bela died, and Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, reigned in his place.

PAITE: Huan, Hadad a si a, Masrek mi Samla in a sikin vai a hawm.
ENGLISH: Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

PAITE: Huan, Samla a si a, Luipi gei a Rebototh khua a mi Saula in a sikin vai a hawm hi.
ENGLISH: Husham died, and Hadad, the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Avith.

PAITE: Huan, Saula, a si a, Akbor tapa Baal-hanana in a sikin vai a hawm ta hi.
ENGLISH: Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.

PAITE: Huan, Akbor tapa Baal-hanana a si a, Hada in a sikin vai a hawma: a khopi min Pau ahi; a ji min Hehetabel ahia, amah Mesahaba ta Matred tanu ahi.
ENGLISH: Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river, reigned in his place.

PAITE: Huan, hiaite a inkuan uh bang jel leh, a mun bang jel u leh a min bang jel Esau suan heutute min ahi; heutu Timna te, heutu Alva te, heutu Jetheth te;
ENGLISH: Shaul died, and Baal Hanan, the son of Achbor reigned in his place.

PAITE: Heutu Oholibamte, heutu Elate, heutu Pinonte;
ENGLISH: Baal Hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pau. His wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

PAITE: Heutu Kenazte, heutu Temante, heutu Mibzarte;
ENGLISH: These are the names of the chiefs who came from Esau, according to their families, after their places, and by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,

PAITE: Heutu Magdiel te, heutu Iram te; huaite a gam neih uah a omna uh bang jelin Edom suan heutute ahi uh: huai Edom Edomte suangpa Esau ahi.
ENGLISH: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

PAITE: Heutu Kenazte, heutu Temante, heutu Mibzarte;Heutu Magdiel te, heutu Iram te; huaite a gam neih uah a omna uh bang jelin Edom suan heutute ahi uh: huai Edom Edomte suangpa Esau ahi.
ENGLISH: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

PAITE: Heutu Magdiel te, heutu Iram te; huaite a gam neih uah a omna uh bang jelin Edom suan heutute ahi uh: huai Edom Edomte suangpa Esau ahi.
ENGLISH: chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their habitations in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.

PAITE: Huan, Jakob a pa mikhuala a omna gam, Kanan gamah, a om a.
ENGLISH: Jacob lived in the land of his father’s travels, in the land of Canaan.

PAITE: Hiaite Jakob suante ahi uh: Joseph, kum sawm leh kum sagih a upa ahihin, a ute toh ganhon a khak ua; amah naupang ahi laia, a pa jite Bilha leh Zilpa tapate kiangah a om a; huan, Joseph in a gitlouh thuthang uh a pa uh kiangah a tun a.
ENGLISH: This is the history of the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers. He was a boy with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives. Joseph brought an evil report of them to their father.

PAITE: Huan, Israel in Joseph, a teklam ta ahihjiakin a tate tengteng sangin a it jaw a: huchiin, puannak tual ze tuamtuam a gial abawl saka.
ENGLISH: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a coat of many colors.

PAITE: Huan, a pa un amah bel a ute tengteng sangin a it jaw chih a uten ana theita ua; huchiin, amah amudah mahmah uh, kam hoih himhim in a houpih thei takei uhi.
ENGLISH: His brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him, and couldn’t speak peaceably to him.

PAITE: Juan, Joseph in mang a neia, a ute a hilha: huchiin, amah a mudah semsem uh.
ENGLISH: Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated him all the more.

PAITE: Huan, aman, a kiang uah, hehpihtakin ka mang thu ngai dih uh:
ENGLISH: He said to them, “Please hear this dream which I have dreamed:

PAITE: Ngai un, lou ah buhphalte I na gak ua, huan, ngai un, kei buhphal a hong thou a, a ding nemnom a; huan, ngai un, nou buhphalten a hong um ua, kei buhphal chibai a buk chiat uh, achia.
ENGLISH: for behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves came around, and bowed down to my sheaf.”

PAITE: Huan, hichi ahia, Joseph puin, a jiin a kianga, na sikha in hichiin a honbawl, chia, a thugen a jakin, a heh guiha.
ENGLISH: It happened, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, “This is what your servant did to me,” that his wrath was kindled.

PAITE: Huchiin, Joseph puin amah a pia, suangkulh ah, lal suangkulh tang hena a omna uah a khumta a: huchiin huaiah suangkulh ah a omta hi.
ENGLISH: Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.

PAITE: Ahihhangin, Toupa bel Joseph kiangah a om jela, a tungah a chinga, suangkulh vengmi mah leng a hehpihsak a.
ENGLISH: But Yahweh was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

PAITE: Huchiin, suangkulh vengmiten suangkulha tang omte tengteng Joseph khut ah a kemsak tavek ua; huchiin, huailaia a hihpeuh uh Joseph bel a hihpa ahi jela.Toupa Joseph kiangah a oma, a thilhih peuhmah Toupan a lohchinsak nak jiakin suangkulh vengmi in a khut a thil om himhim a en nuam takei hi.
ENGLISH: The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever they did there, he was responsible for it.

PAITE: Toupa Joseph kiangah a oma, a thilhih peuhmah Toupan a lohchinsak nak jiakin suangkulh vengmi in a khut a thil om himhim a en nuam takei hi.
ENGLISH: The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that was under his hand, because Yahweh was with him; and that which he did, Yahweh made it prosper.

PAITE: Huan, Adamin a ji Evi a ompiha; huchiin a gaia, Kaina a nei hi, Toupa panpihin pasal kon nei ta, a chi a.
ENGLISH: The man knew Eve his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Cain, and said, “I have gotten a man with Yahweh’s help.”

PAITE: Huan, a nau Abel a honnei nawn hi. Huan, Abel belam chingmiin a oma. Kaina bel leilet miin a om
ENGLISH: Again she gave birth, to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

PAITE: Huan, a nungin hichi a hong hia, Kainain Toupa kianga a lat din loua piang a hontawi a.
ENGLISH: As time passed, it happened that Cain brought an offering to Yahweh from the fruit of the ground.

PAITE: Huan Abelin leng a belam hon laka piang masapente leh, a thau a hontawi sama, huan, Toupan Abel leh a thillat a kipahpiha:
ENGLISH: Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat. Yahweh respected Abel and his offering,

PAITE: A hihhangin Kaina leh a thillat bel akipahpih kei. Huchiin, Kaina a heh mahmaha, a mel a liapta hi.
ENGLISH: but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell.

PAITE: Huchiin, Toupa, Kaina kiangah, bangdia heh na hia? Bangdia na mel liap ahia?
ENGLISH: Yahweh said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen?

PAITE: Thil hihhoih lechin pahtak na loh kei dia hia? Na hih hoih keia a hihlebel khelhna kongkhak bulah a kual nilouh hi: a deihlam nangmah kiang lam ahi dinga, a tungah thu na nei ding hi a chi a.
ENGLISH: If you do well, will it not be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”

PAITE: Huan, Kainain a nau Abel a houpiha: huan, hichi ahia, loua a om lai un Kainain a nau Abel a suala, a thatta hi.
ENGLISH: Cain said to Abel, his brother, “Let’s go into the field.” It happened when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, and killed him.

PAITE: Huchiin, Toupan, Kaina kiangah, na nau Abel ko omta ahia? A chi a. Huan aman, ka theikei: ka nau donpa ka hi ahia? A chi hi.
ENGLISH: Yahweh said to Cain, “Where is Abel, your brother?” He said, “I don’t know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”

PAITE: Huan, aman, bang hih na tamaia? Na nau sisan awin leitung akipanin lah a hon sama.
ENGLISH: Yahweh said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.

PAITE: Huaijiakin, lei, na khuta kipana na nau sisan sang dinga a kam naka akipan hamsiat na hita hi;
ENGLISH: Now you are cursed because of the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

PAITE: Leitung na lehin leng ahoihna a honpe phal nawn kei ding; a chi a.
ENGLISH: From now on, when you till the ground, it won’t yield its strength to you. You shall be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth.”

PAITE: Huan, Kainain, Toupa kiangah, non gawtna a na mahmaha, ka thuak zou kei ding.
ENGLISH: Cain said to Yahweh, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.

PAITE: Ngaiin, tuniin leitunga kipan non delhkheta ngala; na mit muh phak louha sela om ding ka hita; lei ah tai mang leh vakvai hi ding lah ka hita ngala; huchiin hichi ahi dinga, kuapeuh honmuin a hon that mai ding uh, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Behold, you have driven me out this day from the surface of the ground. I will be hidden from your face, and I will be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth. It will happen that whoever finds me will kill me.”

PAITE: Huan, Toupan, a kiangah, huchi ahihleh, kuapeuh Kaina that amun sagihin a tungah phu a la ding uh, a chi a. Huchiin, min amah a muh ua a thah louhna ding un Toupan Kaina achiamtehta hi.
ENGLISH: Yahweh said to him, “Therefore whoever slays Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.” Yahweh appointed a sign for Cain, lest any finding him should strike him.

PAITE: Huchiin, Kaina Toupa kianga kipan a pawta, Eden suahlama Nod gamah a omta hi.
ENGLISH: Cain went out from Yahweh’s presence, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

PAITE: Huan, Kainain aji a ompiha; huchiin, a gaia, Enok a nei hi: huan, khua a sata, a kho min dingin a tapa tam sakin, Enok a chi hi.
ENGLISH: Cain knew his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.

PAITE: Huan, Enokin tapa Irad a neia: Iradin tapa Mahujael a neia: Mahujaelin tapa Methusael a neia; Methusaelin tapa Lamek a ni hi.
ENGLISH: To Enoch was born Irad. Irad became the father of Mehujael. Mehujael became the father of Methushael. Methushael became the father of Lamech.

PAITE: Huan Lamekin ji nih a neia: khat min Adia ahi, khat min Zillai ahi.
ENGLISH: Lamech took two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.

PAITE: Huan, Adaiin Jabal a neia; amah bel puanina om gan vulmite suangpa ahi.
ENGLISH: Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.

PAITE: A nau min Jubal ahi: amah bel kaihging leh tamngai tummite tengteng suangpa ahi.
ENGLISH: His brother’s name was Jubal, who was the father of all who handle the harp and pipe.

PAITE: Huan Zillain leng Tubal-Kaina, dal leh sik tuzatheizat chiteng sekmi, a neia: huan, Tubal- Kaina sanggamnu Naamai ahi.
ENGLISH: Zillah also gave birth to Tubal Cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron. Tubal Cain’s sister was Naamah.

PAITE: Huan, Lamekin, ajite kiangah: Adal leh Zillai te aw ka aw ja unla; Lamek jite aw, ka thugen ngai un: honliamsak jiakin mi ka thata, honsidupsak jiakin mi ka that hi:
ENGLISH: Lamech said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice. You wives of Lamech, listen to my speech, for I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for bruising me.

PAITE: Kaina phu bawn amun sagiha la ding ahih uleh Lamek phu amun sawm sagih leh sagihin a la ngei ngei ding uh, a chi hi.
ENGLISH: If Cain will be avenged seven times, truly Lamech seventy-seven times.”

PAITE: Huan, Adamin a ji a ompih nawna; huchiin aman tapa anei nawna, a min din Seth a saa: Pathianin Abel sikin chi suah ding honseh sakta; Kaina in lah amah a that ngala, achia.Huan, Sethin, amah mahin tapa a neitaa; a min din Enosa a sa hi; hualaiin miten Toupa min a na lou pan uh.
ENGLISH: Adam knew his wife again. She gave birth to a son, and named him Seth, “for God has appointed me another child instead of Abel, for Cain killed him.”

PAITE: Huan, Sethin, amah mahin tapa a neitaa; a min din Enosa a sa hi; hualaiin miten Toupa min a na lou pan uh.
ENGLISH: There was also born a son to Seth, and he named him Enosh. Then men began to call on Yahweh’s name.

PAITE: Huan, huai thil khitin hichi ahia, Aigupta kumpipa uain pepa leh a tanghou bawlpan a pu uh Aigupta kumpipa a lungkimlousak ua.
ENGLISH: It happened after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.

PAITE: Huchiin, Pharo bel a sikha heutu nih tungah, a uain pia heutupen tungah leh a tanghou bawl heutupen tungah a hehta a.
ENGLISH: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

PAITE: Huchiin vengmi pawl heutu in ah, suangkulh, Joseph hena a omna ah, a tangsakta hi.
ENGLISH: He put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.

PAITE: Huan, vengmi pawl heutu in Joseph bel amau a kemsaka, huchiin amau a na a sepsak ua, huan, ni bangzah hiam tak a tang uhi.
ENGLISH: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many days.

PAITE: Huan, suangkulh a hena om, Aigupta kumpipa uain pepa leh tanghou bawlpa in, jan khat mang khiakna tuamtuam tuak a nei ua.
ENGLISH: They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.

PAITE: Huan, a jingin Joseph a kiang uah a valut a, amau a hong mu a, huan, ngaiin, a na lungkham mahmah uhi.
ENGLISH: Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and saw that they were sad.

PAITE: Huchiin, aman, bang achia ahia tuniin lungkham mel po natel uchia? Chiin, Pharo sikha heutu, a pu inn a tang teita, a donga.
ENGLISH: He asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”

PAITE: Huan, amau, a kiangah, mang ka nei ua, hon hilh chiansak thei kuamah lah a om ngal keia ahi, a chi ua. Huan, Joseph in, a kianguah, mang hilhchetna te Pathian a ahi ka hia? Hehpihtakin honhilh dih ua, achia.
ENGLISH: They said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it.” Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.”

PAITE: Huchiin, uain pia heutu penin a mang Joseph a hilha, a kiangah, ngai dih, ka mangin, ka maah grepgui a hong om a;
ENGLISH: The chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,

PAITE: Grepgui ah ka thum a oma: huan, selnou bangin a hong om a, a pakte a hong om khia a; a pak bomten grep minte a hon omsak ua:
ENGLISH: and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.

PAITE: Huan, Pharo nou ka khut ah a hong om a; huchiin, grep, gahte ka loua, Pharo nou ah ka suak a, huai nou Pharo khut ah ka na pia a, achia.
ENGLISH: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”

PAITE: Huan, Joseph in, a kiangah, a hilhchetna hiai ahi: ka thumte ni thum ahia:
ENGLISH: Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.

PAITE: Tua kipan ni thumin Pharo in na lutang a domkang dinga, na nasep mah a honsemsak nawn ding: huchiin a uain pepa na nahin laia na piak ngeina bangin, Pharo nou a khut ah na pe nawn ding hi.
ENGLISH: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You will give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cupbearer.

PAITE: Ahihhangin na hong hamphat nawn chiangin hon theigige inla, hehpihtakin hehpihna ka tungah hon kilangsak inla, Pharo kiangah ka tungtang hon gen inla, hiai in a kipan honpi khia in:
ENGLISH: But remember me when it will be well with you, and please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.

PAITE: Hebru te gam a kipan min a guka a honguk mang uh ka hia: hiai gamah leng khuk sunga a honkhum na ding in bangmah ka hihkhial kei hi, achia.
ENGLISH: For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”

PAITE: Tanghou bawlpain hilhchetna a hoih chih a theih in, Joseph kiangah, ken leng mang ka neia, ngaiin, tanghou ngou lohbeu thum ka luin kana pua a:
ENGLISH: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.

PAITE: Huan, lohbeu tungnung penah Pharo an, tanghou bawlpa bawl, chi chih ana om a; huan, huaite vasaten lohbeu ka lu a ka puaka kipan a nane souhsouh ua, achia.
ENGLISH: In the uppermost basket there was all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”

PAITE: Huan, Joseph in a dawnga, hiai a hilhchetna ahi: Lohbeu thum ni thum ahi;
ENGLISH: Joseph answered, “This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.

PAITE: Tua kipan ni thum in Pharo in na pumpi akipanin na lutang a domkang dinga, sing dawn ah a hon khai ding; huchiin, vasaten na sa a ne souhsouh ding uh, achia.
ENGLISH: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from off you.”

PAITE: Huan, hichi ahia, a ni thum ni, Pharo pian tanphak niin, aman a sikha tengteng a dingin ankuang a luia: huan, a sikhate laka uain pia heutupen lutang a domkang ta a.
ENGLISH: It happened the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

PAITE: Huan, uain pia heutu pen uain pemi mah in apangsak nawna; huchiin, nou Pharo khut ah a peta a:
ENGLISH: He restored the chief cupbearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;

PAITE: Ahihhangin, Joseph in amau a hilhchet bangtakin, tanghou bawl heutupen bel a khaita hi.Himahleh, uain pia heutu penin Joseph a theigige zenzen kei a, a mangnghilh maimah.
ENGLISH: but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.

PAITE: Himahleh, uain pia heutu penin Joseph a theigige zenzen kei a, a mangnghilh maimah.
ENGLISH: Yet the chief cupbearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.

PAITE: Huan, kum nih vengveng nungin hichi ahia, Pharo in mang a neia; huan, ngaiin, lui gei ah ana dinga.
ENGLISH: It happened at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and behold, he stood by the river.

PAITE: Huan, ngaiin, bawngpi sagih hoih taktak thau taktak tui akipan in a hongpawt khe tou ua, loupa nou lakah a hongta uh.
ENGLISH: Behold, there came up out of the river seven cattle, sleek and fat, and they fed in the marsh grass.

PAITE: Huan, ngaiin, bawngpi dang sagih kil theuthou gawng gemgom a hongpawt khe tou nawn ua, bawngpi dangte kiangah lui gei ah a hong ding uhi.
ENGLISH: Behold, seven other cattle came up after them out of the river, ugly and thin, and stood by the other cattle on the brink of the river.

PAITE: Huan, bawngpi kil theuthou ten bawngpi hoih taktak thau taktak te a gai maimah uhi.
ENGLISH: The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh awoke.

PAITE: Huchiin, Pharo a khangloua a. Huan, a ihmu nawna, mang a nei nawn a: huan, ngaiin, buh a kung khat a h vui sagih lian pipi hoih liahliah a hong om khia a.
ENGLISH: He slept and dreamed a second time: and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, healthy and good.

PAITE: Huan, ngaiin, huai nungin vui sagih ngat gigeuh suahlam huih nuai ek a hing om khe nawna,
ENGLISH: Behold, seven heads of grain, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

PAITE: Huan, vui ngat gigeuh ten vui sagih lian pipi hoih liahliah te a valh khin maimah ua. Huan, Pharo a khangloua a; huan, ngaiin, mang ana hi hi.
ENGLISH: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

PAITE: Huan, a jingin hichi ahia, a lungsim a buai mahmah a; hichiin, mi a sawl a, Aigupta gama mitkhialdawi siam tengteng leh mipil tengteng a sam khawm a: huan, Pharo in a mang amau a na hilh a; himahleh Pharo hilhchian thei kuamah lah a om ngal kei ua.
ENGLISH: It happened in the morning that his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all of Egypt’s magicians and wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.

PAITE: Huchih laiin uain pia heutupen in Pharo kiangah, tuni in ka mohdan te ka honthei kheta:
ENGLISH: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my faults today.

PAITE: Pharo a sikhate tungah a heh a, huchiin vengmi pawl heutu in ah kei leh tanghou bawl heutupen a hon tangsak a:
ENGLISH: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, me and the chief baker.

PAITE: Huan, kei leh aman jan khat mang ke nei ua, mang khiakna tuam tuak ahi ka mat uh.
ENGLISH: We dreamed a dream in one night, I and he. We dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.

PAITE: Huan, huailai ah ka kiangah vengmi pawl heutu sikha, Hebru mi, tangval khat a om a; huan, amah ka hilh ua, aman ka mangte uh a hilhchian ta hi; ka mang bang tuaktuak un ahi a hon hilhchet.
ENGLISH: There was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. To each man according to his dream he interpreted.

PAITE: Huan, hichi ahia; kei bel ka nasep mah a hon semsak nawn a, amah bel a khaita a, achia.
ENGLISH: It happened, as he interpreted to us, so it was: he restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”

PAITE: Huchiin, Pharoin Joseph a samsak pah ngala, huchiin kintakin kokhuk akipan a pikheta ua: huan, a kimet ngila, a puansilh a kheka, Pharo kiangah a valutta hi.
ENGLISH: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Pharaoh.

PAITE: Huan, Pharo in Joseph kiangah, mang ka neia, a hilhchian thei kuamah a om kei ua, nang bel mang a thu na theih leh na hilhchian thei chih na tungtang mi gen ka naja a, achia.
ENGLISH: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”

PAITE: Huan, Joseph in Pharo a dawnga, huai ahihleh keia om ahikei hi, Pathianin Pharo lungmuanhuai takin a dawng zaw ding, achia.
ENGLISH: Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “It isn’t in me. God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”

PAITE: Huan, Pharo in Joseph kiangah, ka mangin, ngaiin, lui gei ah ka na dinga:
ENGLISH: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I stood on the brink of the river:

PAITE: Hua, ngaiin, bawngpi sagih thau taktak hoih pipi tuia kipan in a hongpawt khetou ua, loupanou lakah ana ta ua:
ENGLISH: and behold, there came up out of the river seven cattle, fat and sleek. They fed in the marsh grass,

PAITE: Huan, bawngpi dang sagih ginalou leh deih huailou leh gawng siatsuat, huchibang tela hoihlou Aigupta gam tengteng a leng ka muh ngeilouh, nung uah a hong pawt khetou nawn ua:
ENGLISH: and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.

PAITE: Huan, bawngpi gawng siatsuat deih huailou pipiten bawngpi sagih thau taktak hongpawt masa te a hon gai maimah ua:
ENGLISH: The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle,

PAITE: Huan, a gaih khit nung un leng a ne uh chih a kithei tuan keia: a tunglai mah bangin deih huailou takin a om lailai uhi. Huchiin ka khangloua ta hi.
ENGLISH: and when they had eaten them up, it couldn’t be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.

PAITE: Huan, ka mangin, ngaiin, buh kung khat ah vui sagih lian pipi, hoih pipi a hong om khia a:
ENGLISH: I saw in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, full and good:

PAITE: Huan, ngaiin, huai nungin vui sagih vuai niangnuang, neu chikchik, suahlam huih in a nuai a hong om khe nawn ua:
ENGLISH: and behold, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

PAITE: Huan, vui ngat ngingeuh ten vui sagih hoih taktak te a valh khit maimah uh ka mu a: huan, mitkhialdawi siamte ka hilh a, himahleh hon hilhchian thei lah kuamah a om tuan ngal kei ua, chiin, a gen hi.
ENGLISH: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”

PAITE: Huan, Joseph in, Pharo kiangah, Pharo mang jaw khat ahi: Pathian in hih dia a kisak Pharo theisak eive.
ENGLISH: Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.

PAITE: Bawng sagih hoih taktak te kum sagih ahi ua; vui sagih hoih taktak te leng kum sagih ahi uh: mang bel khat ahi hi.
ENGLISH: The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.

PAITE: Huan, a nung ua bawng sagih tek taktak deih huailou taktak hongpawt khetou te kum sagih hi ua, vui sagih a hawm ngen suahlam huih nuaite toh; huaite kial kum kum sagih ding ahi.
ENGLISH: The seven thin and ugly cattle that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted with the east wind; they will be seven years of famine.

PAITE: Huai ahi Pharo kianga ka gen: Pathian in hih dia a kisak Pharo kianga a theihsak ahi.
ENGLISH: That is the thing which I spoke to Pharaoh. What God is about to do he has shown to Pharaoh.

PAITE: Ngaiin, Aigupta gamsung tengteng ah niang leh tai a om kum kum sagih a hongtung ding;
ENGLISH: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt.

PAITE: Huai nungin kial kum kum sagih a hong om nawn ding; huchiin niang leh tai a omna Aigupta gamah mangngilh vek ahita ding; kial in gam a ne gawp vek ding hi;
ENGLISH: There will arise after them seven years of famine, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,

PAITE: Niang leh tai, a honjui kial jiakin, hiai gamah a thei nawnta kei ding uh; a thupi sin mahmah ngala
ENGLISH: and the plenty will not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it will be very grievous.

PAITE: Huan, mang Pharo nihvei a neih tuansakna ahihleh hiai jiak ahi, thil hih ding Pathianin a hihkipa, Pathian mahin a tunsak pah ding jiakin.
ENGLISH: The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.

PAITE: Huchiin tuin Pharo in mi khat tei tak pilsak mai zong khia henla, Aigupta gam tungah heutuin omsak hen,

PAITE: Huan, Joseph in a pi luta a om jiak in a lau ua, hoh masak laia I ip ua dangka hon kiknawnte jiakin eive a honpi lut uh; I tung ua siatna zonga, hon sualin, ei leh I sabengtungte toh sikha dinga hon mat tum eive, a chi ua.
ENGLISH: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time, we’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”

PAITE: Huan, Joseph in kemmi kiangah a vahoh ua, kong bul ah a houpih ua,
ENGLISH: They came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,

PAITE: Pu aw, ka hong masak lai ua buh lei ding lela hongsuak ka hi ua:
ENGLISH: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.

PAITE: Huan, hichi ahia, giah buk ka tun un ka ipte uh ka hong ua, huan, ngaiin, ka dangka chiat uh ka ip gong bul uah a na om chiata, ka dangka uh a buk ngeingeiin a na om a: huchiin ka hontawi uhi.
ENGLISH: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.

PAITE: Huan, aman, lungmuangtakin om unla, lau keiun: na Pathian, na pa uh Pathianin na ipte uah gou a honpia ahi mai ve: na dangka ulah ka mu ngala, achia. Huan, Simeon a kiang uah a honpi khia ua.
ENGLISH: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.

PAITE: Huan, amah a daka, a nau Benjamin, a nu tapa a mua, hiai na nautumpen uh, a tanchin na honhilh uh hia? a chi a. Huan, amah mahin, Ka tapa, Pathian honhehpih hen, a chi a.

Huan, uainte a dawn ua, nuam asa chiat mahmah uh.

ENGLISH: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.
