PAITE: Ka khain ka hinna a chimtaka; ka utdandanin ka phun ding hi: ka kha thangpaihnain ka gen ding.
ENGLISH: “My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

PAITE: Pathian kiangah, Honmohpaih ken; bangdia honkinakpih na hia hontheisak in, ka chi ding hi.
ENGLISH: I will tell God, ‘Do not condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.

PAITE: Na nuaisiah nang adia hoih ahi maw, na khutte thilhih na muhsita, giloute thugen tunga na maitai?
ENGLISH: Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of your hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?

PAITE: Sa mitte nei na hi hia, ahihkeileh mihing muh banga mu na hi hia?
ENGLISH: Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?

PAITE: Na nite mihing nite bang hia, ahihkeileh na kumte mihing kumte bang,
ENGLISH: Are your days as the days of mortals, or your years as man’s years,

PAITE: Ka thulimlouhna na kana, ka khelhna na nungdelha,
ENGLISH: that you inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?

PAITE: Ka gilou kei chih na theih nakpia, na khuta kipan hon suaktasak ding a omlouh?
ENGLISH: Although you know that I am not wicked, there is no one who can deliver out of your hand.

PAITE: Na khutten a honsek un a honbawl kimvel sipsipa; tun kiheiin non hihse dia hia?
ENGLISH: “‘Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.

PAITE: Theigige in, ka honngen ahi, tungman banga na honmek dan; leivui hontun nawn ding na hi hia?
ENGLISH: Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?

PAITE: Nawitui bangin na honsung khiain, nawituidat bangin na hontok kei maw?
ENGLISH: Haven’t you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?

PAITE: Vun leh sain na hontuama, guhte leh thagui-tein na honphan khawm hi.
ENGLISH: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.

PAITE: Hinna leh deihsakna na honphala, huan na kepnain ka lungsim a hawi hi.
ENGLISH: You have granted me life and loving kindness. Your visitation has preserved my spirit.

PAITE: Himahleh hiai thilte na lungtang sungah na sela; hiai bel na tup ahi chih ka thei hi:
ENGLISH: Yet you hid these things in your heart. I know that this is with you:

PAITE: Thil ka hihkhelh leh, huchiin non chiamteha, huan ka thulimlouhna akipan na honkhah kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: if I sin, then you mark me. You will not acquit me from my iniquity.

PAITE: Ka gitlouh leh, ka tung a gik hi; ka diktat leh, huchiin leng ka lutang ka sangsak kei ding, zahlaknaa dim ngalin leh ka gimthuakna enin.
ENGLISH: If I am wicked, woe to me. If I am righteous, I still shall not lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.

PAITE: Huan ka lutang a kiletsak leh, humpinelkai bangin nang non benga: huan ka tunga na lamdandan na hon ensak nawn hi.
ENGLISH: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.

PAITE: Kei kalh na palaite na thaksaka, ka tunga na hehna na khangsaka; hondou ding sepaih hon thak non sawl hi.
ENGLISH: You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.

PAITE: Bangdia sul akipan kei honlakhia na hia oi leh? na si taleng, kuamah muh main.
ENGLISH: “‘Why, then, have you brought me forth out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.

PAITE: Omlou mahbang bangta ding hiinga; sul akipana hana puaka omta ding hi inga.
ENGLISH: I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

PAITE: Ka nite a tom kei maw? huchi ahihleh, tawpin, honom sak maimaiin, huchia neukhaa ka lungmuan theihna dingin.
ENGLISH: Aren’t my days few? Cease then. Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,

PAITE: Ka kik nawn louhna akipana ka pai main, khomialna gam leh sihna limliap gam mahmah ah:Mialna mahbanga, mialna sahna gama: sihna limliap gam, dan himhim omlouhna, khovak khomial banga a omna mun ah.
ENGLISH: before I go where I shall not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;

PAITE: Mialna mahbanga, mialna sahna gama: sihna limliap gam, dan himhim omlouhna, khovak khomial banga a omna mun ah.
ENGLISH: the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.’”

PAITE: Huan zophar Naamanmi in a dawnga, huchiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answered,

PAITE: Thu tampite dawn louh ding ahia hia? huan mi houlimnaa dim siamtansak ding hia?
ENGLISH: “Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?

PAITE: Na kisaktheihnaten mite daisak ding hia? huan na simmoh chiangin, kuamahin nang honzahlaksak lou ding uhia?
ENGLISH: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, shall no man make you ashamed?

PAITE: Ka thuhilh a siangthoua, huan na mit uah ka siang hi, na chi ngala.
ENGLISH: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.’

PAITE: Himahleh Pathianin thugen maijen le jaw, nang demin a mukte hongleh;
ENGLISH: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,

PAITE: Huchin pilna thugukte nang a honensak dinga, a theihna ah thuah tampi ahi chih: huaijiakin na thulimlouhna gun sanga tawmjaw na lakah Pathianin nang a honphut chih theiin.
ENGLISH: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.

PAITE: Zonin Pathian na mu thei diam; hoihkimna ah Thilbangkimhihthei na mu thei diam?
ENGLISH: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

PAITE: Van bangin a sanga; bang na hih thei dia? Seol sangin a thuka; bang na thei thei dia?
ENGLISH: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. . What can you know?

PAITE: Huaia tehna lei sangin a saujawa, tuipi sangin a zajaw hi.
ENGLISH: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

PAITE: Paisuak henla, man henla, huan vaihawmna ah sam leh, huchiin kuan amah a dal thei dia?
ENGLISH: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?

PAITE: Aman lah mi bangmahloute a thei ngala: ngaihtuah kei mahleh, thu limlouhna leng a mu hi.
ENGLISH: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.

PAITE: Mihing theihsiamna beiin theihsiamna a nei ding, sabengtung nou mihinga a pian chiangin.
ENGLISH: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.

PAITE: Na lungtang na koih dika, amah lama na khutte na jak leh;
ENGLISH: “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.

PAITE: Na khuta thulimlouhna a oma, gamlapia na koihkhiaka, gitlouhna na puanina na tensak kei leh;
ENGLISH: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.

PAITE: Huchiin gensiatna ding omlouin na mai na daksak taktak dinga; ahi, na kip dinga, na lau kei ding:
ENGLISH: Surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear:

PAITE: Na haksatna na mangngilh ding jiakin; tui luang mangsa bangin na theigige ding hi:
ENGLISH: for you shall forget your misery. You shall remember it as waters that are passed away.

PAITE: Huan sunlai sangin na hinna a telzo dinga; khomial om mahleh, jingsang bang ahi ding hi.
ENGLISH: Life shall be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it shall be as the morning.

PAITE: Huan lametna a om jiakin, na kipta ding hi; ahi, amah tanchin na zong dinga, muangin na khawlta ding hi.
ENGLISH: You shall be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take your rest in safety.

PAITE: Lup leng na lum lai dinga, huan kuamahin nang honlausak kei ding uhi; ahi, mi tampiin nang a honzong ding uhi.Himahleh gilou mitte a juausuak dinga, taina ding lampi a neikei ding ua, huan a lametna uh kha khah ahi ding hi.
ENGLISH: Also you shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid. Yes, many shall court your favor.

PAITE: Himahleh gilou mitte a juausuak dinga, taina ding lampi a neikei ding ua, huan a lametna uh kha khah ahi ding hi.
ENGLISH: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail. They shall have no way to flee. Their hope shall be the giving up of the spirit.”

PAITE: Huchiin Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered,

PAITE: Ginlelh vuallouhin mite jaw na hi hi peuhmah ua, huan nou toh pilnaa si ding hi.
ENGLISH: “No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.

PAITE: Himahleh noute bangmahin theihsiamna ka nei hi; nou sangin ka niamzo kei hi: ahi, hiaite bang thilte kuan a theikei a?
ENGLISH: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn’t know such things as these?

PAITE: Kei jaw mi a inveng adia nuihzabuk ka hi a, kei, huai Pathian sama, hua aman amah dawnpa, mi dik, mi hoihkim, nuihzabuk kana hi.
ENGLISH: I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.

PAITE: Omnuama om ngaihtuahnaah vangsiatna muhsitna a oma; ahihhangin, a khe uh teute adingin mansain a om hi.
ENGLISH: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.

PAITE: Suamhatmite puaninte a lohchinga, Pathian hehsakte akip ua; a khut uh pathiana neite Pathian in tampi a pia.
ENGLISH: The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their God in their hands.

PAITE: Himahleh gamsate dongin, huan amau nang a honsinsak ding uh; huan huihkhuaa vasate, huchiin nang a honhilh ding uh:
ENGLISH: “But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you.

PAITE: Ahihkeileh lei kiangah thu genin, nang a honsinsak dinga; huan tuipia ngasaten na kiangah a phuang ding uhi.
ENGLISH: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you.

PAITE: Hiaite tengteng ah, TOUPA khutin a hihkhin chih kua ahia theilou?
ENGLISH: Who doesn’t know that in all these, the hand of Yahweh has done this,

PAITE: Amah khut ah thil hing chiteng kha leh, mihing tengteng hatna a om hi.
ENGLISH: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?

PAITE: Bilin thute a enchian kei maw, dangtungin a an achiam bangin?
ENGLISH: Doesn’t the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?

PAITE: Mi upate kiangah pilna a om, huan nite sauna ah theihsiamna a om hi.
ENGLISH: With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.

PAITE: Amah kiangah pilna leh hatna a om; aman thupha leh theihsiamna a nei.
ENGLISH: “With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.

PAITE: Ngaiin, a kai puka, a kilam nawn theikei ding; mihing a khak binga, kuaman a hong theikei ding.
ENGLISH: Behold, he breaks down, and it can’t be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.

PAITE: Ngaiin, tui a chinga a kang; a khahkhiaa lei a tum vek.
ENGLISH: Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.

PAITE: A kiangah hatna leh pilna a oma; khema omte leh khempa amaha ahi.
ENGLISH: With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.

PAITE: Thuhilhmite lohsamin a pi manga, huan vaihawmmite mihaiin a bawl hi.
ENGLISH: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.

PAITE: Kumpipate kolte a suta, huan kawnggakin a kawng uh a gak hi.
ENGLISH: He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.

PAITE: Siampute lohsamin a pimanga, huan mi hatte a zou hi.
ENGLISH: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.

PAITE: Muante thugen a suana, upate theihsiamna a la mang hi.
ENGLISH: He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.

PAITE: Lalte tungah muhsitna a buaka, mihatte kawnggak a phel hi.
ENGLISH: He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.

PAITE: Mial akipanin thil thukte a mukhiaa, huan sihna limliap khovakah a honla khia hi.
ENGLISH: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.

PAITE: Namte a pungsaka, huan amau a hihsia: namte a theh-jaka, huan a lakhawm nawn hi.
ENGLISH: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.

PAITE: Leia mite hausate lungtang a la manga, huan gamdaia lampi omlouhna ah amau a vakvai sak hi.Vakna beiin khomial ah a mai ua, huan zukhammi bangin amau a hoisak hi.
ENGLISH: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.

PAITE: Vakna beiin khomial ah a mai ua, huan zukhammi bangin amau a hoisak hi.
ENGLISH: They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.

PAITE: Ngaiin, ka mitin hiai tengteng a muta hi, ka bilin huai a jaa a theisiam ta hi.
ENGLISH: “Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.

PAITE: Na thei uh, huaimah ken leng ka thei hi: nou sangin ka niamzo kei hi.
ENGLISH: What you know, I know also. I am not inferior to you.

PAITE: Thilbangkimhihthei kiangah thu ka gen mahmah ding, huan Pathian toh houlim ka ut hi.
ENGLISH: “Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.

PAITE: Himahleh nou jaw juau phuakte na hi ua, a phattuamlou daktolte na hi vek uhi.
ENGLISH: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.

PAITE: Aw na vek un dai sipsip le uchin maw; na pilna uh hi ding hiven.
ENGLISH: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.

PAITE: Tuin ka thusut ja un, ka mukte ngetna ngaikhia un.
ENGLISH: Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.

PAITE: Pathian adingin diktatloutakin thu na gen ding uam, amah adingin khemhat takin na houlim ding uam?
ENGLISH: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?

PAITE: Ami na zahtak ding uam? Pathian adin na sual ding uam?
ENGLISH: Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?

PAITE: Nou a honzonkhiak a hoih hia? ahihkeileh min mi a khem bangin, amah na khem ding uam?
ENGLISH: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?

PAITE: Nou a honsal mahmah ding, a guka mite na zahtak uleh.
ENGLISH: He will surely reprove you if you secretly show partiality.

PAITE: A hoih tungtuannain nou a honlausak kei dia hia, nou tungah a kihtakhuaina a ke kei diam?
ENGLISH: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall on you?

PAITE: Na thugen minthangte uh vut paunakte ahi, na kidalnate uh tungman kidalnate ahi.
ENGLISH: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of clay.

PAITE: Dai unla, thu ka gen theihna dingin, honomsak maimai un, ka tungah a hongtung ding hongtung heh.
ENGLISH: “Be silent, leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.

PAITE: Bangdingin ka hain ka sa ka lain, ka khut ah ka koih dia?
ENGLISH: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?

PAITE: Aman honhihlum mahleh, amah ka ngak lai ding: ama ah ka lampite ka kemhoih lailai ding hi.
ENGLISH: Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will maintain my ways before him.

PAITE: Hiai leng ka hotdamna ahi ding; pathianlimsaklou mi a maa hongpai lou ding a hih jiakin.
ENGLISH: This also shall be my salvation, that a godless man shall not come before him.

PAITE: Ka thugen thanuam takin ja un, ka thuphuan na bil sung uah om hen.
ENGLISH: Hear diligently my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.

PAITE: Ngai un, tuin ka thu ka bawlhoihtaa; ka diktat ahi chih ka thei hi.
ENGLISH: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.

PAITE: Kei hon kiselpih ding amah kua ahia? kei lah tuin ka dai dia kha ka khah ding hi.
ENGLISH: Who is he who will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the spirit.

PAITE: Ka tungah thil nih hih kei phot le uchin, huan na mai akipan ka bu kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: “Only don’t do two things to me; then I will not hide myself from your face:

PAITE: Kei akipanin gamla ah na khut kai kikin; huan na lauhuainain honlausak ken.
ENGLISH: withdraw your hand far from me; and don’t let your terror make me afraid.

PAITE: Huaichiangin honsam lechin, ka hondawng ding; ahihkeileh honpausak inla, hondawng in.
ENGLISH: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.

PAITE: Ka thulimlouhnate leh khelhnate bang ahia? Ka tatlekna leh ka khelhna hontheisakin.
ENGLISH: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.

PAITE: Bangdia na mai sela na melma dia honbawl na hia?
ENGLISH: Why hide you your face, and hold me for your enemy?

PAITE: Singnah mutleng na hihbuai dia hia? buhpawl keu na delh dia hia?
ENGLISH: Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?

PAITE: Nang lahkei demin thil kha taktak na gelh ngala, ka tuailai thulimlouhnate na honluahsak hi:
ENGLISH: For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth:

PAITE: Ka khete leng kol na bunsaka, ka lampite tengteng na chiamteh hi; ka khenuai kimah gi na khunga.Mihing jaw thil muat bangin a mangthanga, nget nekgawp puansilh bangin.
ENGLISH: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,

PAITE: Mihing jaw thil muat bangin a mangthanga, nget nekgawp puansilh bangin.
ENGLISH: though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.

PAITE: Mihing numei apan piang nite tawmchik ahia,
ENGLISH: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.

PAITE: Pak bangin hong dawn khiaa, a vuai nawn pah, limliap bangin a taia, a om gige kei.
ENGLISH: He comes forth like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn’t continue.

PAITE: Huan mi huchibang tungah ma mit na hakin, nang toh vaihawmna ah kei non pi hia?
ENGLISH: Do you open your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?

PAITE: Thil nin akipanin kuan ahia thil siang la khe thei? Kuamahin.
ENGLISH: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one.

PAITE: A nite sehsa ahi chih theiin, na kiangah a khate simna a oma, a kan theilouh dingin a gamgite na septa hi;
ENGLISH: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he can’t pass;

PAITE: Amah en ken, a khawl theihna dingin, kiloh banga, a ni a hihkim matan.
ENGLISH: Look away from him, that he may rest, until he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.

PAITE: Phuk paihin om mahleh, a hongsel nawn dinga, huaia ahiang nou a tawp kei ding, chih sing adin lametna lah a om ngala.
ENGLISH: “For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease.

PAITE: Huaia a zung lei ah upa mahleh, huaia a kungpi lei ah sita mahleh;
ENGLISH: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground,

PAITE: Himahleh tui gim jiakin a hongnou thak dia, singsuan bangin bawkte a honnei khe nawn ding hi.
ENGLISH: yet through the scent of water it will bud, and put forth boughs like a plant.

PAITE: Himahleh mihing a sia, a mang jel hi: ahi, mihingin kha a khaha, huan koiah a om a?
ENGLISH: But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?

PAITE: Tuipi akipan tuite a pai bangin, luipi bel a tula, a kang hi;
ENGLISH: As the waters fail from the sea, and the river wastes and dries up,

PAITE: Huaimahbangin mihing a luma a thou kei hi: vante a om nawn louh matan, akhanglou kei ding uh, a ihmu uh leng a halhkhe sam kei ding uhi.
ENGLISH: so man lies down and doesn’t rise. Until the heavens are no more, they shall not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.

PAITE: Aw Seol ah honna sel lechin aw, na thangpaihna aman masiah honna guk kep lechin, hun sehsa honna piain, kei hontheigige lechin aw;
ENGLISH: “Oh that you would hide me in Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. , that you would keep me secret, until your wrath is past, that you would appoint me a set time, and remember me!

PAITE: Mi si leh, a hing nawn diam? ka galdouna leh nasepna ni tengteng ka ngak dinga, ka suahtakna a hongtun ma tanin.
ENGLISH: If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my warfare would I wait, until my release should come.

PAITE: Non na sam dia, huan ka hondawng ding hi: na khut nasep non lunggulh ding hi.
ENGLISH: You would call, and I would answer you. You would have a desire to the work of your hands.

PAITE: Himahleh tuin ka kalsuante na sima: ka khelhna peuhmah na chiamteh hi.
ENGLISH: But now you number my steps. Don’t you watch over my sin?

PAITE: Ip sungah ka tatlekna bilhin a oma, huan ka thulimlouhna na gonggak hi.
ENGLISH: My disobedience is sealed up in a bag. You fasten up my iniquity.

PAITE: Huan mual puk bangmahlou a honghi taktaka, a mun akipanin suangpi suanin a om hi;
ENGLISH: “But the mountain falling comes to nothing. The rock is removed out of its place;

PAITE: Tuiten suang a kiamsak ua; huaia dimletten leia leivui a tai mang uh; huan mihing lametna na hihsia hi.
ENGLISH: The waters wear the stones. The torrents of it wash away the dust of the earth. So you destroy the hope of man.

PAITE: Khantawnin amah na zou a, a paia; a mel na lamdang saka, amah na sawl mang hi.
ENGLISH: You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You change his face, and send him away.

PAITE: A tapate zahin a om ua, aman a theikei; hihniamin a om ua, himahleh aman amau ahi chih a theikei.Himahleh a tunga a sain natna a neia, huan a sunga a khain a sun hi.
ENGLISH: His sons come to honor, and he doesn’t know it. They are brought low, but he doesn’t perceive it of them.

PAITE: Himahleh a tunga a sain natna a neia, huan a sunga a khain a sun hi.
ENGLISH: But his flesh on him has pain, and his soul within him mourns.”

PAITE: Huchiin Elipha Teman miin a dawng a, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

PAITE: Mi pilin theihna bangmahlou toh dawnna a bawlin, suahlam huihin a gilpi a dimsak sak diam?
ENGLISH: “Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill himself with the east wind?

PAITE: Houlimna phatuamlou toh thu a ngaihtuahin, ahihkeileh hoih a hih theihna louh dinga thugente a ngaihtuah diam?
ENGLISH: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, or with speeches with which he can do no good?

PAITE: A hi, launa na hihmanga, huan Pathian maa kipiakzohna na dal lai hi.
ENGLISH: Yes, you do away with fear, and hinder devotion before God.

PAITE: Na thulimlouhnain lah na kam a sinsaka, zekhemhat mi lei na tel ngal a.
ENGLISH: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.

PAITE: Nang mahmah kamin nang siamlouh ahontang saka, kei hilouin; ahi, nang demin nangmah mukte mahmahin a hontheihpih hi.
ENGLISH: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I. Yes, your own lips testify against you.

PAITE: A piang mihing masapen na hi ahia? ahihkeileh tangte maa lakkhiaka om na hi maw?
ENGLISH: “Are you the first man who was born? Or were you brought forth before the hills?

PAITE: Pathian thuhilh guk na za ta hia? huan pilna na kikoih hoih hia?
ENGLISH: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?

PAITE: Ka theih louh uh bang na theia? koua omlou bang na theisiama?
ENGLISH: What do you know, that we don’t know? What do you understand, which is not in us?

PAITE: Ka lak uah samkang leh mi upa mahmah a om tuaktuak, na pa sanga nakpia upajawte.
ENGLISH: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, much elder than your father.

PAITE: Pathian nepnate leh siamtaka honhilh thute nang adia neu lua uhia?
ENGLISH: Are the consolations of God too small for you, even the word that is gentle toward you?

PAITE: Bangdia na lungtangin nang honpi mang ahia? Bang dia na mitte phia ahia?
ENGLISH: Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,

PAITE: Huchia Pathian dema na lungsim na heia, na kam akipana huchibang thute na pawtkhiak sak.
ENGLISH: That you turn your spirit against God, and let such words go out of your mouth?

PAITE: Mihing bang ahia, a sian ding? numei apan piang amah kua ahia a diktat ding?
ENGLISH: What is man, that he should be clean? What is he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

PAITE: Ngaiin, a mi siangthoute ah muanna a koih keia: ahi, a mitmuhin vante a siang kei uhi.
ENGLISH: Behold, he puts no trust in his holy ones. Yes, the heavens are not clean in his sight;

PAITE: Mi kihhuai leh sia, mi thulimlouhna tui banga dawn, nak sian keina semin chia:
ENGLISH: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water!

PAITE: Ka honensak ding, honja in; huan ka muhsa ka phuang ding:
ENGLISH: “I will show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I will declare:

PAITE: (Huai tuh mi pilten a pipute ua kipan na gen ua, a im kei uh;
ENGLISH: (Which wise men have told by their fathers, and have not hidden it;

PAITE: Amau kiangah kia gam tuh piakin a oma, huan mikhual kuamah a lak uah a pai kei uh: )
ENGLISH: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them):

PAITE: Mi gilouin a damsung ni tengin natna a thuaka, nuaisiahhatmi adia khawlkhawm kumte zah mahmah.
ENGLISH: the wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.

PAITE: Launa ging a bil ah a oma; hauhlaiin lokmi a tungah a hongpai ding hi:
ENGLISH: A sound of terrors is in his ears. In prosperity the destroyer shall come on him.

PAITE: Khomial akipan a hongkik ding chih a um keia, huan namsaua ngakin a om hi.
ENGLISH: He doesn’t believe that he shall return out of darkness. He is waited for by the sword.

PAITE: Tanghou zongin a tamvaka, Koia om ahia? chiin. Khomial ni a kiang chinah mansain a om chih a theikei hi.
ENGLISH: He wanders abroad for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

PAITE: Dahna leh haksatnain amah a lausaka; kumpipa galdou dia mansa bangin, amah a zou uhi.
ENGLISH: Distress and anguish make him afraid. They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

PAITE: Pathian dou dinga a khut a likkhiak jiakin, Thilbangkimhihthei dou dinga kisathei taka a oma,
ENGLISH: Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and behaves himself proudly against the Almighty;

PAITE: A lum, a tuamna sahtaknei toh amah doua a tai teitei jiakin;
ENGLISH: he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick shields of his bucklers;

PAITE: A thaua a maitang a khuha, a gila thau a kholkhawma,
ENGLISH: because he has covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.

PAITE: Khopi tulsaa a tena, kuamah ten tuak louhna inte, segawp ngiingei dingte a luah jiakin;
ENGLISH: He has lived in desolate cities, in houses which no one inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.

PAITE: A hau kei dinga, a neihlehlam a om gige kei dinga; amah leiah zung a kai kei ding;
ENGLISH: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall their possessions be extended on the earth.

PAITE: Khomial akipan a suakta kei dinga, meikuangin a selnoute a kangkeu dinga, a paklunlaite huchin a mut mang ding.
ENGLISH: He shall not depart out of darkness. The flame shall dry up his branches. By the breath of God’s mouth shall he go away.

PAITE: Amah kikhemin, banglou ah muang kei hen: bangmahlou lah a thukna hi ding ahi ngala.
ENGLISH: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself; for emptiness shall be his reward.

PAITE: A hun main hihzohin a om dia, huan ahiang nou kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: It shall be accomplished before his time. His branch shall not be green.

PAITE: Grepgui bangin a gah min lou a singpulh dia, oliv bangin a pak a pai khe ding.
ENGLISH: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive tree.

PAITE: Pathianlimsaklou kithuahpihna lah hut ding ahia, golhna puaninte lah meiin kangmang ding ahi ngala.Siatna a pai ua, thulimlouhna a suakkhe sak uh, huan a lungtang un khemna a opkeuh uh.
ENGLISH: For the company of the godless shall be barren, and fire shall consume the tents of bribery.

PAITE: Siatna a pai ua, thulimlouhna a suakkhe sak uh, huan a lungtang un khemna a opkeuh uh.
ENGLISH: They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity. Their heart prepares deceit.”

PAITE: Huan Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered,

PAITE: Huchibang thil tampi ka zata hi: lungmuanmi chimtakhuai ngen na hi uhi.
ENGLISH: “I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!

PAITE: Thu bangmahlouten tawp a nei ding uam? ahihkeileh dawng dinga nang honhihheh bang ahia?
ENGLISH: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?

PAITE: Nou bangin kei leng ka pai thei sam hi; na kha uh ka kha muna om hileh, noute dema thute kaikhawma, ka lu hon sinkhum thei ding hi vengin.
ENGLISH: I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you,

PAITE: Himahleh ka kamin nou kon hatsak dinga, ka muka muannain na lungkhamna uh kon nem ding.
ENGLISH: but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.

PAITE: Thu gen mahleng, ka dahna nepin a om keia: huan doh mahleng, hihnopin ka oma hia?
ENGLISH: “Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?

PAITE: Himahleh a honchimtak saktaa: ka lawmte tengteng na hihgamta hi.
ENGLISH: But now, God, you have surely worn me out. You have made desolate all my company.

PAITE: Huan kip takin na honlena, huai tuh kei demna theihpihna ahi: huchiin ka gawnna kei demin a thoua, ka mai tangah a theisak hi.
ENGLISH: You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.

PAITE: A hehnain kei a honbot keka, a honsawi hi; a ha a hon gawi khuma: ka tungah ka galin a mit a tathiam hi.
ENGLISH: He has torn me in his wrath, and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.

PAITE: A kam uh lianpiin a honkat khum ua; simmoh takin biang ah a honbeng uh: kei dou dingin a kikai khawm ua.
ENGLISH: They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.

PAITE: Pathianin pathianlimsakloute kiangah a honpe khiaa, migiloute khut ah a honpai khia hi.
ENGLISH: God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.

PAITE: Om nuamin ka om, huan a honkitam jaksaka; ahi, ka ngawngin a honmana, a honpai nen hi: a muitum dingin a hontung tou lai hi.
ENGLISH: I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up for his target.

PAITE: A thalkapmiten ka kim ka velah a hon um ua, ka sisanguite a bottata, a hawi kei; leiah ka sinkha a sung khia hi.
ENGLISH: His archers surround me. He splits my kidneys apart, and does not spare. He pours out my gall on the ground.

PAITE: Siatna tungah siatnain a honsesaka; galhat bangin ka tungah a tai.
ENGLISH: He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs on me like a giant.

PAITE: Ka vun tungah saiip ka khuia, leivui ah ka kingata hi.
ENGLISH: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.

PAITE: Kahnain ka mai a hoihta keia, ka mitvunte ah sihna limliap a om hi;
ENGLISH: My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids.

PAITE: Ka khut ah hiamgamna omkei mahleh, huan ka thumna siangthou mahleh.
ENGLISH: Although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.

PAITE: Aw lei, ka sisan khuh ken, huan ka kahnain khawlmun neikei hen.
ENGLISH: “Earth, don’t cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.

PAITE: Tu mahmahin, Ngaiin, a hontheihpih van ah a oma, kei hontheihpihpa tungsangah a om hi.
ENGLISH: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.

PAITE: Ka lawmten honnuihsan ua, himahleh ka mitin Pathian lamah khituite a sungkhia hi;
ENGLISH: My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,

PAITE: Huchia Pathian laka mihing dikna a letkip theiha, a inveng laka mihing tapa dikna, a letkip theihna dingin:Kum tawm a hongtun chiangin lah ka kik nawn louhna ding lampi ah ka pai ta ding ahi ngala.
ENGLISH: that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!

PAITE: Kum tawm a hongtun chiangin lah ka kik nawn louhna ding lampi ah ka pai ta ding ahi ngala.
ENGLISH: For when a few years have come, I shall go the way of no return.

PAITE: Ka lungsim hihgawpin a oma, ka nite a bei, kei dingin han mansain a om hi.
ENGLISH: “My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct, And the grave is ready for me.

PAITE: Ka kiangah musitmite a om taktak ua, a hehna uah ka mit a omgige hi.
ENGLISH: Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.

PAITE: Tuin thuchiam honpia in, nangmahmah toh kei adingin mohkhu honghi in; kei toh khutte beng ding kua a oma?
ENGLISH: “Now give a pledge, be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike hands with me?

PAITE: Theihsiamna akipan a lungtang uh na sel ngala: huai jiakin amau na hihlian kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: For you have hidden their heart from understanding, Therefore you shall not exalt them.

PAITE: Kuapeuh matdinga a lawmte heka, a neihlehlam tan tummi, a tate nangawn nit a juausuak ding hi.
ENGLISH: He who denounces his friends for a prey, Even the eyes of his children shall fail.

PAITE: Mite houlimna dingin a honbawl laia; huan tangpi kih ka honghita hi.
ENGLISH: “But he has made me a byword of the people. They spit in my face.

PAITE: Lungkhamna jiakin ka mit leng a miala, huan ka hiangte tengteng limliap bang ahi.
ENGLISH: My eye also is dim by reason of sorrow. All my members are as a shadow.

PAITE: Mi dikten hiaiah lamdang a sa ding ua, huan mihoih pathianlimsakloute dou dingin a kitokthou ding.
ENGLISH: Upright men shall be astonished at this. The innocent shall stir up himself against the godless.

PAITE: Himahleh mi diktat a lampi ah a pang zouzou dia, huan kuapeuh khut siangneite a hat semsem ding uhi.
ENGLISH: Yet shall the righteous hold on his way. He who has clean hands shall grow stronger and stronger.

PAITE: Himahleh hongkik un, na vek un, huan tuin hong un: huchiin na lak uah mi pil ka mu kei ding.
ENGLISH: But as for you all, come on now again; I shall not find a wise man among you.

PAITE: Ka nite a beita, ka thiltupte a se gawpta hi, ka lungtang ngaihtuahte nasanin.
ENGLISH: My days are past, my plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.

PAITE: Jan sunin a kheng ua: khovakin khomial a naih, a chi uh.
ENGLISH: They change the night into day, saying ‘The light is near’ in the presence of darkness.

PAITE: Seol ka in bangin en leng; khomial ah ka tutnanem phahta leng;
ENGLISH: If I look for Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. as my house, if I have spread my couch in the darkness,

PAITE: Siatna kiangah, Ka pa na hi, chi leng; tangtel kiangah, ka nu leh ka sanggamnu na hi, chi leng;
ENGLISH: If I have said to corruption, ‘You are my father;’ to the worm, ‘My mother,’ and ‘my sister;’

PAITE: Huchi hileh ka lametna koia om ahia? Huan lamet nei hileng kuan honmusak dia?Seol mundai ah te paisukin leivui ah ka kik khawm ding ua adiam?
ENGLISH: where then is my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?

PAITE: Seol mundai ah te paisukin leivui ah ka kik khawm ding ua adiam?
ENGLISH: Shall it go down with me to the gates of Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. , or descend together into the dust?”

PAITE: Huchiin Bildad Sua miin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

PAITE: Thute zonga bangtan thang kam ding na hia ua? Ngaihtuah in, huaikhit chiangin ka pau ding uh.
ENGLISH: “How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.

PAITE: Bangdia gamsa banga sima oma, na mitmuh ua sianglou honghi ka hi ua?
ENGLISH: Why are we counted as animals, which have become unclean in your sight?

PAITE: Nang na hehna kipumpei nang jiakin lei mangngilhin a om diam? ahihkeileh a mun akipatin suangpi suan khiakin a om diam?
ENGLISH: You who tear yourself in your anger, shall the earth be forsaken for you? Or shall the rock be removed out of its place?

PAITE: A hi, migilou vakna mihsakin a om dinga, a meiek a tang kei ding.
ENGLISH: “Yes, the light of the wicked shall be put out, The spark of his fire shall not shine.

PAITE: A puanin ah vakna a mial dia, a tunga a khawnvak mihsak ahi ding.
ENGLISH: The light shall be dark in his tent. His lamp above him shall be put out.

PAITE: A hatna kalsuante hihtuailuai ahi dia, huan amah thupha genin amah a paikhe ding hi.
ENGLISH: The steps of his strength shall be shortened. His own counsel shall cast him down.

PAITE: Amah khe mahmahin lah len sungah amah a pai lut ngala, huan len ah a kiawksak hi.
ENGLISH: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he wanders into its mesh.

PAITE: Thangin a khetulah a man dia, thangin amah a len ding hi.
ENGLISH: A snare will take him by the heel. A trap will catch him.

PAITE: Leiah amaha dingin a ba selin a oma, lampi ah amah adin thang.
ENGLISH: A noose is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him in the way.

PAITE: Kihtakhuaiten ning chiteng ah amah a lausak dia, a khetul ah a delhjui ding hi.
ENGLISH: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall chase him at his heels.

PAITE: A hatna gilkial nekin a om dia, huan tuahsiatna a khawlna dingin mansain a om ding.
ENGLISH: His strength shall be famished. Calamity shall be ready at his side.

PAITE: A pumpi hiangte a negai dinga, ahi, ahiangte sihna ta masapenin a negai ding.
ENGLISH: The members of his body shall be devoured. The firstborn of death shall devour his members.

PAITE: A suan a puanin akipan zungkalh khiakin a om dia; huan lauhuainate kumpipa kianga piin a om ding.
ENGLISH: He shall be rooted out of his tent where he trusts. He shall be brought to the king of terrors.

PAITE: Amaha hi lou a puanin sungah teng a om ding: a tenna ah kat theh jakin a om ding hi.
ENGLISH: There shall dwell in his tent that which is none of his. Sulfur shall be scattered on his habitation.

PAITE: Nuailamah a zungte a keu dia, huan tunglamah ahiang sat khiak ahi ding.
ENGLISH: His roots shall be dried up beneath. Above shall his branch be cut off.

PAITE: Lei akipanin a theihgige a mangthang ding; huan kongzing ah min a neikei ding.
ENGLISH: His memory shall perish from the earth. He shall have no name in the street.

PAITE: Khovak akipanin khomial ah hawllut ahi dinga, huan khovel akipana delh khiak.
ENGLISH: He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.

PAITE: A mite lakah tapa a neikei dia tapa tapa leng: a omna ah kuamah omlai a om kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: He shall have neither son nor grandson among his people, nor any remaining where he lived.

PAITE: Tumlama omten a ni lamdang a sa ding ua, suahlama omte hihlaua a om bang un.Huchibang mi diktatloute tennate ahi petmaha, huan hiai Pathian theilou mi mun ahi hi.
ENGLISH: Those who come after shall be astonished at his day, as those who went before were frightened.

PAITE: Huchibang mi diktatloute tennate ahi petmaha, huan hiai Pathian theilou mi mun ahi hi.
ENGLISH: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous. This is the place of him who doesn’t know God.”

PAITE: Huan Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered,

PAITE: Bangtan ka kha hihbuaia, thutea honhihjan gawp ding na hi ua?
ENGLISH: “How long will you torment me, and crush me with words?

PAITE: Hiai sawmvei tak na honkouta ua: ka tunga giloutaka na hih uh na zum kei ua.
ENGLISH: You have reproached me ten times. You aren’t ashamed that you attack me.

PAITE: Huan na na paikhialta mawng leng maw, keimah kianga ka diklouhna om gige hi.
ENGLISH: If it is true that I have erred, my error remains with myself.

PAITE: Kei demin nou kiliansak petmah ve nuchin, ka minsiatna ka tungah gen ven uchin:
ENGLISH: If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach;

PAITE: Pathianin ka thu ah honzouta chih tuin thei un, huan a lenin a honum suak hi.
ENGLISH: know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.

PAITE: Ngai un, Hiamgamna, chiin ka kikou khiaa, himahleh jakin ka om kei: panpih deihin ka kikoua, himahleh vaihawmna a om kei hi.
ENGLISH: “Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard. I cry for help, but there is no justice.

PAITE: Ka pai theihlouhna dingin ka lampi a um a, huan ka paina dingte ah khomial a koih hi.
ENGLISH: He has walled up my way so that I can’t pass, and has set darkness in my paths.

PAITE: Ka thupina honsuahsaka, ka lu akipan lallukhu a la.
ENGLISH: He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.

PAITE: Ning chitengah a hon hihniama, ka mangta hi: huan, sing bangin ka lametna a bot khia.
ENGLISH: He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. My hope he has plucked up like a tree.

PAITE: Ka tungah a hehna leng a soua, amah adingin a galte laka khat bangin a honsim hi.
ENGLISH: He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries.

PAITE: A sepaihpawlte a hongkuan khawm ua, ka siatna dingin a lampi uh a bawl uh, huan ka puanin kimvelin puanin a kai uh.
ENGLISH: His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.

PAITE: Kei akipanin ka unaute gamlapi ah a koiha, ka mel-theihte kei akipanin a mituam vekta uh.
ENGLISH: “He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.

PAITE: Ka tanauten a honjuausanta ua, huan ka lawm theihngeiten a honmangngilhta uh.
ENGLISH: My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.

PAITE: Ka in tengte leh, ka sikhanuten, mikhual a honsa ua: a mitmuh un namdangmi ka hi.
ENGLISH: Those who dwell in my house, and my maids, count me for a stranger. I am an alien in their sight.

PAITE: Ka sikha ka sama, a hondawng kei, ka kamin amah khem mahleng leng.
ENGLISH: I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.

PAITE: Ka ji adingin muhthadahhuai ka hia, ka nu tate adingin, kihhuai.
ENGLISH: My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother.

PAITE: Naupang neute nangawnin a honsimmoh ua; ka thoh leh, ka siatna dingin thu a gen uhi.
ENGLISH: Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me.

PAITE: Ka lawm gilte tengtengin kei a honhua ua: huan amau ka itte ka tungah a hel uh.
ENGLISH: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.

PAITE: Ka guh ka vun ah leh ka sa ah a belh bikbeka, huan ka ha vun toh ka suakta hi.
ENGLISH: My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

PAITE: Honhehpih un, honhehpih un, Aw nou ka lawmte; Pathian khutin kei a honkhoihta ngala.
ENGLISH: “Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends; for the hand of God has touched me.

PAITE: Bangdia Pathian banga nou honsawi na hi ua, ka saa bangdia lungkim lou na hi ua?
ENGLISH: Why do you persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?

PAITE: Aw ka thute tuin gelhin om le uh aw; Aw laibu ah kigelh lut le aw;
ENGLISH: “Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!

PAITE: Sik leh ngen gelhna zumin khantawn adingin suangpia gelh hile uh aw;
ENGLISH: That with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!

PAITE: Himahleh ka Tanpa a hing chih leh, leitungah a tawp chiangin a ding ding chih ka thei hi:
ENGLISH: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.

PAITE: Huan ka vun huchibanga hihsiata a om khit nungin, himahleh ka sa akipan Pathian ka mu ding hi:
ENGLISH: After my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I see God,

PAITE: Keimah adingin amah keimahmahin ka mu dia, huan ka miten a en dia, midang hi louin. Ka sungah ka lungtang a sidangta hi!
ENGLISH: Whom I, even I, shall see on my side. My eyes shall see, and not as a stranger. “My heart is consumed within me.

PAITE: Amah bangchibangin i sawi ta phet diamah; na chih uleh, kei ah thu bul muhin a om chih theiin;Namsau kihta un: hehnain lah namsau gawtnate a hontun ngala, huchia vaihawmna a om chih na theih theihna ding un.
ENGLISH: If you say, ‘How we will persecute him!’ because the root of the matter is found in me,

PAITE: Namsau kihta un: hehnain lah namsau gawtnate a hontun ngala, huchia vaihawmna a om chih na theih theihna ding un.
ENGLISH: be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment.”

PAITE: TOUPA Pathian tapate ahongkilak ni uh a om nawna, huan a lak uah Setan leng a hongpai sama TOUPA maa kilak ding in.
ENGLISH: Again it happened on the day when the God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, that Satan came also among them to present himself before Yahweh.

PAITE: Huan TOUPAN Setan kiangah, Kaw hongkipan na hia? a chi a. Huan Setanin TOUPA a dawnga, Leia langkhat langkhata hoha, a sunga tou vaka suk vak ka hi, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”

PAITE: Huan TOUPAN Setan kiangah, Ka sikha Job na ngaihtuah ngei hia? amah banga hoihkim leh mi tang, Pathian kihtaa hoihlou mudah leiah lah kuamah a om ngal keia: amah siatna dingin hon tangsak mah lechin, a ginomna a len chinten hi, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is none like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”

PAITE: Huan Setanin TOUPA a dawnga, Vun sikin vun, ahi, mihingin a neih tengteng hinna sikin a pe ding hi.
ENGLISH: Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.

PAITE: Himahleh tuin na khut khainla, a guh leh a sa khoih lechin, huan na maitangah nang hon gense ding hi, a chi a.
ENGLISH: But put forth your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face.”

PAITE: Huan TOUPAN Setan kiangah, Ngaiin, Amah na khut ah a om hi; a hinna leltak hawiin, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life.”

PAITE: Huchiin Setan a pawt khiaa TOUPA ma akipanin, meima tumin a khepek nuai akipan a lujang tanin Job a gawta.
ENGLISH: So Satan went forth from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

PAITE: Huchiin aman kikhuatna dingin belpei a laa; huan meivu lakah a tuta hi.
ENGLISH: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.

PAITE: Huchihlaiin a jiin a kiangah, Na ginomna len chinten lailai na hi hia? Pathian gensia inla, siin, a chi a.
ENGLISH: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”

PAITE: Himahleh a kiangah, Numei haite thugente laka khat bangin thu na gen. Bang ahia? Pathian khut ah hoih i mu dia, hoihlou leng i mu kei dia hia? a chi a. Hiai tengtengah Jobin a muk in thil a hihkhial kei hi.
ENGLISH: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.

PAITE: Huchia Job lawm thumten a tunga hiai hoihlou hongtung tengteng a jak un, amau mi chih amah mun akipanin a hong ua: Elipha Teman mi leh, Bildad Sua mi leh Zophar Naaman mi: huan amah kah ding leh amah lungmuan dingin hoh khawm dingin thuseh a bawl uhi.
ENGLISH: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.

PAITE: Huan gamla pia a dak touh uleh, amah a theikei ua, huan nakpiin a kikou khia ua, a kapta uhi; huan a puannaktual uh michihin a botkek ua, a lu tang uah van lamah leivui a khita uhi.Huchiin a kiangah leitungah ni sagih leh jan sagih a tu ua, a kiangah kuamahin thu khat leng a gen kei uh: a lungkhamna a thupi mahmah chih lah a thei ngal ua.
ENGLISH: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.

PAITE: Huchiin a kiangah leitungah ni sagih leh jan sagih a tu ua, a kiangah kuamahin thu khat leng a gen kei uh: a lungkhamna a thupi mahmah chih lah a thei ngal ua.
ENGLISH: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.

PAITE: Huan Zophar Naaman miin a dawng a, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered,

PAITE: Huaijiakin ka ngaihtuahnaten kei dawnna a honpiaa, ka sunga om ka kinna thu jiak mahmahin.
ENGLISH: “Therefore do my thoughts give answer to me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.

PAITE: Kei honzahlaksak salhna ka zataa, huan ka theihsiamna khain a hondawng hi.
ENGLISH: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.

PAITE: Lei tunga mihing koiha a om nungsiah, hun lui thu hiai na theikei maw;
ENGLISH: Don’t you know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,

PAITE: Gilou vualzohna a toma, huan pathianlimsakloute nuamsakna mitphiat kal sunglel ahi chih?
ENGLISH: that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment?

PAITE: A hoihkimna vante phain tuangtou mahleh, a luin meipite pha mahleh;
ENGLISH: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,

PAITE: Himahleh amah ek bangin khantawnin a mangthang dinga: Koia om ahia? amah muten a chi ding uh.
ENGLISH: yet he shall perish forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him shall say, ‘Where is he?’

PAITE: Mang bangin a lengmang dinga, huan muhin a omkei ding hi: ahi, jan mengmuh banga hawlmangin a om ding hi.
ENGLISH: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found. Yes, he shall be chased away like a vision of the night.

PAITE: Amah mu mitin amah a muta kei ding hi; a munin leng amah a muta kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: The eye which saw him shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more see him.

PAITE: A taten gentheite deihsakna a zong ding ua, huan a khutten a hauhsakna ape nawn ding hi.
ENGLISH: His children shall seek the favor of the poor. His hands shall give back his wealth.

PAITE: A guhte a tuailainain a dima, himahleh leivui ah amah toh a lum ding hi.
ENGLISH: His bones are full of his youth, but youth shall lie down with him in the dust.

PAITE: Gitlouhna a kam ah khum mahleh, a lei ah sel mahleh;
ENGLISH: “Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,

PAITE: Sitin, paisak keiin, a kam sungah kem gige zo mahleh;
ENGLISH: though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his mouth;

PAITE: Himahleh a gila a an a kitoka, a sunga khuai gu ahi hi.
ENGLISH: yet his food in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.

PAITE: Hauhsaknate a nawmvalha, huan a lokhe nawn ding hi: Pathianin a gilpi akipanin apaikhe ding hi.
ENGLISH: He has swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again. God will cast them out of his belly.

PAITE: Khuai gu a tep dia: gul leiin amah a that ding.
ENGLISH: He shall suck cobra venom. The viper’s tongue shall kill him.

PAITE: Luipite, khuaiju leh nawituidat lui luangte a en kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: He shall not look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter.

PAITE: Sepgim gah a pe nawn dia huan a nawmvalh suk kei ding hi; a muhsa ah kipahna a neikei ding.
ENGLISH: That for which he labored he shall restore, and shall not swallow it down. According to the substance that he has gotten, he shall not rejoice.

PAITE: Aman lah gentheite a nuaisiaha, a mangngilh hi; a lam louhpi in hiamgamtakin alata.
ENGLISH: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he shall not build it up.

PAITE: A deihgawlnain tawp aneihlouhjiakin, a kipahpih thil himhim a khol kei ding.
ENGLISH: “Because he knew no quietness within him, he shall not save anything of that in which he delights.

PAITE: A nekgaihlouh bangmah omlai a om kei hi; huaijiakin a hauhnain a daih sawt kei ding.
ENGLISH: There was nothing left that he didn’t devour, therefore his prosperity shall not endure.

PAITE: A nian san lain haksa sakna a nei dia: gimthuak mi chiteng khut a tungah a hongtung ding.
ENGLISH: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress shall overtake him. The hand of everyone who is in misery shall come on him.

PAITE: A gilpi hihdim dinga a kisaklaiin, Pathianin a tungah a thangpaihna kihtakhuaina a khe dinga, a nek laiin a tungah a zusak ding hi.
ENGLISH: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.

PAITE: Sik galvan akipan a tai dia, huan dal thalin amah a kap pailet ding.
ENGLISH: He shall flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow shall strike him through.

PAITE: A dok khiaa, huan a pumpi akipanin a hongpai khia: ahi a sinkha apat a mukzum te velvel hongpai khiaa launate a tungah a hongtung hi.
ENGLISH: He draws it forth, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him.

PAITE: A gou dingin mialna tengteng kholkhawmin a om: mi mutlouh meiin amah a negai ding; a puanina nutsiata om a negai ding hi.
ENGLISH: All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire shall devour him. It shall consume that which is left in his tent.

PAITE: Vanten a thulimlouhna a taklang ding ua, huan lei amah dou dingin a thou ding.
ENGLISH: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity. The earth shall rise up against him.

PAITE: A ina punna a paimang dinga, a vante a heh niin a luang mang ding hi.Hiai bel Pathian akipana mi gilou tantuan ahi, a gouluah dia Pathianin a sehsak.
ENGLISH: The increase of his house shall depart. They shall rush away in the day of his wrath.

PAITE: Hiai bel Pathian akipana mi gilou tantuan ahi, a gouluah dia Pathianin a sehsak.
ENGLISH: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God.”

PAITE: Huan Jonin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered,

PAITE: Ka thugen hoihtakin ngaikhia unla, hiai na khamuanna thu uh hihen.
ENGLISH: “Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.

PAITE: Honthuak teitei unla, ka hon-gen ding a, ka gen khit chiangin nuihsan na nu teh.
ENGLISH: Allow me, and I also will speak; After I have spoken, mock on.

PAITE: Kei phunna mihing tungah ahi ahia? Bangdia kuhkalloua omlou ding ka hia?
ENGLISH: As for me, is my complaint to man? Why shouldn’t I be impatient?

PAITE: Honen unla, lamdang sa unla, khutin na kam uh hum un.
ENGLISH: Look at me, and be astonished. Lay your hand on your mouth.

PAITE: Ka ngaihtuahin ka lung a donga, linnain ka sa a man nak.
ENGLISH: When I remember, I am troubled. Horror takes hold of my flesh.

PAITE: Bangjiakin ahia migilou a hina, tekkuna a dama, a hong thupikhiak?
ENGLISH: “Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?

PAITE: A suante uh a kiang uah a mitmuh uah a hihkipa, a gil ua gahte a mai ma uah.
ENGLISH: Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes.

PAITE: A inleloute uh lauhuai lakah a bita, Pathian chiang a tunguah a ke kei hi.
ENGLISH: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.

PAITE: A bawngtal un chi a khah a, a juau ngeikei, a bawngpi un nou a nei a, a nou a siat ngeikei.
ENGLISH: Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows calve, and don’t miscarry.

PAITE: Ganhon bangin a taneute uh a pawtsak ua, a tate uh a lam uh.
ENGLISH: They send forth their little ones like a flock. Their children dance.

PAITE: A pekging uleh kaihging toh kituakin la a sa ua, a tamngai ging uah a kipak uh.
ENGLISH: They sing to the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.

PAITE: A nite uh lamzangtakin a zang ua, lungmuangin Seol ah a paisuk uh.
ENGLISH: They spend their days in prosperity. In an instant they go down to Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. .

PAITE: Huan, Pathian kiangah, Honpaisan in, na lampite theih ka kilawp kei uh.
ENGLISH: They tell God, ‘Depart from us, for we don’t want to know about your ways.

PAITE: Bangkimhihthei banga a hih, a na ka sep ding uh, A kianga ka thum un punna banga ka muh ding uh? a chi uh.
ENGLISH: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What profit should we have, if we pray to him?’

PAITE: Ngaiin; a lamzanna uh a khut ua om ahi kei ahia? Migilou lemtheihna kei akipana gamlapia om ahi.
ENGLISH: Behold, their prosperity is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.

PAITE: Migilou meisel bangzah vei tak a mita, vangtahna a tung ua a tuna, a thangpaihnaa Pathianin lungkhamna a piak chiat?
ENGLISH: “How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out, that their calamity comes on them, that God distributes sorrows in his anger?

PAITE: Bangzah vei ahia buhpawl huih mut bang a hihua, buhsi huihpi mutmang bang a hih uh?
ENGLISH: How often is it that they are as stubble before the wind, as chaff that the storm carries away?

PAITE: Pathianin gitlouhnate a tate uh adingin a kholkhawm, na chi ua, amau tungah tungsak le ake, a theihsiam nadingun.
ENGLISH: You say, ‘God lays up his iniquity for his children.’ Let him recompense it to himself, that he may know it.

PAITE: Amau mit ngeiin a siatna uh mu uhenla, Bangkimhihthei thangpaihna dawn uhen.
ENGLISH: Let his own eyes see his destruction. Let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

PAITE: Aman nungin a in uh amau adin banga ahih, a kha zah uh hihtawp a hih nungin?
ENGLISH: For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?

PAITE: Kuan ahia Pathian theihna sinsak ding? aman lah sangpia omte vai a hawmsak ngala.
ENGLISH: “Shall any teach God knowledge, since he judges those who are high?

PAITE: A lutlaiin mi a si a, nuamsa leh bittaka om in.
ENGLISH: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

PAITE: A sa thauin a dima, a guhngekte leng nawnnain a dim hi.
ENGLISH: His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.

PAITE: Midang lungkhamtakin a si a, hoihna himhim chiam ngei louin.
ENGLISH: Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good.

PAITE: Vutlak ah kibangin a lum ua, thanin a pumtuam hi.
ENGLISH: They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.

PAITE: Ngaiin, na ngaihtuahte uh ka thei, dikloupia ka tunga na sawmte uh.
ENGLISH: “Behold, I know your thoughts, the devices with which you would wrong me.

PAITE: Koiah ahia kumpi in a om, migilou tenna puanin koiah a om a? na chi uh.
ENGLISH: For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?’

PAITE: Zinzin mite na dong ngeikei ua hia? A gente uh na pom kei ua hia?
ENGLISH: Haven’t you asked wayfaring men? Don’t you know their evidences,

PAITE: Migilou tuh vangtah niin hawiin a om a, thangpaih niin amah hotkhiakin a om, chih.
ENGLISH: that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity, That they are led forth to the day of wrath?

PAITE: Kua ahia a maitang a a lampi pulak dinga, kua ahia a thilhih banga amah din ding?
ENGLISH: Who shall declare his way to his face? Who shall repay him what he has done?

PAITE: Han lama puak ahih laiin, a han ven ahi.
ENGLISH: Yet he will be borne to the grave. Men shall keep watch over the tomb.

PAITE: Luiguama leitangte amah adin a nuama; mi tengteng in a nung a jui ua, amah maa napaite simsenglouh ahi uh.Bangchiin thumumal omlou piin hon khamuan ding na hia? Na dawnnate uah juauthu loungal bangmah a om kei hi.
ENGLISH: The clods of the valley shall be sweet to him. All men shall draw after him, as there were innumerable before him.

PAITE: Bangchiin thumumal omlou piin hon khamuan ding na hia? Na dawnnate uah juauthu loungal bangmah a om kei hi.
ENGLISH: So how can you comfort me with nonsense, because in your answers there remains only falsehood?”

PAITE: Huchiin Elipha Teman miin a dawng a, hichiin a chi a;
ENGLISH: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

PAITE: Mihing Pathian adingin a phatuam thei diam? Kuapeuh a pil amah mah adingin a phatuam ngeia.
ENGLISH: “Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.

PAITE: Na diktat, Thilbangkimhihthei adinga kipahna ahi himhim hia? ahihkeileh na lampite na hoihkim sak, amah dia punna hia?
ENGLISH: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him, that you make your ways perfect?

PAITE: Nang a honsalha, vaihawmnaa nang toh a lut, amah na kihtak jiak hia?
ENGLISH: Is it for your piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?

PAITE: Na gitlouhna a lian kei maw? Na thulimlouhna ah leng tawpna a om sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: Isn’t your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities.

PAITE: Bangmahlou dingin na unau thuchiamte na lata ngala, huan vuaktangte a puansilh uh na suahsaka.
ENGLISH: For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.

PAITE: Gim adin dawn dingin tui na pe kei a, huan gilkial adin tanghou na it hi.
ENGLISH: You haven’t given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.

PAITE: Himahleh mi hat in gam a neia; mi deihthoh a sungah a teng hi.
ENGLISH: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.

PAITE: Khutvuakin meithaite na sawl manga, huan pabeite khutte hihtanin a om hi.
ENGLISH: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.

PAITE: Huaijiakin thangte na kim ah a om ua, huan lau guihnain nang honhihbuai hi.
ENGLISH: Therefore snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,

PAITE: Ahihkeileh khomial, na muh theihlouh, leh tui tampiin nang a honkhuh hi.
ENGLISH: or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you.

PAITE: Van sangah Pathian a om ka hia? huan aksite sandan en in, sang hina tel uh e;
ENGLISH: “Isn’t God in the heights of heaven? See the height of the stars, how high they are!

PAITE: Huan nang, Pathianin bang a theia? khomial bikbek lakah vai a hawm thei dia hia?
ENGLISH: You say, ‘What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?

PAITE: Amaha dingin meipi sahte, a muhlouhna din, khuhna ahi a; huan van kum sungah a vak ahi, na chi.
ENGLISH: Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he doesn’t see. He walks on the vault of the sky.’

PAITE: Mi giloute totsa lampi lui na kem ding hia?
ENGLISH: Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,

PAITE: A hun ma ua lak manga oma, a kingakna ua tuiluang banga butkhiak a omte:
ENGLISH: who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a stream,

PAITE: Pathian kianga, Hon pai mangsanin; huan eia dingin Thilbangkimhihtheiin bang a hih theia? chite.
ENGLISH: who said to God, ‘Depart from us;’ and, ‘What can the Almighty do for us?’

PAITE: Himahleh a inte uh thil hoihin a dimsak ua: himahleh migiloute thugen kei akipan a gamla hi.
ENGLISH: Yet he filled their houses with good things, but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

PAITE: Mi diktatten a mu ua, a kipak ua; huan mihoihten amau a nuihsan ua,
ENGLISH: The righteous see it, and are glad. The innocent ridicule them,

PAITE: Chihtaktakin ei dou dinga thoute sat khiakin a om ua, huan amaute laka omlai meiin a hulgaita, chiin.
ENGLISH: saying, ‘Surely those who rose up against us are cut off. The fire has consumed their remnant.’

PAITE: Tuin amah kimeltheihpih inla, muang takin omin: Huaiah hoih na kiangah a hongpai ding hi.
ENGLISH: “Acquaint yourself with him, now, and be at peace. Thereby good shall come to you.

PAITE: A kam akipanin dan tuh sangin, ka honngen hi, huan na lungtang ah a thute khol khawmin.
ENGLISH: Please receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.

PAITE: Thilbangkimhihthei kianga na kik nawn leh, lam kipin na om ding hi; na puaninte akipana gamla pia diktatlouhna na koih mang leh.
ENGLISH: If you return to the Almighty, you shall be built up, if you put away unrighteousness far from your tents.

PAITE: Huan na gou leivui ah koih inla, huan luite suangte lakah Ophir dang kaeng;
ENGLISH: Lay your treasure in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.

PAITE: Huchiin Thilbangkimhihthei na gou ahi dia, nanga dingin manpha dangka.
ENGLISH: The Almighty will be your treasure, and precious silver to you.

PAITE: Huchiin Thilbangkimhihthei ah na kipakin, Pathian kiangah na dak tou ding a hih jiakin.
ENGLISH: For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and shall lift up your face to God.

PAITE: Amah kiangah na thumna na gen dia, aman a honza ding.
ENGLISH: You shall make your prayer to him, and he will hear you. You shall pay your vows.

PAITE: Thil khat tungah thupukna bawlin thu na pe dia, huan nanga dia hihkipin a om ding hi; huan na lampite ah khovak a tang ding.
ENGLISH: You shall also decree a thing, and it shall be established to you. Light shall shine on your ways.

PAITE: A honsawnpuk chiang un, Thoh touhna a om, na chi ding; huan mi niamkhiak aman a hondam ding hi.Amah a hoihlou nasan a suaktasak dinga: ahi, na khutte sianna jiakin amah suangtaksakin a om ding.
ENGLISH: When they cast down, you shall say, ‘be lifted up.’ He will save the humble person.

PAITE: Amah a hoihlou nasan a suaktasak dinga: ahi, na khutte sianna jiakin amah suangtaksakin a om ding.
ENGLISH: He will even deliver him who is not innocent. Yes, he shall be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”

PAITE: Huchiin Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered,

PAITE: Tuni mahmahin ka phunna helhuai ahi: ka thuakna ka mauna sangin a gikjaw hi.
ENGLISH: “Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.

PAITE: Aw amah ka muhna mun thei lengla, a tutna mahmah ah hoh thei leng aw!
ENGLISH: Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!

PAITE: A maah ka thu ka bawlhoih dia, thugentein ka kam dimsak ding hi veng.
ENGLISH: I would set my cause in order before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.

PAITE: A honna dawnna ding thute ka thei dia, huan bang ahia ka kianga a gen ding ka theisiam ding.
ENGLISH: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would tell me.

PAITE: A thilhihtheihna letnain kei a honsel diam? Ii; himahleh kei a honlimsak ding hi.
ENGLISH: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No, but he would listen to me.

PAITE: Huailaiah mi dikin amah thu a sutpih thei dia; huchiin ka vaihawmmi akipan suahtaksakin ka om tawntungta ding hi.
ENGLISH: There the upright might reason with him, so I should be delivered forever from my judge.

PAITE: Ngaiin, mailam juanin ka paia, himahleh huailaiah a om kei; huan nunglam juanin, himahleh amah ka mu kei hi.
ENGLISH: “If I go east, he is not there; if west, I can’t find him;

PAITE: Veilam pangah, na sep laiin, himahleh amah ka mu theikeia: taklam pangah a bu, amah ka muh theihlouhna dingin.
ENGLISH: He works to the north, but I can’t see him. He turns south, but I can’t catch a glimpse of him.

PAITE: Hiamhleh ka zuih lampi a thei a; a hon zeet laiin, dangkaeng bangin ka honsuakkhe ding hi.
ENGLISH: But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I shall come forth like gold.

PAITE: Ka khein a kalsuante a len kipa; a lampi ka juita, ka pial kei.
ENGLISH: My foot has held fast to his steps. I have kept his way, and not turned aside.

PAITE: A mukte thupiak akipan ka pai kik keia, a kama thute a kiphamoh ka an sangin ka kholkhawm jaw hi.
ENGLISH: I haven’t gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.

PAITE: Himahleh amah lungsim khek lou ahia, amah kuan a hei thei dia? a khain a deih, huai mah a hih jel hi.
ENGLISH: But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? What his soul desires, even that he does.

PAITE: Kei dia sehsa a hih ngala: huan thil huchibang tampi a kiangah a om hi.
ENGLISH: For he performs that which is appointed for me. Many such things are with him.

PAITE: Huaijiakin a omna ah ka buaia; ka ngaihtuah chiangin amah ka lau hi.
ENGLISH: Therefore I am terrified at his presence. When I consider, I am afraid of him.

PAITE: Pathianin lah ka lungtang a bahsakta ngala, huan Thilbangkimhihtheiin a honhihbuaita hi.Khomial main satkhiakin ka om ngal keia, ka maia kipan khomial sah leng a khuh sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: For God has made my heart faint. The Almighty has terrified me.

PAITE: Khomial main satkhiakin ka om ngal keia, ka maia kipan khomial sah leng a khuh sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face.

PAITE: Bangdia Thilbangkimhiihtheiin vaihawmna hunte bawl lou ahia? huan amah theiten bangdia a nite mu lou uh ahia?
ENGLISH: “Why aren’t times laid up by the Almighty? Why don’t those who know him see his days?

PAITE: Gamgi suan a om ua; ganhon hiamgamtakin a la mang ua, a vak uh.
ENGLISH: There are people who remove the landmarks. They violently take away flocks, and feed them.

PAITE: Pabeite sabengtung a hawl mang ua: thuchiamna dingin meithai bawngtal a la uh.
ENGLISH: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.

PAITE: Lampi akipan tasamte a hei khia ua: leia gentheite a kisel khawm uhi.
ENGLISH: They turn the needy out of the way. The poor of the earth all hide themselves.

PAITE: Ngaiin gam keua sabengtungte bangin a thilhihna lam uah, an thanuamtaka zongin a pai khia ua; a tate uh a dingin gamdaiin amau an a suaksak hi.
ENGLISH: Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert, they go forth to their work, seeking diligently for food. The wilderness yields them bread for their children.

PAITE: Gam lamah a gan an uh a at ua; huan migiloute grep gah a la uh.
ENGLISH: They cut their provender in the field. They glean the vineyard of the wicked.

PAITE: Jan khuain puan beiin vuaktangin a lum ua, huan khovot ah khuhna neilouin.
ENGLISH: They lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.

PAITE: Mualte vuahphinin a kawt ua, belhding deihmanin suangpi a kawi uhi.
ENGLISH: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for lack of a shelter.

PAITE: Nawi akipan pabei kai khia a om ua, huan gentheite thuchiam la:
ENGLISH: There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,

PAITE: Huchiin tasamte puanbeiin vuaktangin a vialvak ua, buhphalte gilkialin a pua uhi.
ENGLISH: So that they go around naked without clothing. Being hungry, they carry the sheaves.

PAITE: Oliv sing lakah sathau a bawl ua; a uain sukna uh a chil ua, himahleh a dangtak uhi.
ENGLISH: They make oil within the walls of these men. They tread wine presses, and suffer thirst.

PAITE: Khopi akipanin mite a mau ua, huan liamte kha a kikou khiaa; himahleh Pathianin a limsak kei hi.
ENGLISH: From out of the populous city, men groan. The soul of the wounded cries out, yet God doesn’t regard the folly.

PAITE: Hiaite khovak tunga helte laka ahi ua; huai lampite a theikei ua, huaia lampite ah a om gige sam kei uhi.
ENGLISH: “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths.

PAITE: Tualthatmi jan mialin a thoua, gentheite leh tasamte a thata; ahi, janin gutami ahi.
ENGLISH: The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.

PAITE: Angkawm mi mitin leng khomui a ngaka, kuamahin honmu kei ding, chiin: huan a mai a bawl lamdang hi.
ENGLISH: The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye shall see me.’ He disguises his face.

PAITE: Khomialin inte a vut pailet ua: sun chiangin a kikhum bilh ua; khovak a theikei uh.
ENGLISH: In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They don’t know the light.

PAITE: Amaute tengteng adingin lah jingsang sihna limliap bang ahi ngala; janmial lauhuaite lah lawmin a nei ngal ua.
ENGLISH: For the morning is to all of them like thick darkness, for they know the terrors of the thick darkness.

PAITE: Tuite tungah kintaka taihmangin om ua; a tantuan uh leiah hamsiatin a om: agrephuante sukmiin a naih kei.
ENGLISH: “They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their portion is cursed in the earth. They don’t turn into the way of the vineyards.

PAITE: Khokhal leh nisain vuk tuite a tawpkanga: huaibangmahin thilhihkhialte Seolin a hih hi.
ENGLISH: Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. those who have sinned.

PAITE: Sulin amah a mangngilh dia; thanin limsa takin amah kivaknain a nei ding uh; theihgigein a omta kei dia, huan diktatlouhna sing banga hihtanin a om ding.
ENGLISH: The womb shall forget him. The worm shall feed sweetly on him. He shall be no more remembered. Unrighteousness shall be broken as a tree.

PAITE: Ta neilou numei ching a negaia; meithai adingin hoih a hih kei hi.
ENGLISH: He devours the barren who don’t bear. He shows no kindness to the widow.

PAITE: Ahia lah Pathianin a thilhihtheihnain in hatte hin a sausaka, hinna a lamet phaklouh lai unleng a dingtou uh.
ENGLISH: Yet God preserves the mighty by his power. He rises up who has no assurance of life.

PAITE: Bitna Pathianin amau a piaa, huchiin huaiah a khawl uh; huan a mitte a lampite uah a om hi.
ENGLISH: God gives them security, and they rest in it. His eyes are on their ways.

PAITE: Hihletin a om ua; himahleh sawtlou kalin, a bei uhi; ahi, sukniamin a om ua, mi dang tengteng bangin lampi akipan lak khiakin a om ua, buhvui banga at khiakin a om uhi.Huchibang na hi kei ta leh kua ahia juautheia hon chian dinga, ka thugen ah leng bangmah omlou-a lak ding?
ENGLISH: They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone. Yes, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.

PAITE: Huchibang na hi kei ta leh kua ahia juautheia hon chian dinga, ka thugen ah leng bangmah omlou-a lak ding?
ENGLISH: If it isn’t so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?”

PAITE: Huan Bildad Sua miin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

PAITE: Lalna leh launa Pathian kiangah a om; aman a mun sangte ah muanna a bawl hi.
ENGLISH: “Dominion and fear are with him. He makes peace in his high places.

PAITE: A sepaihte hihzah himhim a om ahia? huan a vakna suahlouhna kua a om a?
ENGLISH: Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not arise?

PAITE: Huchi a hih chiangin Pathian lakah bangchiin mihing a dik thei dia? ahihkeileh amah numei suan bangchiin a siang thei dia?
ENGLISH: How then can man be just with God? Or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?

PAITE: Ngaiin, khapi nangawnin tetna a neikeia, a mitmuhin aksite a siangthou kei hi.Mihing, tangtel, bangchiphetin a siangkei zo de aw; huan mihing ta, tangtel;
ENGLISH: Behold, even the moon has no brightness, and the stars are not pure in his sight;

PAITE: Mihing, tangtel, bangchiphetin a siangkei zo de aw; huan mihing ta, tangtel;
ENGLISH: How much less man, who is a worm, the son of man, who is a worm!”

PAITE: Huan Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered,

PAITE: Thilhihtheihna neilou amah bangchiin na panpihta a amai; hanta neilou ban bangchiin na hondamta a amai;
ENGLISH: “How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!

PAITE: Pilna neilou amah bangchin na thuhilha, huan nakpitaka theihna hoih na phuangkheta a;
ENGLISH: How have you counseled him who has no wisdom, and plentifully declared sound knowledge!

PAITE: Kua kiangah ahia thute na genkhiak tak? Huan kua kha ahia nang akipan hongpai khia?
ENGLISH: To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came forth from you?

PAITE: Sisate tuite nuai leh huaia tengte nuaiah a ling uh.
ENGLISH: “Those who are deceased tremble, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.

PAITE: A maah Seol vuaktangin a oma, huan Abaddon in kikhuhna a neikei hi.
ENGLISH: Sheol Sheol is the lower world or the grave. is naked before God, and Abaddon Abaddon means Destroyer. has no covering.

PAITE: Aman mal mun awng tungah a phalh khia a, huan bang mahlou tungah lei a khai hi.
ENGLISH: He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.

PAITE: A meipi sahin tuite a tuna; huan huaite nuaiah meipi a kikek kei hi.
ENGLISH: He binds up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not burst under them.

PAITE: Khapi mai a khuha, a tungah a meipi a phalh hi.
ENGLISH: He encloses the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud on it.

PAITE: Tuite tungah, khovak leh khomial kigitna ah, kawlmong a kaikual hi.
ENGLISH: He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of light and darkness.

PAITE: A salhna ah van khuamte a ling ua, lamdang a sa uh.
ENGLISH: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.

PAITE: A thilhihtheihnain tuipi a khawlsaka, huan a theihsiamna in Rahab a sat.
ENGLISH: He stirs up the sea with his power, and by his understanding he strikes through Rahab.

PAITE: A huin vante bawlhoihin a oma; a khutin gulpi man-gang tailai a sun hi.Ngaiin, hiaite a thilhih mong lel ahi uh. Ngatchika a huau siausiau lel! A thilhihtheihna Vanging kua ahia theisiam ding?
ENGLISH: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished. His hand has pierced the swift serpent.

PAITE: Ngaiin, hiaite a thilhih mong lel ahi uh. Ngatchika a huau siausiau lel! A thilhihtheihna Vanging kua ahia theisiam ding?
ENGLISH: Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?”

PAITE: Huchiin Jobin a gentehna thu apan nawna, huchiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Job again took up his parable, and said,

PAITE: Pathian a hing bangin, aman ka dikna a la manga; huan Thil bangkim hihtheiin, aman ka kha a hih buai a;
ENGLISH: “As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter.

PAITE: Ka hinna ka sunga a om laiteng, huan Pathian hu ka nakvanga a om laiteng?
ENGLISH: (For the length of my life is still in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils);

PAITE: Ka mukten thutaklou a gen kei ding, ka leiin leng khemna thu a gen kei ding.
ENGLISH: surely my lips shall not speak unrighteousness, neither shall my tongue utter deceit.

PAITE: Siam kon tansak mahmah kei ding hi: ka sihma tan ka takna kei akipanin ka koih mang kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me.

PAITE: Ka diktatna ka len chintena, ka khah kei ding hi: ka damlai teng ka lungtangin kei honkou kei ding.
ENGLISH: I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.

PAITE: Ka melma gilou bang hi henla, huan kei dou dia thou mi diktatlou bang hihen.
ENGLISH: “Let my enemy be as the wicked. Let him who rises up against me be as the unrighteous.

PAITE: Punna muta mahleh, Pathian limsakloumi lametna, Pathian in a kha a lak mang ngalin, bang ahia?
ENGLISH: For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

PAITE: A tunga buaina a tunin, a kikou Pathian in a za diam?
ENGLISH: Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?

PAITE: Thil bangkim hihthei ah nuam asa in, chiklaipeuhin Pathian sap nuam asa diam?
