ENGLISH: Will he delight himself in the Almighty, and call on God at all times?

PAITE: Pathian khut tungtangah nang ka honsinsak ding; Thil bangkim hihthei kianga om ken ka im kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: I will teach you about the hand of God. That which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.

PAITE: Ngai un, noute tengteng in huai na muta ua; ahihngalleh, bangdia bangmahlou honghi vek na hi ua?
ENGLISH: Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?

PAITE: Hiai Pathian laka mi gilou tantuan leh, nuaisiahhat mite goutan, Thil bangkim hihthei akipana a muh uh ahi.
ENGLISH: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty.

PAITE: A tate a pun uleh, nuamsau ading ahi; huan a suan tanghouin a tai kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword. His offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.

PAITE: A nunga omlaite hi lengin a vuidia, huan a meithaite un kahna a bawl kei ding uh.
ENGLISH: Those who remain of him shall be buried in death. His widows shall make no lamentation.

PAITE: Dangka leivui bangin vum touin, puansilh tungman bangin bawl mahleh;
ENGLISH: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;

PAITE: A bawl thei, himahleh mi dikten a silh ding, huan mi hoihten dangka pen a hawm ding hi.
ENGLISH: he may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.

PAITE: Inn a lam tuh maimom len bang ahia, vengmiin a bawl aidakbuk bang ahi.
ENGLISH: He builds his house as the moth, as a booth which the watchman makes.

PAITE: Hausa inn a luma, himahleh khopin a om kei ding; a mit a haka, huan a om kei.
ENGLISH: He lies down rich, but he shall not do so again. He opens his eyes, and he is not.

PAITE: Tuite bangin launaten amah a pha a; janin huihpiin amah a gu mang hi.
ENGLISH: Terrors overtake him like waters. A storm steals him away in the night.

PAITE: Suahlam huihin amah a po manga, huan a pai mang hi; huchiin a mun akipanin amah a mut mang hi
ENGLISH: The east wind carries him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place.

PAITE: Pathianin lah amah nakpiin a lawn dia, a dawm kei ding: a khut akipan taimang a ut ding.Miten amah a khut uh a bet khum ding ua, huan a mun akipanin amah a nuihsan khe ding uhi.
ENGLISH: For it hurls at him, and does not spare, as he flees away from his hand.

PAITE: Miten amah a khut uh a bet khum ding ua, huan a mun akipanin amah a nuihsan khe ding uhi.
ENGLISH: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

PAITE: Chihtaktakin dangka adingin khuk a oma, huan a hihsiang uh dangkaeng adingin mun.
ENGLISH: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.

PAITE: Lei akipanin sik a kilakhia a, huan suang akipanin dal a ki sungkhia hi.
ENGLISH: Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.

PAITE: Mihingin khomial phaktawp a neisaka, huan khomial sah leh thukah phaktawp gamlapen tanin sik-bua a zongkhia.
ENGLISH: Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.

PAITE: Mite om louhna ah kokhuk lutna hawm a tou vangua, mite apat gamla ah a kikhai ua, khatlam khatlamah a ki vei uh.
ENGLISH: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the foot. They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.

PAITE: Lei ahihleh, huai akipanin tanghou a hongsuaka: huan a nuaiah meia hihbangin a kilumlet hi.
ENGLISH: As for the earth, out of it comes bread; Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.

PAITE: Huailaia suangte saphir suang mun ahi a, huan dangkaeng nen a nei hi.
ENGLISH: Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.

PAITE: Huai lampi sasial ne vasain a theikei a, mu-akla mitin leng a mu ngei sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon’s eye seen it.

PAITE: Gamsa kisatheiten a sikkha ngeikei ua, humpinelkai lunlai leng huailaiah a paikha neikei hi.
ENGLISH: The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.

PAITE: Meisah suanpi tungah a khut a koiha; a zungin mualte a lumlet a lumlet hi.
ENGLISH: He puts forth his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots.

PAITE: Suangpite lakah lam a tou honga; huan a mitin thil mangpha chiteng a mu hi.
ENGLISH: He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.

PAITE: A takkhiak louhna ding un lui luangte a tuama; huan thilkisel khovak ah a honlakhia a.
ENGLISH: He binds the streams that they don’t trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings forth to light.

PAITE: Himahleh ko ilaiah a pilna a kimu dia? Huan theihsiamna mun koilaia om ahia?
ENGLISH: “But where shall wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?

PAITE: Mihingin a lampi a theikei hi; mihing gamah leng muhin a om kei hi.
ENGLISH: Man doesn’t know its price; Neither is it found in the land of the living.

PAITE: Tui thukin, Ka kiangah a omkei, a chi a.
ENGLISH: The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’

PAITE: Dangkaenga muh theih ahi keia, huai man dingin dangka leng buk theih ahi kei hi.
ENGLISH: It can’t be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for its price.

PAITE: Ophir dangkaeng toh a manphatna teh theih ahi kei ding, onik mantam hiam saphir toh hiam.
ENGLISH: It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire or, lapis lazuli .

PAITE: Dangkaeng leh limlangin a kimpih theikei ua: huai khenna dingin dangkaeng hoih suangmantam leng ahi theikei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.

PAITE: Suang dum hiam suang muhpaisuak theih a kigen kei ding: A hi, pilna man rubi suang sangin a sangjaw hi.
ENGLISH: No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.

PAITE: Ethiopia topazi suangin a pha kei dia, dangkaeng tak toh leng a manphatna teh ding ahi kei.
ENGLISH: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, Neither shall it be valued with pure gold.

PAITE: Ahihleh pilna koi akipana hongpai ahia? Huan theihsiamna mun koia om hia?
ENGLISH: Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?

PAITE: Mihing tengteng mit akipana sel ahi chih leh, huihkhua a vasate akipan sitsa a om ahi chih theiin.
ENGLISH: Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky.

PAITE: Siatna leh sihnain, huaia thuthang ka bil un ka ja uh, a chi ua.
ENGLISH: Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’

PAITE: Huaia lampi Pathianin a theisiam, huai amun a thei hi.
ENGLISH: “God understands its way, and he knows its place.

PAITE: Lei mong tanin a en ngala, huan van nuai thil tangtang a mu hi.
ENGLISH: For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole sky.

PAITE: Huiha dinga gikna a piak lain, leh tuite tehna a a teh laiin;
ENGLISH: He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure.

PAITE: Vuah adinga thupiak a bawla, vanging khophia adia lampi a bawl laiin;
ENGLISH: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder;

PAITE: Huailaiin aman a mua, a phuanga; ahih kipa, ahi, a zong khia hi.Huan mihing kiangah, Ngaiin, TOUPA kihtak, huai pilna ahi: huan hoihlou akipan pai mang theisiamna ahi, a chi hi.
ENGLISH: then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.

PAITE: Huan mihing kiangah, Ngaiin, TOUPA kihtak, huai pilna ahi: huan hoihlou akipan pai mang theisiamna ahi, a chi hi.
ENGLISH: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” , that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’”

PAITE: Huan Jobin a gentehna thu a gen nawna, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Job again took up his parable, and said,

PAITE: Aw nidanglai khate banga om hileng, Pathianin a honveh lai nite bangin;
ENGLISH: “Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me;

PAITE: Ka lu tunga a khawnvak a tana, amah vakna a khomiala ka vak lai;
ENGLISH: when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness,

PAITE: Ka hoihlai nitea ka om banga, ka puanin tunga a Pathian thuguk a om laiin;
ENGLISH: as I was in the ripeness of my days, when the friendship of God was in my tent,

PAITE: Ka kianga Thilbangkimhihthei a om laia, ka kima ka tate a om lai un;
ENGLISH: when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me,

PAITE: Ka kalsuante bawngnawia sawp a hiha, suangpiin sathau luipite a honbut khiaklaiin:
ENGLISH: when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,

PAITE: Khopia kongpi juana ka pai laiin, kongzinga ka tutna ka bawl laiin,
ENGLISH: when I went forth to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.

PAITE: Tangvalten a honmu ua, huan a bu ua: huan upate a thou ua a ding uh:
ENGLISH: The young men saw me and hid themselves. The aged rose up and stood.

PAITE: Lalte houlim a kidek ua, huan a kam uah a khut uh a koih uh:
ENGLISH: The princes refrained from talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.

PAITE: Miliante aw a daia, huan a lei uh a kam dangtawng uah a belh hi.
ENGLISH: The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.

PAITE: Bilin a honjak laiin, hampha a honchia; huan mitin a honmuh laiin, pom a honchia;
ENGLISH: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw me, it commended me:

PAITE: A kap mi genthei, amah panpih ding kuamah neilou, pa bei leng ka suahtaksak jiakin.
ENGLISH: Because I delivered the poor who cried, and the fatherless also, who had none to help him,

PAITE: Mangthang dinga mansa vualjawlna ka tungah a hongtunga: huan meithai lungtang kipah jiaka lasa dingin ka omsaka.
ENGLISH: the blessing of him who was ready to perish came on me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.

PAITE: Diktatna ka silha, huan a hontuam hi: ka dikna puannak thupi bang leh suangmantam bang ahi.
ENGLISH: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.

PAITE: Mittaw adingin mitte ka hi a, khebai adingin khete ka hi.
ENGLISH: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame.

PAITE: Tasam adingin pa ka hia: huan ka theihlouh thubul ka zong khia hi.
ENGLISH: I was a father to the needy. The cause of him who I didn’t know, I searched out.

PAITE: Diktatlou mi haijek ka hihtana, huan aha akipan a samat ka khahsak.
ENGLISH: I broke the jaws of the unrighteous, and plucked the prey out of his teeth.

PAITE: Huan ken, Ka bu ah ka si dinga, piaunel bangin ka nite ka pungsak ding, ka chi a:
ENGLISH: Then I said, ‘I shall die in my own house, I shall number my days as the sand.

PAITE: Ka zungte tuite phain a dalh jaka, huan ka hiangah jankhuain daitui a kai:
ENGLISH: My root is spread out to the waters. The dew lies all night on my branch.

PAITE: Kei ah ka thupina a thak gige a, huan ka khut ah ka thalpeu a thak gige.
ENGLISH: My glory is fresh in me. My bow is renewed in my hand.’

PAITE: Miten a honngai ua, a ngak ua, ka thuhilh adingin a dai dide uh.
ENGLISH: “Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.

PAITE: Ka thute zohin a pau nawn kei uh; huan ka thugen a tunguah a takkhia.
ENGLISH: After my words they didn’t speak again. My speech fell on them.

PAITE: Huan vuah ngak bangin a honngak ua; huan vuah nanungte ading bangin lianpiin a kamka uh.
ENGLISH: They waited for me as for the rain. Their mouths drank as with the spring rain.

PAITE: Kimuanna a neih louh chiangun a tunguah ka nuihmai a; huan ka mel tang a paikhe kei uh.A lampi ding uh ka telsaka, hausa bangin ka tua; sepaihpawl laka kumpipa bangin ka lenga, sunmite lungmuanmi bangin.
ENGLISH: I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They didn’t reject the light of my face.

PAITE: A lampi ding uh ka telsaka, hausa bangin ka tua; sepaihpawl laka kumpipa bangin ka lenga, sunmite lungmuanmi bangin.
ENGLISH: I chose out their way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.

PAITE: Hiai khitin Jobin a kam a kaa, a ni a hamsiat ta hi.
ENGLISH: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.

PAITE: Huan Jobin a dawnga hichiin a chi hi:
ENGLISH: Job answered:

PAITE: Ka pianna ni leh jan, Pasal naupang paiin a om, a kichihna mangthang hen.
ENGLISH: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’

PAITE: Huai ni mialna hihen; tunglam akipan Pathianin kah dah hen, a tungah leng khovak tang kei hen.
ENGLISH: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.

PAITE: Khomial leh sihna limin amau adingin huai ngen uhen; a tungah meipi kai hen; khua nimsak tengtengin huai tuh lausak uhen.
ENGLISH: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes black the day terrify it.

PAITE: Jan a hihleh, mial sah bikbek a tungah tu hen; kum nite lakah kipak kei hen; khate simna ah tel kei heh.
ENGLISH: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.

PAITE: Ngaiin, huai jan hut hen; huaiah kipah aw hong kei hen.
ENGLISH: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.

PAITE: Huai ni hamsiat amauten hamsiat uhen, leviathan tokthou dinga mansaa om te.
ENGLISH: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.

PAITE: Huaia khomui aksite mial uhen: khovak zong henla, himahleh bangmah neikei hen; jingsang mitvunte leng mu sam kei hen:
ENGLISH: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,

PAITE: Ka nu sul kongkhakte a khak louh jiakin, ka mit akipana buaina a sel louh jiakin.
ENGLISH: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.

PAITE: Sul akipana bang dia silou ka hia? gil akipan ka hongpai khiak laia bangdia kha khah lou kahia?
ENGLISH: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?

PAITE: Bangdia khukten kei honsang uh ahia? Ahihkeileh bangdia ka tep ding, nawiten?
ENGLISH: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?

PAITE: Tuchiangin na lum khina na dai mai ding lah ka hi ngala; ka na ihmuta dia; huchiin ka nakhawlta ding hi:
ENGLISH: For now should I have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,

PAITE: Lei kumpipate leh thudotmite, amau adinga mun siate bawlte toh;
ENGLISH: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;

PAITE: Ahihkeileh dangkaeng nei lalte, a inte uh dangkaa dimsakte toh;
ENGLISH: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver:

PAITE: Ahihkeileh muh louha a hunloua piang bang na hilou ka hia, naungek khovak mu ngeiloute bang?
ENGLISH: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.

PAITE: Huaiah mi gilouten sukbuai a tawpsan ua; huan huaiah mitawlte a khawl uh.
ENGLISH: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.

PAITE: Huai ah suangkulha tangte nuamin a om khawm uh; nasep heutu aw a za kei uh.
ENGLISH: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.

PAITE: Huaiah a lian leh a neu a om ua; huan a pu akipanin sikha a nuamlen.
ENGLISH: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.

PAITE: Bangdia daha om kianga khovak piak ahia, khaa haksa sa kiangah hinna;
ENGLISH: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,

PAITE: Sihna deiha, lah a tunlouhnate kiangah; huan gou sel guk zon sanga thupia zongmite kiang ah;
ENGLISH: Who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,

PAITE: Han a tun lai ua, nakpitaka kipakte kiang ah?
ENGLISH: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

PAITE: Bangdia mi a lampi sela om kiang leh Pathianin a umsuak kianga khovak piaka om ahia?
ENGLISH: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

PAITE: Ka thumna lah an ka nek main a hongtunga, ka maunate tui banga leihbuakin a om hi.
ENGLISH: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.

PAITE: Ka kihtak thil lah ka tungah a hongtung ngala, ka laulau lah ka tungah a hongtung hi.Nuam ka sa keia, muan leng ka muang kei, khawlna leng ka neikei hi; himahleh buaina a hongpai hi.
ENGLISH: For the thing which I fear comes on me, That which I am afraid of comes to me.

PAITE: Nuam ka sa keia, muan leng ka muang kei, khawlna leng ka neikei hi; himahleh buaina a hongpai hi.
ENGLISH: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; but trouble comes.”

PAITE: Himahleh kei sanga naupang, a pate uh ka ganching uite toh koih dia ka sitten, kei nuihzabawlna in a hon zang uh.
ENGLISH: “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to put with my sheep dogs.

PAITE: A hi, a khutte uh hata, huaiin kei bang a honlohtak dia, huai a hatna uh beisaten?
ENGLISH: Of what use is the strength of their hands to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?

PAITE: Taksapna leh kialna in a tuikang ua; lei keu leh sia a kheuh uh,
ENGLISH: They are gaunt from lack and famine. They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.

PAITE: Pawna annteh a lou ua; huan loukha zungte a an uh ahi.
ENGLISH: They pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom are their food.

PAITE: Mite lak akipan hawl khiakin a om ua; guta nung bangin amau nungah a kikou ua.
ENGLISH: They are driven out from the midst of men. They cry after them as after a thief;

PAITE: Guama hengte ah a teng ngei ding ua, lei leh suangpi hawmte ah.
ENGLISH: So that they dwell in frightful valleys, and in holes of the earth and of the rocks.

PAITE: Pawn lakah a ham ua; lahou nuaite ah a kise-khawm uh.
ENGLISH: Among the bushes they bray; and under the nettles they are gathered together.

PAITE: Mihaite tate ahi ua, ahi, mi thulimloute tate; gama kipanin delhkhiak ahi uh
ENGLISH: They are children of fools, yes, children of base men. They were flogged out of the land.

PAITE: Huan tuin kei a la uh ka honghia ahi, amaua dingin houlimna ka hi.
ENGLISH: “Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a byword to them.

PAITE: A honkih ua, kei akipan a tuam din uh, ka maia chil siat a kidek kei uh.
ENGLISH: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, and don’t hesitate to spit in my face.

PAITE: Pathianin lah Ka khau a khaha, a honhihgim hi, huan ka maah kamkaihna a khahkhia uh.
ENGLISH: For he has untied his cord, and afflicted me; and they have thrown off restraint before me.

PAITE: Ka khut taklam pangah mipi thuzohlouhte a thou ua; ka khe a a nawlkhin ua, huchiin a siatna lampi uh ka maah a koih uh.
ENGLISH: On my right hand rise the rabble. They thrust aside my feet, They cast up against me their ways of destruction.

PAITE: Ka lampi a hihsia ua, ka tuahsiatna a zong ua, kuaman a kham kei uh.
ENGLISH: They mar my path, They set forward my calamity, without anyone’s help.

PAITE: Awng zapia paisuak bangin a hong ua: siatna lakah ka tungah a kikhuk uh.
ENGLISH: As through a wide breach they come, in the midst of the ruin they roll themselves in.

PAITE: Launate ka tungah a hei ua, huih bangin ka minphatna a delhmang uh; huan meipi bangin ka hauhna a paimang hi.
ENGLISH: Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor as the wind. My welfare has passed away as a cloud.

PAITE: Huchiin tuin ka sungah ka kha buakkhiakin a om; gimthuakna niten kei a honman uh.
ENGLISH: “Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of affliction have taken hold on me.

PAITE: Janin ka guhte a sawi, huan kei honseuh natna ten khawl chih a neikei uh.
ENGLISH: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.

PAITE: Ka natna hi hat mahmahna jiakin ka puansilh a nina: ka puannak ngawng bangin kei a honggak hi.
ENGLISH: By great force is my garment disfigured. It binds me about as the collar of my coat.

PAITE: Buannawi ah a honpai luta, huan leivui leh meivu bang ka honghi hi.
ENGLISH: He has cast me into the mire. I have become like dust and ashes.

PAITE: Na kiangah ka kikoua, huan non dawng kei hi: Ka dinga, huan kei non en maimaha.
ENGLISH: I cry to you, and you do not answer me. I stand up, and you gaze at me.

PAITE: Ka tunga khel dingin na kilumleta: na ban hatnain kei non sawi hi.
ENGLISH: You have turned to be cruel to me. With the might of your hand you persecute me.

PAITE: Huihah non domkang tou a, huai tungah na hontuang sak; huan huih ah non lumlet let hi.
ENGLISH: You lift me up to the wind, and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.

PAITE: Sihna na hontun ding chih lah ka thei ngala, huan mihing tengteng adia sehsa in ah.
ENGLISH: For I know that you will bring me to death, To the house appointed for all living.

PAITE: Hitamahleh siatnaa pukgawp miin a ban jak lou ding hia? Ahihkeileh a tuahsiatna ah panpihna ngenin kikou lou ding hia?
ENGLISH: “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?

PAITE: Buainaa om adingin ka kap kei maw? Tasamte adingin ka kha a dah kei maw?
ENGLISH: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy?

PAITE: Hoih ka ngak chiangin, hoihlou a hongpaia; khovak ka ngak chiangin, khomial a hongpai.
ENGLISH: When I looked for good, then evil came; When I waited for light, there came darkness.

PAITE: Ka lungtang a buai, khawl a mu ngei kei; gimthuakna nite ka tungah a hongtung.
ENGLISH: My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest. Days of affliction have come on me.

PAITE: Hihvoma omin ka vialvak, himahleh ni hihvom hilou-in; khawmpi ah ka dinga panpih deihin ka kikou hi.
ENGLISH: I go mourning without the sun. I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.

PAITE: Sehalte unaupa ka hia, vakengsangte lawm ka hi hi.
ENGLISH: I am a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.

PAITE: Ka vun a voma, kei akipan a pilh uh, huan kholumin ka guhte a kang hi.Huaijiakin ka kaihging sunna a suaka, ka mutging mikapte aw.
ENGLISH: My skin grows black and peels from me. My bones are burned with heat.

PAITE: Huaijiakin ka kaihging sunna a suaka, ka mutging mikapte aw.
ENGLISH: Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of those who weep.

PAITE: Ka mit toh thukhun ka nabawlkhinta; bangchin nungak ka en theita dia oi?
ENGLISH: “I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?

PAITE: Ahihleh tunglam Pathian akipanin ka tantuan bang a hita dia, tungsang Thilbangkimhihthei akipanin ka goutan?
ENGLISH: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?

PAITE: Mi dikloute tungah tuahsiatna a tung kei mo, gitlouh nasemte tungah siatna?
ENGLISH: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity?

PAITE: Aman ka lampite a mukhin keiin, ka kalsuante a sim vek kei ahia?
ENGLISH: Doesn’t he see my ways, and number all my steps?

PAITE: Thujuau toh na oma, hua ka khe khem dinga nakinoh ahih leh;
ENGLISH: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit

PAITE: (Bukna diktak ah honbuk dih ua, Pathianin ka thutakna thei hen! )
ENGLISH: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);

PAITE: Ka kalsuan lampi akipan anapial hiam, ka lungtang-in ka mitte anajui hiam, huan ka khutte ah nin himhim anabelh hiam:
ENGLISH: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,

PAITE: Huchi anahihleh, chi tuh ning, midangin ne hen; ahi, ka loua piang bulkalh khiak hi hen.
ENGLISH: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.

PAITE: Ka lungtang numei lama khema anaoma, huan ka innveng kongkhaka ka nangaktak leh:
ENGLISH: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,

PAITE: Huchi anahihtak leh ka jiin midan adingin an su henla, huan midangte amah tungah kun uhen.
ENGLISH: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.

PAITE: Huchibang gitlouhna hoih hetlou lah ahi ngala; ahi, vaihawmmite gawt ding thulimlouhna ngei,
ENGLISH: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges:

PAITE: Siatna dinga kangbei leh, ka punna tengteng zungkalh ding mei hi ding lah ahi ngala.
ENGLISH: For it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.

PAITE: Ka tunga phunna a neihlai ua, ka sikhapa hiam ka sikhanu hiam makhua namusita, nakhualsak lou ka hih leh;
ENGLISH: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me;

PAITE: Pathian a thohkhiak chiangin bang ka hihta dia? Thu a kan hun chiangin bangin ka dawngta dia?
ENGLISH: What then shall I do when God rises up? When he visits, what shall I answer him?

PAITE: Kei sula honbawlpan amah a bawl kei mo? Huan khatin a honbawl tuak ahi kei mo?
ENGLISH: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?

PAITE: Migentheite a lunggulh uh ka napiak louha, ahihkeileh a vuaksuak dinga meithai mitte ka naomsak leh;
ENGLISH: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

PAITE: Ahihkeileh kei kiain ka an ka naneka, huaia pabeiin ananek kei leh;
ENGLISH: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it

PAITE: (Ii, ka tuailai akipanin pa bang ka hi, ka kiangah ana khanglianta; huan ka nu sul akipan amah pipa ka nahita hi: )
ENGLISH: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, her have I guided from my mother’s womb);

PAITE: Kuapeuh taksap jiaka mangthang hiam, ahihkeileh tasam khuhna neilou hiam ka namuh leh;
ENGLISH: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;

PAITE: A kawngten kei a honna vualjawl louha, ka belam mula lumsaka ana om kei leh;
ENGLISH: if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;

PAITE: Kongpia panpihna ka muh jiaka pabeite siatna dinga ka khut ka nalik leh;
ENGLISH: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate,

PAITE: Huchi anahihleh, ka liang ka liangjang akipan kia henla, a guh akipan ka ban kitan hen.
ENGLISH: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.

PAITE: Pathian akipan tuahsia lah keia dingin launa ahi ngala, A thupina lah ka tuak ngam ngal keia.
ENGLISH: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because his majesty, I can do nothing.

PAITE: Dangkaeng lametpena ka nabawla, dangkaeng hoih kiangah, ka muanna na hi, ka nachihtaka;
ENGLISH: “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’

PAITE: Ka hauhna thupi jiaka hiam, ka khutin tam a nalam jiaka ka nakipaha;
ENGLISH: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;

PAITE: A vak laia ni hiam, thupitaka pai pai kha hiam kana eta,
ENGLISH: if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,

PAITE: Huchia ka lungtang aguka khema a oma, ka kamin ka khut anatawptak aleh:
ENGLISH: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,

PAITE: Hiai leng thulimlouhna vaihawmmite gawt ding ahi: tunga Pathian kianga najuauta hi ding ka hih jiakin.
ENGLISH: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges; for I should have denied the God who is above.

PAITE: Kei honmudah siatnaa ka nakipaha, ahihkeileh hoihlou a tunga a tun chianga ka nakipah uat aleh;
ENGLISH: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him;

PAITE: (Ka melma hamsiat ding leh a henna thum dingin ka kam ka nakhialsak kei);
ENGLISH: (yes, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);

PAITE: Ka puaninaten, A ana kihihvah lou kua a oma, hon nachih kei ua leh;
ENGLISH: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’

PAITE: (Kongzing ah mikhual ana giak ngei kei; khualzin adingin ka kongte ka nahongta)
ENGLISH: (the foreigner has not lodged in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);

PAITE: Adam banga ka angsunga ka thulimlouhna na sela, ka tatlekna na khuh ka hiha,
ENGLISH: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,

PAITE: Ajiak, mi tampi launa thupitak ka neihjiak ahiha, sungte hon muhdaina launa jiak a huchia dai didea, popawt lou ka nahih leh-
ENGLISH: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—

PAITE: Aw, kei honja mi nei leng maw: (Ngaiin, hiaiah ka min gelh a om hi. Thil bangkim hihtheiin hondawng hen; ) huan ka galin a gelh khiat matna nei leng maw:
ENGLISH: oh that I had one to hear me! (behold, here is my signature, let the Almighty answer me); let the accuser write my indictment!

PAITE: Chihtaktakin ka liang jangah ka po dinga; lallukhu bangin kei ah ka kan den ding hi.
ENGLISH: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; and I would bind it to me as a crown.

PAITE: A kiangah ka kal suan zah ka phuang dinga; lal bangin ka kiang naiah ka hoh ding hi.
ENGLISH: I would declare to him the number of my steps. as a prince would I go near to him.

PAITE: Ka kam kei dema a kikoua, huaia lei lehsate a kah khawm uleh;
ENGLISH: If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;

PAITE: Sum loua huai gahte ka nanektaka, ahihkeileh huaia a neite a hinna uh ka natansak aleh:Buh hilouin loulingneite, barli-buh hilouin loubualte pou jaw hen.
ENGLISH: if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life,

PAITE: Buh hilouin loulingneite, barli-buh hilouin loubualte pou jaw hen.
ENGLISH: let briars grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.

PAITE: Huchibangin hiai mi thumte Job dawn a tawpta ua, amah mit a diktat a hih jiakin.
ENGLISH: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

PAITE: Huailaiin Buz mi Barakel tapa Elihu hehna a kuangkhia a, Ram innkuana mi: Job tungah a hehna kuangkhiaa, Pathian hizo loua amah siam a kitansak jiakin.
ENGLISH: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His wrath was kindled because he justified himself rather than God.

PAITE: A lawm thumte tungah leng a hehna a kuangkhiaa, dawnna ding neiloua, hinapia lah Job a mohpaih jiak un.
ENGLISH: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

PAITE: Amah sanga a upatjawk jiak uh, Job kianga thugen dingin Elihuin a ngak a.
ENGLISH: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were elder than he.

PAITE: Huan hiai mi thumte kama dawnna a om kei chih a theihin, a hehna a kuangkhia hi.
ENGLISH: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.

PAITE: Huchiin Buz mi Barakel tapa Elihuin a dawnga: Ka naupanga, huan nou na upa mahmah uh; huaijaikin ka daia, ka lungsim ka hon ensak ngam kei hi.
ENGLISH: Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, “I am young, and you are very old; Therefore I held back, and didn’t dare show you my opinion.

PAITE: Huchiin ka chi, Niten thu a gen ding uh, huan kum tampiin pilna a sinsak ding hi.
ENGLISH: I said, ‘Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.’

PAITE: Himahleh mihing lungsim a oma, huan Thilbangkimtheiin amaute theihsiamna a pia hi.
ENGLISH: But there is a spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.

PAITE: A pilte mi thupite ahi kei ua, vaihawmna theisiamte leng upate ahi sam kei uh.
ENGLISH: It is not the great who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice.

PAITE: Huaijiakin, hongngaikhia un; ken leng ka lungsim ka ensak ding, ka chi.
ENGLISH: Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me; I also will show my opinion.’

PAITE: Ngai un, na thute uh ka ngaka, gen ding na zon khiak lai un, na thusutte uh ka ngaikhia.
ENGLISH: “Behold, I waited for your words, and I listened for your reasoning, while you searched out what to say.

PAITE: Ahi, kon limsaka, huan, ngai un, kuamah Job thuzoh zou na om kei uh, ahihkeileh na lak uah, a thute dawng.
ENGLISH: Yes, I gave you my full attention, but there was no one who convinced Job, or who answered his words, among you.

PAITE: Pilna I muta, chi lou dingin pilvang un; mihing hilouin Pathianin amah a zou thei hi:
ENGLISH: Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom, God may refute him, not man;’

PAITE: Aman lah kei siatna dingin a thute ahihkeia; ken leng nou thugente in amah ka dawng sam kei ding.
ENGLISH: for he has not directed his words against me; neither will I answer him with your speeches.

PAITE: Lamdang asa ua, a dawng nawnta kei uh; gen ding thu khat leng a neikei uh.
ENGLISH: “They are amazed. They answer no more. They don’t have a word to say.

PAITE: Thu a genlouh jiak uh, a ding kinken ua, a dawn nawnlouh jiakin ka ngak diam?
ENGLISH: Shall I wait, because they don’t speak, because they stand still, and answer no more?

PAITE: Ken leng ka dawn ding ka dong hia, ka lungsim ka ensak sam ding hi.
ENGLISH: I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion.

PAITE: Thuin lah ka dim ngala; ka sunga khain a honsawl teitei hi.
ENGLISH: For I am full of words. The spirit within me constrains me.

PAITE: Ngai un, ka gilpi pawtkhiakna neilou uain bang ahi; khuainulhaite bangin puakjak dingin mansain a om hi.
ENGLISH: Behold, my breast is as wine which has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.

PAITE: Ka halh theihna dingin, ka pau ding; ka mukte ka hong dinga ka dawng ding hi.
ENGLISH: I will speak, that I may be refreshed. I will open my lips and answer.

PAITE: Mihing himhim mihinna honzahtaksak kei un, ka hon ngen hi; kuamah kiangah leng maitangphatna min ka pe ding hi.Maitangphatna minte piak ding ka thei ngal keia; huchilouinjaw kei a honla zok ding hi.
ENGLISH: Please don’t let me respect any man’s person, neither will I give flattering titles to any man.

PAITE: Maitangphatna minte piak ding ka thei ngal keia; huchilouinjaw kei a honla zok ding hi.
ENGLISH: For I don’t know how to give flattering titles; or else my Maker would soon take me away.

PAITE: Akoi abang hileh, Job, ka honngen hi, thugen ja inla ka thugen tengteng ngaikhiain.
ENGLISH: “However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.

PAITE: Ngaiin, tuni, ka kam ka kaa, ka kamin ka pau hi.
ENGLISH: See now, I have opened my mouth. My tongue has spoken in my mouth.

PAITE: Ka thuten ka lungtang dikna a genkhe ding uh; huan ka mukten a theih ngei uh chihtaktakin a gen ding uhi.
ENGLISH: My words shall utter the uprightness of my heart. That which my lips know they shall speak sincerely.

PAITE: Pathian Khain a honbawla huan Thil bangkim hihthei huin hinna a honpai hi.
ENGLISH: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

PAITE: Na theih leh, hondawng in; ka maah na thute a kizomzomin koihin, na panna ah ding in.
ENGLISH: If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand forth.

PAITE: Ngaiin, nang bangin Pathian lamah ka om hi: kei leng tungmana bawl ka hi.
ENGLISH: Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.

PAITE: Ngaiin, ka lauhuainain nang a honlausak kei ding, ka hahkatna leng na tungah a gik kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Behold, my terror shall not make you afraid, neither shall my pressure be heavy on you.

PAITE: Chihtaktakin ka jakin na pautaa, huan na thute ging ka zata hi.
ENGLISH: “Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of your words, saying,

PAITE: Ka siang hi, tatlekna bei; ka hoiha, kei ah thulimlouhna leng a om kei, chiin:
ENGLISH: ‘I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me.

PAITE: Ngaiin, kei demna ding a jiak a mua melmain a honsimta hi;
ENGLISH: Behold, he finds occasions against me. He counts me for his enemy.

PAITE: Ka khete kol a bunsaka, ka lampite tengteng achiamteh hi.
ENGLISH: He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.’

PAITE: Ngaiin, ka hondawng ding, hiai na diklouhna ah; mihing sangin lah Pathian a lianzo ngala.
ENGLISH: “Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.

PAITE: Bangdia amah dou na hia, Ka thute a bangmahmah lah a dawng kei ding, chiin?
ENGLISH: Why do you strive against him, because he doesn’t give account of any of his matters?

PAITE: Pathianin lah khatvei a gena, ahi, nihvei, mihingin limsak kei mahleh.
ENGLISH: For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.

PAITE: Jana mang ah, mengmuhna ah, mite tunga ihmut kip a kiak laiin, lupna tunga ihmut laite in;
ENGLISH: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed;

PAITE: Huailaiin mite bilte a honga, vaunatein amau a hihlaua,
ENGLISH: Then he opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction,

PAITE: Huchia a thiltup akipana mihing a lakkika, mihing a kipana kisaktheihna a satkhiak theihna dingin;
ENGLISH: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.

PAITE: Aman kokhuk akipan a kha a kep kik saka, namsaua kipan a hinna.
ENGLISH: He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

PAITE: A lupna tungah natnaa sawiin leng a om, huan a guhtea kinakna omgige tohin:
ENGLISH: He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones;

PAITE: Huchiin a hinnain tanghou a kiha, huan a khain an lim.
ENGLISH: So that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty food.

PAITE: Asa a tum manga, huchiin muh theihin a om kei; huan a kimulou a guhte hongdawk khia uh.
ENGLISH: His flesh is so consumed away, that it can’t be seen. His bones that were not seen stick out.

PAITE: A hi, a kha kokhuk kiangah a hong naia, huan a hinna hihsemite kiangah.
ENGLISH: Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.

PAITE: A kianga angel, kamlet, sang khat laka khat, mihing kianga amah adia dik bang ahia chih etsakding a om leh;
ENGLISH: “If there is beside him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man what is right for him;

PAITE: Huchia amah adinga chingtheia, Kokhuka pai sukna akipan amahsuaktasak un, tatna ka muta,
ENGLISH: then God is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.’

PAITE: A sa naupanga sangin nou jaw hen; a tuailai nite lamah kik nawnta hen, chi angel.
ENGLISH: His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s. He returns to the days of his youth.

PAITE: Pathian kiangah a thuma, huan amah dingin deihsak theihin a om hi; huchiin nuamna toh a mai a mua: huan a diktatna a kiangah a pe nawn hi.
ENGLISH: He prays to God, and he is favorable to him, so that he sees his face with joy. He restores to man his righteousness.

PAITE: Mite maah la asa a, Ka khialta a, a dik kana hekkawia thukin ka om kei!
ENGLISH: He sings before men, and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it didn’t profit me.

PAITE: Kokhuk sunga paisukna akipan ka kha a tanta a, huan ka hinna vakna a muta ding hi, achia.
ENGLISH: He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life shall see the light.’

PAITE: Ngaiin, hiai thilte tengteng Pathianin, mihing lak ah hihna, nihvei, ahi thumvei.
ENGLISH: “Behold, God works all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,

PAITE: Kokhuk akipan a kha pi kik dingin, huchia mihing vaknaa hihvaka a om theihna dingin.
ENGLISH: to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.

PAITE: Chiamteh hoihin, Aw Job, honngaikhia in: dai inla, thu ka gen ding.
ENGLISH: Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.

PAITE: Gending mahmah na neih leh, hon dawng in: Pau in, siam hontansak lah ka ut ngala.Na neih kei leh, kei honngaikhia in: dai inla pilna ka honsinsak ding hi.
ENGLISH: If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, for I desire to justify you.

PAITE: Na neih kei leh, kei honngaikhia in: dai inla pilna ka honsinsak ding hi.
ENGLISH: If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.”

PAITE: Huailouin Elihuin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Moreover Elihu answered,

PAITE: Ka thute ja un, nou mi pilte; nou theihna neite, bil hondoh un.
ENGLISH: “Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.

PAITE: Dangtawngin ann achiam bangin, bilin thute a enchain hi.
ENGLISH: For the ear tries words, as the palate tastes food.

PAITE: A dik eia dingin I tel ding uh; I lak ua hoih bang ahia I thei ding uh.
ENGLISH: Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.

PAITE: Job in lah, Ka dika, huan Pathianin ka dikna a la mang, a chi ngala:
ENGLISH: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, God has taken away my right:

PAITE: Ka dikna huchin hita mahleh juautheia sim ka hia; tatlekna bei himahleng, ka liamna hihdam theihlouh ahi.
ENGLISH: Notwithstanding my right I am considered a liar. My wound is incurable, though I am without disobedience.’

PAITE: Muhsitna tui banga dawn bei, Job bang mihing kua ahia?
ENGLISH: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,

PAITE: Thulimlou nasemmite toh a hona pai, mi giloute toh om khawmmi.
ENGLISH: Who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men?

PAITE: Aman lah, Pathian laka ka kipahna ding bangmah ka lohtak kei, a chi ngala.
ENGLISH: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’

PAITE: Huaijiakin, nou theisiammite, honngaikhia un: Pathianin, gilou bangchiin a hih ngei mahmah dia; huan Thilbangkimhihtheiin thulimlou bangchiin a hih mahmah dia.
ENGLISH: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

PAITE: Aman lah mihing thilhih amah kianga pe kik ding hi ngala, huan mi chiteng a lampite kianga pekik ding ahi.
ENGLISH: For the work of a man he will render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.

PAITE: A hi, mohkhuksakna thu ah, Pathianin giloutakin a hih kei dia, Thilbangkimhihtheiin leng vaihawmna a hihse sam kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.

PAITE: Kuan ahia amah leitunga heututna pia? Ahihkeileh khovel pumpi kuan ahia a thua koih?
ENGLISH: Who put him in charge of the earth? or who has appointed him over the whole world?

PAITE: Mihing tunga a lungtang a ngaka, amah lama a kha leh a hu a lakkhawm leh;
ENGLISH: If he set his heart on himself, If he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,

PAITE: Sa tengteng a mangthang khawm ding ua, huan mihing leivui a suak nawn ding hi.
ENGLISH: all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.

PAITE: Theihsiamna na neih leh, hiai ja in: ka thute aw ngaikhia in.
ENGLISH: “If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.

PAITE: Mi thudik huaiin vai a hawm ding hia? Huan dik leh hat amah na mohpaih ding hia?
ENGLISH: Shall even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty?—

PAITE: Kumpipa kianga, Na hoih kei chih a kilawm hia? Ahihkeileh miliante kianga, Na gilou uh? Chih.
ENGLISH: Who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?

PAITE: Mi lalte mi hinna zahtak loua, mi genthei sanga mi hausate limsak zote kianga chih kilawm sem lou ding hia? Amaute tengteng lah a khut nasep ahi ngal ua.
ENGLISH: Who doesn’t respect the persons of princes, nor respects the rich more than the poor; for they all are the work of his hands.

PAITE: Mitphiat kallouin a si ua jankim lai mahmahin; mite a ling ua a pai mang ua, mihingkhut hilouin mihatte lakmangin a om uhi.
ENGLISH: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.

PAITE: A mitte lah mihing lampite tungah a oma, huan a painate tengteng a mu hi.
ENGLISH: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.

PAITE: Thulimlou nasemmite buk theihna ding, khomial a omkei a, sihna limliap leng a om sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

PAITE: Vaihawmna a Pathian maa a pai dingin, mihing a ngaihtuah lailai a kiphamoh ngal keia.
ENGLISH: For he doesn’t need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.

PAITE: Lamte theihphak vual louhin aman mi hatte a hihjan veka, a mun uah midangte a tungkhia hi.
ENGLISH: He breaks in pieces mighty men in ways past finding out, and sets others in their place.

PAITE: Huaijiakin a nasepte uh a thei hi; janin amau a lumleta, huchiin hihsiatin a om uhi.
ENGLISH: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

PAITE: Midang mitmuh mahmahin mi giloute bangin amau a gawt hi.
ENGLISH: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

PAITE: Amah zuihna akipan a pialkhiak ua, a lampitea a koi mahmah a limsaklouh jiakun:
ENGLISH: because they turned aside from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways,

PAITE: Huchiin genthei kahna a kiang tung dingin a bawl ua, huan gimthuak kahna a ja hi.
ENGLISH: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.

PAITE: Amah napau kei leh, huchiin kuan siamlouh a tangsak dia? huan aman a mai a sel leh, huchiin amah kuan a mu thei dia? namte kianga hih hiam, ahihkeileh, mihing kianga hih hiam zong a kibang hi:
ENGLISH: When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? Alike whether to a nation, or to a man,

PAITE: Huchia pathiantheilou min vai a hawm louha, huchia mite thanga awksak ding kuamah a omlouhna dingin.
ENGLISH: that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.

PAITE: Kuapeuhin Pathian kiangah, Gawtna ka thuakta, ka gilou nawn kei ding,
ENGLISH: “For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.

PAITE: Ka muh louh nang honsinsak in: gilou ka hih aleh ka hih nawn kei ding, a chi uhia?
ENGLISH: Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?

PAITE: A thukna na deih bangin a om diam, huchia na nial? Kei hilouin, nang na tel ngeingei ding lah ahi ngala.
ENGLISH: Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.

PAITE: Theisiammiten ka kiangah, A hi, a chi ding uh, a honja mi pil chitengin,
ENGLISH: Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:

PAITE: Jobin theihna beiin thu a gena, huan a thute pilna bei ahi uh.
ENGLISH: ‘Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.’

PAITE: Mihaite banga a dawnna thu ah, a tawp chiangin Job tungtang ngaihtuah le uh.Aman lah a khelhna ah helna a behlapa, I lak uah a khut a benga, Pathian kalhin a thute a pungsakta ngala.
ENGLISH: I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.

PAITE: Aman lah a khelhna ah helna a behlapa, I lak uah a khut a benga, Pathian kalhin a thute a pungsakta ngala.
ENGLISH: For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.”

PAITE: Huailouin Elihuin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Moreover Elihu answered,

PAITE: Hiai na dikna hiin na ngaihtuah hia, ahihkeileh, keia mawng ahi, Pathian mai ah, na chi hia,
ENGLISH: “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’

PAITE: Kei adingin bang phattuamna a om dia? huan. Ka khelh nak sal aleh, bang phattuamna ka neia? na chih?
ENGLISH: That you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?’

PAITE: Nang, leh na kianga na lawmte ka hondawng ding.
ENGLISH: I will answer you, and your companions with you.

PAITE: Vante lam en inla, mu in; huan vante, nang sanga sangjaw, en in.
ENGLISH: Look to the heavens, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.

PAITE: Na hihkhelh leh, amah dema bang hih na hia? Huan na tatleknate punsak hileh, amah tunga bang hih na hia?
ENGLISH: If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?

PAITE: Daktat hi lechin, amah bang na pia a? Ahihkeileh na khut akipan bang a mu a?
ENGLISH: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?

PAITE: Na gitlouhnain mi bang bangin a hihna thei a; huan na diktatnain mihing tapa a hih hampha thei hi.
ENGLISH: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.

PAITE: Nuaisiahna tam mahmah jiakin a kikou khia ua; mi hat ban jiakin panpih deihin a kikou uh.
ENGLISH: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.

PAITE: Himahleh kuamahin, Jan chia late pia, Pathian kei Bawlpa koia om ahia;
ENGLISH: But none says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

PAITE: Leia gamsate sanga honsinsak tamjaw leh, vana vasate sanga hon pilsakjaw? A chi kei uh.
ENGLISH: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’

PAITE: Huailaiah a kikou ua, himahleh, mi gilou kisaktheihna jiakin, kuamahin dawnna a pe kei uh.
ENGLISH: There they cry, but none gives answer, because of the pride of evil men.

PAITE: Chihtaktakin Pathianin bangmahlou aza kei dia, Thil bangkim hihtheiin leng a limsak sak kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.

PAITE: Nang ngial houh: Amah ka mu kei, a thu maah a om, amah ka ngak hi, na chih vial.
ENGLISH: How much less when you say you don’t see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!

PAITE: Himahleh tuin, heha a veh louha, kiotsakna leng a limsaklouin jiakin;Huaijiakin Jobin bangmahlouin a kam a ka ahi; theihna beiin thu a tamsak ahi.
ENGLISH: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance.

PAITE: Huaijiakin Jobin bangmahlouin a kam a ka ahi; theihna beiin thu a tamsak ahi.
ENGLISH: Therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”

PAITE: Elihu mahin a gen jela, huchiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Elihu also continued, and said,

PAITE: Honna thuakzou zek inla, huan ka hon ensak ding; Pathian sikin lah banghiam khat gending ka nei ngala.
ENGLISH: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.

PAITE: Gamla akipan ka theihna kon la dinga, huan diktatna kei Bawlpa tungah ka nga ding hi.
ENGLISH: I will get my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

PAITE: Diktakin ka thute lah juau ahi ngal keia: hoihkim khat lah ka kiangah a om hi.
ENGLISH: For truly my words are not false. One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.

PAITE: Ngaiin, Pathianin thil a hihtheia, kuamah a musit kei: theihsiamna hatna ah thil a hihthei hi.
ENGLISH: “Behold, God is mighty, and doesn’t despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.

PAITE: Gilou hinna a hawi keia: himahleh gimthuakte kiangah a dikna uh a pia hi.
ENGLISH: He doesn’t preserve the life of the wicked, but gives to the afflicted their right.

PAITE: Mi diktat akipan a mit a la kik keia: himahleh laltutphah tunga kumpipa toh amau khantawnin a koiha, huchiin hihletin a om uhi.
ENGLISH: He doesn’t withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets them forever, and they are exalted.

PAITE: Huan sikkhautea gaka a om ua, gimthuakna guitea laka a om uleh;
ENGLISH: If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,

PAITE: Huchiin a thilhih uh amau a ensaka, huan a tatlekna uh, huchia kisatheitaka a na omna uh.
ENGLISH: then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.

PAITE: Thuhilhna lamah a bil uh leng a honsaka, thulimlouhna akipan kik dingin thu a pia hi.
ENGLISH: He also opens their ears to instruction, and commands that they return from iniquity.

PAITE: Amah thu a ngaihkhiak ua, a na a sep uh leh, a nite uh hausaknain a hihbei ding ua, a kumte uh kipahnain.
ENGLISH: If they listen and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

PAITE: Himahleh a ngaihkhiak kei ua leh, namsauin a mangthang ding ua, huan theihna beiin a si ding uh.
ENGLISH: But if they don’t listen, they shall perish by the sword; they shall die without knowledge.

PAITE: Himahleh amau lungtanga pathianilimsaklouhnaten hehna a khol khawm uhi: amau a hen laiin panpih deihin a kikou kei uh.
ENGLISH: “But those who are godless in heart lay up anger. They don’t cry for help when he binds them.

PAITE: Tuailaiin a si ua, siangloute lakah a hinna uh a mangthang hi.
ENGLISH: They die in youth. Their life perishes among the unclean.

PAITE: A gimthuaknain gimthuakte a suaktasaka, nuaisiah na ah a bil uh a honsak hi.
ENGLISH: He delivers the afflicted by their affliction, and opens their ear in oppression.

PAITE: A hi, gakchihna om louhna mun, mun lian lamah dahna akipan nang a honpi mang ta ding a; huan na donkan tunga kilui thaunain a dimta ding hi.
ENGLISH: Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a broad place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.

PAITE: Himahleh giloute vaihawmnain na dima: vaihawmna leh diktatnain nang nang a honlen hi.
ENGLISH: “But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.

PAITE: Thangpaihna a om jiakin, pilvangin huchilouin jaw na kichinnain nang a honpi mangkha ding hi; tatna letnain leng nang honpialsak sam kei hen.
ENGLISH: Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.

PAITE: Dahna a na om louhna dingin, na hauhsaknate a hun diam, ahihkeileh na hatna thilhihtheihna tengteng?
ENGLISH: Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?

PAITE: Mite tengteng a mun ua sat khiaka a om lai un, jan deih ken.
ENGLISH: Don’t desire the night, when people are cut off in their place.

PAITE: Pilvangin, gilou limsak ken: gimthuakna sangin hiai lah na telta ngala.
ENGLISH: Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.

PAITE: Ngaiin, Pathianin a thilhihtheihnain sangtakin a hih: amah bang sinsakmi kua ahia?
ENGLISH: Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?

PAITE: Kuan amah a lampi thu a piaa? ahihkeileh, kuan, Diklouhna na bawlta, a chi thei dia?
ENGLISH: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness?’

PAITE: Miten la a asak uh, a thilhih hihlian dingin theigige in.
ENGLISH: “Remember that you magnify his work, whereof men have sung.

PAITE: Huaiah mite tengteng a en ua; huai mihing in gamla pi ah a mu hi.
ENGLISH: All men have looked thereon. Man sees it afar off.

PAITE: Ngaiin, Pathian a liana, amah I theikei uh: a kumte zah zontheih ahi kei.
ENGLISH: Behold, God is great, and we don’t know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.

PAITE: Tui takte aman a tawi khin ngala, huai a tuihu akipan vuah a ju:
ENGLISH: For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,

PAITE: Huai vanten a sungkhe suk ua, tampipiin mihing tungah a tak.
ENGLISH: Which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.

PAITE: A hi, meipi kiphahte, a in vanpigingte kuamahmahin a theisiam dia?
ENGLISH: Yes, can any understand the spreading of the clouds, and the thunderings of his pavilion?

PAITE: Ngaiin, a kimah a khovak a jaka: huan tuipi nuai a tuam hi.
ENGLISH: Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.

PAITE: Hiaitein lah mite a vaihawmsak ngala; an tampi a pia hi.
ENGLISH: For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.

PAITE: Khophiain a khutte a tuama; huan chiamtehna khoh dingin thu a pia hi.Huai husain a tungtang thu a gena, ganhonten leng hongkuan tou huihpi tungtang thu.
ENGLISH: He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.

PAITE: Huai husain a tungtang thu a gena, ganhonten leng hongkuan tou huihpi tungtang thu.
ENGLISH: Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also concerning the storm that comes up.

PAITE: Hiaiah leng ka lungtang a linga, a mun akipan suanin a om hi.
ENGLISH: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.

PAITE: A awging leh a kam akipana ging paikhia nouten ngaikhia un.
ENGLISH: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.

PAITE: Van pumpi nuaiah huai tuh a sawlkhiaa, huan a khophia lei tawpnate tannin.
ENGLISH: He sends it forth under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.

PAITE: Huai zohin aw a kikoua; a lalna awin vanpi a gingsaka: huan a aw jaka a om chiangin amau a len kei.
ENGLISH: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.

PAITE: Pathianin a awin lamdangtakin vanpi a gingsaka; I theih theihlouh, thil thupite a hih jel hi.
ENGLISH: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.

PAITE: Aman lah vuk kiangah, Lei ah kiain, a chi ngala; huchi mahbangin vuah malphin kiangah leng.
ENGLISH: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth;’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.

PAITE: Mi chiteng khut a tuambita; huchia a bawlsa mite tengtengin huai a theihtheihna ding un.
ENGLISH: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.

PAITE: Huailaiin gamsate a mun uah a lut ua, huan a kuate uah a om nilouh uh.
ENGLISH: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.

PAITE: Simlam dantan akipan huihpi a honga: mallam akipan khovot.
ENGLISH: Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.

PAITE: Pathian huin tuikhal piak ahi: huan tuite nakna hihhaksatin a om.
ENGLISH: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the breadth of the waters is frozen.

PAITE: A hi, meipi nawnna a posaka; a khophia meipi a phalhsak hi:
ENGLISH: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.

PAITE: Huan amah piin a kivial heihei ua, tentheihna khovel maikaih tunga amaute thu a piak peuhmah a hihna ding un: S
ENGLISH: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,

PAITE: Bawlhoihna ding hiam, a gam ading hiam, ahihkeileh chitna ding hiama, a hon paisakna ah.
ENGLISH: Whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.

PAITE: Hiai ngaikhiain, Aw Job: Ding kinken inla, Pathian thilhih lamdangte ngaihtuah in.
ENGLISH: “Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

PAITE: Amaute tunga Pathianin a thupiak a koiha, a meipi khophia a tansak dan na thei hia?
ENGLISH: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?

PAITE: Meipite kibukdiknate, amah theihna hoihkim thilhih lamdangte na thei hia?
ENGLISH: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?

PAITE: Sim huih jiaka lei a daih sisip laia, na puansilhte a lum dan?
ENGLISH: You whose clothing is warm, when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?

PAITE: Amah toh van, suntawm limlang banga khauh, na phalh thei hia?
ENGLISH: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?

PAITE: A kianga ka gen ding uh hon sinsak in; mialna jiakin lah ka thugen ding uh ka gelkhol theikei ua.
ENGLISH: Teach us what we shall tell him, for we can’t make our case by reason of darkness.

PAITE: Thu ka gen ding chih amah hilh ding a diam? ahihkeileh mihingin valh khita om ut ding a diam?
ENGLISH: Shall it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?

PAITE: Huchiin miten vantea om vak khovak a mu kei ua: himahleh huih a nunga, amaute a hihsiang hi.
ENGLISH: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.

PAITE: Mal akipanin dangkaenga thupi a hongpaia: Pathianin lalna kihtakhuai a tungah a nei hi.
ENGLISH: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.

PAITE: Thil bangkim hihthei thu ahihleh, mu theikei hang: thilhihtheihna ah a thupi pet mah hi: Huan vaihawmna leh dikna hauhna ah gim a thuaksak kei ding hi.Huaijiakin miten amah a lau ua: lungtanga pil kuamahmah a limsak kei hi.
ENGLISH: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.

PAITE: Huaijiakin miten amah a lau ua: lungtanga pil kuamahmah a limsak kei hi.
ENGLISH: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”

PAITE: Huchiin pingpei akipanin TOUPAN job a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,

PAITE: Theihna bei thutea thuhilh hihmial hiai kua ahia?
ENGLISH: “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?

PAITE: Kipasalsakin tuin na kawng gakin; Hondong ding ka hi, ka kianga na gen ding ahi.
ENGLISH: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!

PAITE: Lei kingaknate ka koih laiin nang koiah na oma? Phuangin, theihsiamna nei na hih leh.
ENGLISH: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.

PAITE: Huaia tehnate kua bawl ahi, thei na hih leh! ahihkeileh a tunga tehna khau kua zan ahia?
ENGLISH: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?

PAITE: A nuai suangphumte kua phum ahia, ahihkeileh huai a ninga suang kua koih ahia;
ENGLISH: Whereupon were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone,

PAITE: Jingsang aksiten la a sak khawm ua, Pathian tapate tengteng kipah jiaka a kikou lai un?
ENGLISH: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

PAITE: Ahihkeileh kuan kongkhaktein tuipite a khak binga, gil akipan hongpawt khia banga, a hongpuahkhiak laiin.
ENGLISH: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth from the womb,

PAITE: Huaia puansilh meipi leh, khomial bikbek, huaia dinga tuamna puan ka bawla,
ENGLISH: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,

PAITE: Huaia dinga ka thupiak bawla, kalhnate leh kongkhakte koiha,
ENGLISH: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,

PAITE: Hiaitan na hongpai ding, himahleh a ban hilouin, ka chiha; huan hiailaiah a kiuangsak na tuikihotte lettangin a om ding uh, ka chih laiin?
ENGLISH: and said, ‘Here you may come, but no further. Here your proud waves shall be stayed?’

PAITE: Na nite a kipat nungsiah jingsang thu na piain, phalvak a mun thei dingin na bawlta hia;
ENGLISH: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place;

PAITE: Huchia lei tawpnate a mat theiha, huai akipana gilou sinkhiak a hihtheihna dingin?
ENGLISH: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?

PAITE: Chiamtehna nuaia tungmanlei bangin mel a kikhenga; huan puansilh bangin thil tengteng ze neiin a dingkhia hi:
ENGLISH: It is changed as clay under the seal, and stands forth as a garment.

PAITE: Huan gilou akipana a khovak uh lettang sak ahia, a ban liksang uh a kitan hi.
ENGLISH: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.

PAITE: Tuipi nakte sungah na lut ta hia? Ahihkeileh tuithuk tawpna ah na paita hia?
ENGLISH: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?

ENGLISH: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?

PAITE: Lei zatdan na thei siamte hia? Phuang in, huai na theih vek leh.
ENGLISH: Have you comprehended the earth in its breadth? Declare, if you know it all.

PAITE: Khovak tenna zotna lampi koiah a oma, huan khomial omna mun koisan ahia;
ENGLISH: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,

ENGLISH: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?

PAITE: Thei mah niteh maw, huailaia piangta lah hi ding china? Hhuan na nite tamdan lah thupi mahmah hi dia!
ENGLISH: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!

PAITE: Vuk koihkhawmna ah na lut ngeita hia, ahihkeileh gial koihkawm na muta hia.
ENGLISH: Have you entered the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasures of the hail,

ENGLISH: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

PAITE: Bang lampi ah ahia khovak a kikhen a, ahihkeileh leitunga suahlam huih a dalhjak?
ENGLISH: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?

PAITE: Kuan ahia tui tampi luanna dinga tuilam khuak, ahihkeileh kekkia adia lampi;
ENGLISH: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm;

PAITE: Mihing om louhna mun gam tunga vuah zusak dingin; mihing om louhna, gamdai tungah;
ENGLISH: To cause it to rain on a land where no man is; on the wilderness, in which there is no man;

PAITE: Lei kisia leh segawpsa lungkimsak ding; loupa hing nou khangkhesak ding?
ENGLISH: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to spring forth?

PAITE: Vuahin pa a nei hia? Ahihkeileh daitui takte kua suan ahia?
ENGLISH: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?

PAITE: Kua gil akipana tuikhal hongpai ahia? Huan van daituikhal ngou, kua suahsak ahia?
ENGLISH: Out of whose womb came the ice? The gray frost of the sky, who has given birth to it?

PAITE: Suang bangin tuite a taka, tuithuk maite a khal hi.
ENGLISH: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.

PAITE: Siguk khaute na khihkhawm thei hia, ahihkeileh zuheisuktun khaute na phel thei hia?
ENGLISH: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?

ENGLISH: Can you lead forth the constellations in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?

PAITE: Van thusehte na thei hia? Huai lalna lei ah na dingkhesak thei diam?
ENGLISH: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?

PAITE: Nang tui tampiin a khuh theihna dingin meipite kiangah na aw na suahkhe thei diam?
ENGLISH: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover you?

PAITE: A pai theihna ding un khophiate na sawl khe thei hia?
ENGLISH: Can you send forth lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are?’

PAITE: Sunggil lamah pilna kuan a koiha? Ahihkeileh lungsim kiangah kuan theihsiamna a pia a?
ENGLISH: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?

PAITE: Pilnain kuan meipite a sim thei dia? Ahihkeileh kuan van tuithawlte a bo khe thei dia.
ENGLISH: Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of the sky,

PAITE: A lompia leivui a luana, a sakte a kimat khawm ngiungeu lai un?
ENGLISH: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?

PAITE: Humpinelkai adingin samat na betsak ding hia? Ahihkeileh humpinelkai noute gilkial na hihdam ding hia?
ENGLISH: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,

PAITE: A kua ua a boh ua, buk dinga a bukna mun ua a om nilouh lai un?Vaak ading a an kuan a pia a? A noute Pathian kianga kikou a ann duh mana a vakvak lai un?
ENGLISH: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?

PAITE: Vaak ading a an kuan a pia a? A noute Pathian kianga kikou a ann duh mana a vakvak lai un?
ENGLISH: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?

PAITE: Suangpia gam sathakten a suahsak hun uh na thei hia? ahihkeileh nou a neih lai uh na chiamteh thei hia?
ENGLISH: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

PAITE: A chinsak zah khate na sim thei hia? Ahihkeileh a suahsak hun na thei hia?
ENGLISH: Can you number the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?

PAITE: A kun ua, a tate uh a suang uh, a lungkhamnate uh a pai khia uhi.
ENGLISH: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young, they end their labor pains.

PAITE: A tate uh deihhuai takin a om ua, gamlak ah a khang lian ua; a kuankhia ua, a hongkik nawn kei uh.
ENGLISH: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go forth, and don’t return again.

PAITE: Kuan gam sabengtung a khah khiaa? Ahihkeileh kuan gam sabengtung honte a phel a?
ENGLISH: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,

PAITE: Loupa gam a inin ka bawla, huan chi gam a tenna munin;
ENGLISH: Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?

PAITE: Khopi buai nuanua a musita, hawlmi kikounate leng a za sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.

PAITE: Mual dungte a gantatna mun ahia, huan thilhing chiteng a zong hi.
ENGLISH: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.

PAITE: Na na sem gingin gam bawngtal a lungkim diam? Ahihkeileh na anpiakna kiangah a omgige diam?
ENGLISH: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?

PAITE: Leilehna ah khauin gam bawngtal na khih thei diam? Ahihkeileh na nungah guamte a toktam diam?
ENGLISH: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?

PAITE: A hatna a thupi jiakin, amah na muang diam? Ahihkeileh a kiangah na sepgimna na khiat diam?
ENGLISH: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?

PAITE: Na chi in a hontuta, na buhphuala buh a kaihkhawm theihna dingin amah na muang diam?
ENGLISH: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?

PAITE: Ostrik-va kha kisathei takin a kijapa; himahleh a khavengte leh a multe a migi hia?
ENGLISH: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?

PAITE: A tuite lah leitungah a nusiaa, leivui ah a lumsaka,
ENGLISH: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,

PAITE: Khein a sikkham thei chih a mangngilha, ahihkeileh gamsain a sikgawp thei chih.
ENGLISH: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.

PAITE: Amaha hi lou bangin, a noute siatna dingin a khauha: a sep gimna bangmahlou hita zongleh, a lau kei hi:
ENGLISH: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,

PAITE: Pathian in pilna a ngolhsak jiakin, theihsiamna leng a pe sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.

PAITE: Tungsang lama a kitawi sang chiangin, sakol leh a tungtuangmi a nuihsan.
ENGLISH: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.

PAITE: Sakol a hatna na piak hia? Mul nemin a ngawng na tuam hia?
ENGLISH: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?

PAITE: Khaukhup bangin na tawmsak hia? A hamna thupi a lauhuai ve.
ENGLISH: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.

PAITE: Guam ah lei a tuana, a hatna ah a kipaka: mi kigalvante tuak dingin a pai khia.
ENGLISH: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.

PAITE: Lauhuai a nuihsana, a lungdong keia; namsau leng a nungngat sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.

PAITE: Amah ah thalbawm a ging lenglenga, teipi tezelzel leh chiangzum.
ENGLISH: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.

PAITE: Kihtakhuaina leh hehnain lei a nawmvalha; Pengkul aw ahi chih leng a um sam kei hi.
ENGLISH: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.

PAITE: Pengkul a gin tengin, Hah; a chi a, huan kidouna, heutute vanpiging leh kikou, gamlapi apan a thei.
ENGLISH: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

PAITE: Na pilnain mu sangpi a lengsakin, a khate simlamah a phalh hia?
ENGLISH: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?

PAITE: Nang thupiakin muvanlai a tunglen in, tungsang ah a bu a sep hia?
ENGLISH: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?

PAITE: Suangpi tungah a tenga, huailaiah giahna a neia, suangpi hengte ah leh kulh muanhuaite ah.
ENGLISH: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.

PAITE: Huai akipanin matding a mu a; a miten gamla ah a mu hi.A nouten leng sisan a tep bei ua: huan thah omna mun ah, huailaiah a om hi.
ENGLISH: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.

PAITE: A nouten leng sisan a tep bei ua: huan thah omna mun ah, huailaiah a om hi.
ENGLISH: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”

PAITE: Huchihlaiin Elipha Teman miin a dawnga, hichiin a chi hi:
ENGLISH: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

PAITE: Min nang honhoulim pih tum leh na zadah diam? Hizongleh pau louin kua a om thei dia?
ENGLISH: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?

PAITE: Ngaiin, mi tampi na hilhtaa, huan khut hatloute na hihhatta hi.
ENGLISH: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.

PAITE: A puklai mah na thuten a dingsaka, khuk hatloute na kipsak hi.
ENGLISH: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.

PAITE: Himahleh tuin na tungah a hongtunga, na baha; nang a honkhoiha, na buaita.
ENGLISH: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

PAITE: Pathian an kihtakna na muanna hi lou hia, na lametna na lampite muanhuaina?
ENGLISH: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?

PAITE: Theigigein, ka honngen hi, hoih hina pia, mangthang ngei kua ahia? ahihkeileh koilaiah ahia midik satkhiaka om?
ENGLISH: “Remember, now, whoever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?

ENGLISH: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity, and sow trouble, reap the same.

PAITE: Pathian huin a mangthang ua, huan a hehna mutin himanin a om uhi.
ENGLISH: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.

PAITE: Humpinelkai huham leh, humpinelkai hangsan aw leh, humpinelkai tuailai hate, a kitan ta.
ENGLISH: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

PAITE: Samat taksap jiakin humpinelkai tek a mangthanga, huan humpinelkai noute a dalhjak ua.
ENGLISH: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.

PAITE: Tuin a gukin thil ka kiang a hongtunga, ka bilin huaia huauna a sangta hi.
ENGLISH: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.

PAITE: Jan mengmuhna akipana ngaihtuahnate ah, mite nakpi taka a ihmut san lai un,
ENGLISH: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

PAITE: Huailaiin ka mai maah kha a paia; ka chimul a ding ta hi.
ENGLISH: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.

PAITE: Ka ding kinkena, himahleh huaia a kilatdan ka theikak theita keia; a lim tuh ka mit maah a oma; daihna a oma, huan aw ka jaa,

PAITE: Pathian sangin sithei mihing a dik zo ding hia? A Bawlpa sangin mihing siangthou zo ding hia? chiin.
ENGLISH: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

PAITE: Ngaiin, a sikhate ah muanna akoih keia; huan a angelte haiin a ngoh hi:
ENGLISH: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.

PAITE: Tungman ina teng amaute hi diak na un chia, a suangphum leivuia oma, leikha maa chimsia:
ENGLISH: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!

PAITE: Jingsang leh nitak kikalin hihsiatin a om ua: theihlouh hialin khantawnin a mangthang uhi.Amau sunga a puanin-khau uh bohkhiak touh hi lou hia? a si ua, huan pilna tel louin.
ENGLISH: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.

PAITE: Huailouin Toupan Job a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:

PAITE: Huan Jobin Toupa a dawnga, hichiin a chi a.:

PAITE: Ngaiin, Bangmah ka hi keia; bang ka hon dawng dia? Ka kam ah ka khut ka koih.
ENGLISH: “Behold, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.

PAITE: Khatvei ka pauta a, ka dawng kei ding; ahi nihvei, himahleh ka pau nawn kei ding.
ENGLISH: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”

PAITE: Huchiin Toupan Job pingpei akipanin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:

ENGLISH: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?

ENGLISH: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?

PAITE: Tuin nang hoihkim leh zahnain kijem in; zahna leh lalnain kivan in.

ENGLISH: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap forth.

PAITE: A huin suang a kuangsaka, a kam akipanin meikuang a pawt khia hi.
ENGLISH: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes forth from his mouth.

PAITE: A ngawng ah hatna a om gigea, a maah lauhuaina a lam hi.
