PAITE: Asa thate a kizom khawm ua: a tungah a kip ua; hihtat theihin a om kei uh.
ENGLISH: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.

PAITE: A lungtang suang bangin a kip a; ahi, buhgawina suang nuainungjaw bang ahi.
ENGLISH: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.

PAITE: Amah a thoh chiangin, mihatte a lau uh: lauluatna jiakin omdan ding a theikei uh.
ENGLISH: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.

PAITE: Min amah namsauin sat leh, a phatuam kei hi; teipi leng, thal leng, sikmuk zum leng.
ENGLISH: If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.

PAITE: Buhpawl bangin sik a sima, sing muatsa bangin dal.
ENGLISH: He counts iron as straw; and brass as rotten wood.

PAITE: Thalin amah a taisak theikei ding: amah lakah vaisuanglot suangte buhpawl a suak hi.
ENGLISH: The arrow can’t make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.

PAITE: Khetbukte buhpawl banga sim ahi: chiangzuma khohte a nuihsan hi.
ENGLISH: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.

PAITE: A nuai lampangte belpei hiam ahi: buannawi tungah buh khetna chiang bangin a kiphah.
ENGLISH: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.

PAITE: Tuithuk bel banga sou dingin a bawla: tuipi nuhtheih bawm bangin a bawl hi.
ENGLISH: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.

PAITE: A nungah lampi a vangsaka; tuithuk samkang min a sa ding hi.
ENGLISH: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.

PAITE: Lei tungah amah bang a om keia, lau loua bawl.A sang peuh thil chiteng a ena: kisathei tapate tengteng tungah kumpipa ahi.
ENGLISH: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.

PAITE: A sang peuh thil chiteng a ena: kisathei tapate tengteng tungah kumpipa ahi.
ENGLISH: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”

PAITE: Huchiin Jobin TOUPA a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered Yahweh,

PAITE: Thil bangkim na hih thei chih leh nang thiltup kham theih ahi kei chih ka thei hi.
ENGLISH: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.

PAITE: Hiai thuhilhna theihna telloua sel kua ahia? Huaijiakin ka theihsiamlouh ka na genkhiaa, ka theih louh, kei adia lamdang lua thilte.
ENGLISH: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ therefore I have uttered that which I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.

PAITE: Ja in, ka honngen hi, huan ka pau ding; nang ka hon phut ding, kei lamah nang phuangin, nonchia.
ENGLISH: You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’

PAITE: Ka bil jaknain nang ka honjaa; himahleh tuin ka mitin nang a mu a,
ENGLISH: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.

PAITE: Huaijiakin ka kikiha, leivui leh meivu ah ka kisik hi.
ENGLISH: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

PAITE: Huan hichi ahia, huchia TOUPAN Job kianga hiai thute a gen khitin, TOUPAN Elipha Teman mi kiangah, Ka hehna nang tung leh, na lawm nihte tungah a kuang ka sikha Job banga nouten ka tanchiin thildik na gen louh jiak un, a chi a.
ENGLISH: It was so, that after Yahweh had spoken these words to Job, Yahweh said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.

PAITE: Huaijiakin tuin, bawngtal sagih leh belamtal sagih la unla ka sikha Job kiangah hoh unla, noua dingin halmang thillat lan un; huchiin ka sikha Job nou adingin a thum dinga; amah vangin ka sang dia, huchiin na haina uh dungjuiin na tunguah ka hih kei ding; ka sikha Job bangin lah ka tanchin thildik na gen ngal kei ua, chiin.
ENGLISH: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”

PAITE: Huchiin Elipha Teman mi leh Bildan Sua mi leh Zophar Naaman mi a kuanta ua, amau TOUPAN thu a piak bangin a hihta uhi: huan TOUPAN Job a sangta hi.
ENGLISH: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.

PAITE: Huan TOUPAN Job koltanna, a lawmte adia thu a nget laiin a heita a: huchiin TOUPAN Job a maa a neih zahnih a peta hi.
ENGLISH: Yahweh turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before.

PAITE: Huailaiin a kiangah, a unaute tengteng leh, a sanggamnute tengteng leh, tumalama a meltheihte hisa tengteng leh, a in sunga tanghou amah toh nete a hongpai ua: amah a nem ua, a tunga TOUPAN hoihlou a tunsak tengteng tungtang thu ah amah a lungmuang uh: michiin leng amah sum nengneng leh, mi chihin dangkaeng zungbuh a pia uhi.
ENGLISH: Then came there to him all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Yahweh had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, literally, kesitah, a unit of money, probably silver and everyone a ring of gold.

PAITE: Huchiin TOUPAN Job tawpna lam a kipatna lam sangin a nak vualjawl jawa: huchiin belam sang sawmleh li, leh sangawngsau sang guk leh bawngtal sang khat leh, sabengtungnu sang khat a neia.
ENGLISH: So Yahweh blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.

PAITE: Tapa sagih leh tanu thum leng a nei a.
ENGLISH: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

PAITE: Huan a masapen, Jemima a chi a; a nihna min, Kezia; a thumna min, Keren-happuk.
ENGLISH: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.

PAITE: Huan gamsung pumpi ah Job tanute banga melhoih a om kei uhi: huan a pa un a unaute uh lakah goutan amau a pia.
ENGLISH: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.

PAITE: Huai nungin Job bel kum ja leh sawmli a dama, a tapate, leh a tapate tapate, khang li nasan a mu hi.Huchiin Job a sita a, a tek mahmah, nite a tam mahmah ngala.
ENGLISH: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.

PAITE: Huchiin Job a sita a, a tek mahmah, nite a tam mahmah ngala.
ENGLISH: So Job died, being old and full of days.

PAITE: Tuin samin; nang hondawng kuamahmah a om a? huan misiangthoute lakah a kua pen lam na nga dia?
ENGLISH: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

PAITE: Lungjinnain lah mi hai a that ngala, huan thiknain mi mawl a hihlum sek hi.
ENGLISH: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.

PAITE: Mihai zungkai ka mutaa; himahleh thakhatin a tenna ka hamsiat hi.
ENGLISH: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

PAITE: A tate bitna akipan gamla pi ah a om ua, huan kongpi ah hihgawpin a om uh, kuamah amaute suakta ding a om sam kei uhi.
ENGLISH: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,

PAITE: Kua anlak ding ahia gilkialmiin a gaih khita, ling laka kipan nasana a lak khiak, thangin a sum uh duhin a kam lianpiin a ka hi.
ENGLISH: whose harvest the hungry eats up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.

PAITE: Gimthuakna lah leivui akipanin a hongpawt keia, lei a kipanin buaina leng a hongdawn khe sam kei hi;
ENGLISH: For affliction doesn’t come forth from the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;

PAITE: Himahleh mihing buai ding maha piang ahi, meiekte a tou len bangin.
ENGLISH: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

PAITE: Himahleh ken ahihleh, Pathian lamah ka zong dinga, huan Pathian kiangah ka thu ka koih ding hi.
ENGLISH: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,

PAITE: Thil thupite hihpa leh zonkhiaktheihlouh; sim zohlouh thil lamdangte:
ENGLISH: who does great things that can’t be fathomed, marvelous things without number;

PAITE: Lei tunga vuah pepa leh, loute tunga tui sawlpa:
ENGLISH: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;

PAITE: Huchiin aman a niamsate tung sangah a koihtou a; huan misi sunte muanna ah a tawisang hi.
ENGLISH: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.

PAITE: Zekhemhatte lunggelte bangmahlou a suaksaka, huchiin a khutte un a thiltup uh a hih theikei uhi.
ENGLISH: He frustrates the devices of the crafty, So that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.

PAITE: Mi pilte a zekhemhatna un a mana: huan mihoihloute thugen akhupathalin a paihsak hi.
ENGLISH: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.

PAITE: Sunlaiin khomialna a thuak ua, janlai bangin suntang laiin a mai maimah uh.
ENGLISH: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.

PAITE: Himahleh a kam ua kipanin pabeite ahondama, mi hatte khut akipanin tasamte mahmah.
ENGLISH: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.

PAITE: Huchiin gentheiin lametna a neia, huan, thulimlouhnain a kam a humsak hi.
ENGLISH: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.

PAITE: Ngaiin, Pathianin a bawlhoih min nuam a sa hi; huaijiakin Bangkim hihthei sawina musit ken.
ENGLISH: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

PAITE: Aman lah meima a bawla, a tuama: a liamsaka, huan a khutin a damsak hi.
ENGLISH: For he wounds, and binds up. He injures, and his hands make whole.

PAITE: Buaina gukah a honsuakta sak dinga; ahi, sagih ah gilouin nang a honkhoih kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil shall touch you.

PAITE: Kial chiangin nang sihna akipan a hontan ding; namsau thilhihtheihna akipan, kidou chiangin.
ENGLISH: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.

PAITE: Lei jepna akipanin selin na om dinga; siatna ahongtun chiangin na lau sam kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither shall you be afraid of destruction when it comes.

PAITE: Siatna leh kialna ah na nui dinga, lei gamsate na kihta sam kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: At destruction and famine you shall laugh, neither shall you be afraid of the animals of the earth.

PAITE: Gama suangte toh na kithuahtheih ding jiak un; huan gama gamsate nang tohna kituak ding uhi.
ENGLISH: For you shall be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field shall be at peace with you.

PAITE: Huan na puanin muangin a om chih na thei ding; huan na ganhuang na veh dinga, bangmah kimlou a om kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: You shall know that your tent is in peace. You shall visit your fold, and shall miss nothing.

PAITE: Na chite leng a thupi ding chih na thei dinga, huan na suante lei loupa bangin.
ENGLISH: You shall know also that your seed shall be great, Your offspring as the grass of the earth.

PAITE: Kum chingin na han na juan dinga, a huna buh lak bangin.Ngaiin, hiai, i zongta ua, huchiin a om, jain, na hoihna dingin theiin.
ENGLISH: You shall come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.

PAITE: Ngaiin, hiai, i zongta ua, huchiin a om, jain, na hoihna dingin theiin.
ENGLISH: Look this, we have searched it, so it is. Hear it, and know it for your good.”

PAITE: Huchiin Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered,

PAITE: Aw ka lungjinna kibuk peuhmah leh, huan ka tuahsiatna khaina ah kikoih khawm peuhmah leh:
ENGLISH: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!

PAITE: Tuin tuipitea piaunel sangin a gikzo ding: huaijiakin ka thute leng a huham hi.
ENGLISH: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.

PAITE: Thilbangkimhihthei thalte lah ka sungah a om ngala, gu huai akipana ka khain a dawn vek: Pathian mulkimhuainate kei dou dingin a kivual petmah uhi.
ENGLISH: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.

PAITE: Loupa a neih laiin gam sabengtung a ham hia? ahihkeileh a annekding tungah bawngtal a ham hia?
ENGLISH: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

PAITE: Gim neilou chi tel louin a kine thei dia hia? ahihkeileh aktuida ah limna mawngmawng a om hia?
ENGLISH: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

PAITE: Ka khain amaute a khoih nuam kei; kei dingin an kihhuai bang ahi uh.
ENGLISH: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.

PAITE: Aw ka nget tang thei leng jaw; ka thil deih Pathianin honphal lejaw:
ENGLISH: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,

PAITE: Kei honhihgawp dingin Pathian deihlam hi lai henla; a khut zanin, kei honsat khe mai leh:
ENGLISH: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

PAITE: Huchiin lungmuanna ka nei lai mai dia; ahi, dawmlou natna ah ka kipak ding: Mi Siangthou thute lah ka kitheihmohbawl ngal kei a.
ENGLISH: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

PAITE: Ka hatna bang ahia, ka ngak ding? huan ka beina bang ahia, ka kuhkal ding?
ENGLISH: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?

PAITE: Ka hatna, suangte hatna hi hia? ahihkeileh ka sa dalsik hia?
ENGLISH: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?

PAITE: Keiah panpihna a om het kei hilou hia, huan kei akipan theihsiamna hawlmangin?
ENGLISH: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?

PAITE: Bah dia mansaa om kiangah a lawmin Siamna a etsak ding ahi kei mo; huchilou-in Bangkimhihthei kihtakna a tawpsan ahi kei ding mo.
ENGLISH: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

PAITE: Luita bangin ka unaute a lepchiah uh; luita mangthang luanna bangin.
ENGLISH: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;

PAITE: Huai tuh tuikhalin a voma; huai ah vuk a kisel.
ENGLISH: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.

PAITE: A lum hun chiangin a tuimang ua, a sat chingin a mun ua kipan a mangthang uh.
ENGLISH: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

PAITE: Huai lampia khualzinte a pial ua, bangmah omlouhna munah a paitou ua, a mangthang uh.
ENGLISH: The caravans that travel beside them turn aside. They go up into the waste, and perish.

PAITE: Tema khualzinten a zong ua, Seba pawlten a lamen uh.
ENGLISH: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.

PAITE: A kilamet hangun a zahlak uh; huai lamah avapai ua a hawmsuak uh.
ENGLISH: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.

PAITE: Tuin lah bangmah na hi ngal kei ua; mulkimhuaina na mu ua, na lau uhi.
ENGLISH: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.

PAITE: Kei honpia un? ahihkeileh na neihlehlam ua kipanin kei adingin thilpiak lan un, ka chi hia?
ENGLISH: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’

PAITE: Ahihkeileh, nuaisiahhatmite khut ahipan hontan un, ka chi hia?
ENGLISH: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’

PAITE: Hon sinsakin, huan ka dai ding: ka lamhaihna theisiam dingin hon bawlin.
ENGLISH: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

PAITE: Dikna thute hat hina mahmah e: Himahleh na miselnain bang a selphoua?
ENGLISH: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?

PAITE: Thute selphou dinga um na hi uh hia? Chimoh mi thugente huih bang ahi chih theiin.
ENGLISH: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?

PAITE: A hi, paneiloute tungah ai na san ding ua, na lawm uh sumsinna vanin na bawl ding uh.
ENGLISH: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.

PAITE: Tuin huaijiakin hehpihtakin hon en un; na ma uah ka juau ka gen sin ngal kei a.
ENGLISH: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.

PAITE: Kik nawn un ka honngen ahi, diklouhna om kei hen; ahi, kik nawn un, ka thu a dik ahi.Ka lei ah diklouhna a om hia? thil hoihlou ka leiin a theikak theikei dia hia?
ENGLISH: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.

PAITE: Ka lei ah diklouhna a om hia? thil hoihlou ka leiin a theikak theikei dia hia?
ENGLISH: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?

PAITE: Lei tungah mihing adin kidouna a om kei mo? huan a nite kilohmi nite bang ahi ka hia?
ENGLISH: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?

PAITE: Lim deih mahmah sikha bangin, a loh lamen kilohmi bangin:
ENGLISH: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,

PAITE: Huaibangin bangmahlou khate nei dinga bawl ka hi, huan kei adingin jan chimhuaite seh ahi hi.
ENGLISH: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.

PAITE: Ka lup chiangin, Chikchiangin ka thou dia? ka chi a; himahleh jan a sawt hi; huan khatlam khatlamah ni suah matan kilumlehnain ka dim hi.
ENGLISH: When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.

PAITE: Ka sa than leh leivui khalin a tuama; ka vun a kimata a puakkham thak hi.
ENGLISH: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.

PAITE: Ka nite siamganmi khohthei sangin a kin jawa, lametna beia zatbei ahi.
ENGLISH: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.

PAITE: Aw ka hinna huih ahi chih theigige in: ka mitin hoih a mu nawn kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye shall no more see good.

PAITE: Kei honmu mitin honen thei nawn takei dinga; na mitte ka tugnah a om ding ua, himahleh ka omta kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: The eye of him who sees me shall see me no more. Your eyes shall be on me, but I shall not be.

PAITE: Meipi a mangthanga a omta kei bangin, huchiin kuapeuh Seola pai suk a hongpai tou nawnta kei uhi.
ENGLISH: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. shall come up no more.

PAITE: A in ah a kik nawnta kei dinga, a munin amah a thei nawnta kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

PAITE: Huaijiakin ka kam ka khou kei dinga; ka lungsim gimnaah thu ka gen ding; ka kha haksatna ah ka phun ding hi.
ENGLISH: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

PAITE: Tuipi ka hi hia, a hihkeileh tuipiganhinglian, huchia kei na honchin nak?
ENGLISH: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?

PAITE: Ka lupnain honlungmuan dinga, ka tutna nemin ka phunna a jangkhaisak ding, ka chih chiangin;
ENGLISH: When I say, ‘My bed shall comfort me. My couch shall ease my complaint;’

PAITE: Huaichiangin mangtein na honlau saka, mengmuhnatein na honmulkimsak hi:
ENGLISH: then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:

PAITE: Huchiin ka khain heklup leh sihna a tela, hiai ka guhte sangin.
ENGLISH: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.

PAITE: Ka hinna ka chimtaka; ka hing gige kei ding: honom sak maimai un; ka nite lah bangmahlou ahi ngala.
ENGLISH: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.

PAITE: Mihing bang ahi, amah na hihlet dinga, amah tunga na lungtang na koih dinga.
ENGLISH: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,

PAITE: Jingsang tenga amah na veh dinga, mitphiat chiha amah na ettel ding?
ENGLISH: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?

PAITE: Bangtan vei kei honlehngatsan lou ding na hia, bangtanvei ka chil ka nawmvalh matan honomsak maimai lou ding na hia?
ENGLISH: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?

PAITE: Na khial hita leng, na tungah bang ka hiha, Aw mite chingpa nang? bangdia nang adia chiamtehna banga konkoih na hia, huchia keimaha dia puakgik ka hih maimah?Huan bangdia ka tatlekna ngaidam loua, ka thulimlohna la mang lou oi? Kei tuin leivuia lum ding ka hi a; kuhkaltakin na honzong dia, himahleh ka omta kei ding.
ENGLISH: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?

PAITE: Huan bangdia ka tatlekna ngaidam loua, ka thulimlohna la mang lou oi? Kei tuin leivuia lum ding ka hi a; kuhkaltakin na honzong dia, himahleh ka omta kei ding.
ENGLISH: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I shall not be.”

PAITE: Huchiin Bildad Sua miin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

PAITE: Bangtan hiai thilte gen ding na hia? huan bangtan na kama thute huih hat bang ding ahi ua?
ENGLISH: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?

PAITE: Pathianin vaihawmna a hekkawi ahia? ahihkeileh Thilbang-kimhih theiin dikna a hekkawi ahia?
ENGLISH: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?

PAITE: Na tate a tunga a khelh ua, hua a tatlekna uh khuta amaute a pikhiak a leh:
ENGLISH: If your children have sinned against him, He has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.

PAITE: Pathian lam kuhkaltaka na zona, hua Thilbangkimhihthei kianga na thilnget na bawl leh;
ENGLISH: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.

PAITE: Na siangthoua na dik leh; nang jiakin tuin ka khanglou mahmah dia, huan na diktatna omna a lohching sak ding hi.
ENGLISH: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.

PAITE: Huan na kipatna neu mahleh, ahihhangin na tawpna na nunglam nakpiin a khang ding hi.
ENGLISH: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.

PAITE: Huai jiakin ka honngen ahi, hun masa thu kan inla, a pipute un a na zonkhiak uh lamah kisuk in:
ENGLISH: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.

PAITE: (Ei lah jana lel i hi ua, bangmah i theikei uh, leitungah i nite uh lah limliap ahi a: )
ENGLISH: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)

PAITE: Amauten nang a honsinsak un, a honhilh un, a lungtang ua kipanin thute a gen kei ding ua hia?
ENGLISH: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?

PAITE: Buannawi louin phaipek a khang khe thei ahia? tui louin loupa a khangthei ahia?
ENGLISH: “Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?

PAITE: Hinga a oma, sat puk louh a hihlaiin, loupa dangte main a vuai nak hi.
ENGLISH: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.

PAITE: Huaibangmahin Pathian manghilhte tengteng lampi ahi; huan pathianlimsaklou mi lametna a mangthang ding:
ENGLISH: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man shall perish,

PAITE: A muanna a kitam dinga, a kingakna maimomlen ahi hi.
ENGLISH: Whose confidence shall break apart, Whose trust is a spider’s web.

PAITE: A intung a ngai dia, himahleh a ding kei ding: huaiah a lenchinten dia, himahleh a pangsawt kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: He shall lean on his house, but it shall not stand. He shall cling to it, but it shall not endure.

PAITE: Ni suah main a hinga, huan a selte a huan tuamin a meng khia uh.
ENGLISH: He is green before the sun. His shoots go forth over his garden.

PAITE: A zungte leivum kimah a jam ua, suangte omna mun ah a hing hi.
ENGLISH: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.

PAITE: A mun akipan lakmang hi leh, huchiin amah a kitheihmohbawl dinga, Ka honmu ngeikei, chiin.
ENGLISH: If he is destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’

PAITE: Ngaiin, hiai a lampi kipahna ahia, huan lei akipanin adangte a hongsuak ding uh.
ENGLISH: Behold, this is the joy of his way: out of the earth, others shall spring.

PAITE: Ngaiin, Pathianin mi hoihkim a paikhe kei ding, gilouhihmite leng a tungding sam kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: “Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.

PAITE: Na kam nuihin a hondimsak lai lai dia, na mukte kikounain.Nang honmudahte zumnain akhuh dinga; huan gilou puanin omta kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.

PAITE: Nang honmudahte zumnain akhuh dinga; huan gilou puanin omta kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Those who hate you shall be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked shall be no more.”

PAITE: Huan Jobin a dawnga, hichiin a chi a:
ENGLISH: Then Job answered,

ENGLISH: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?

ENGLISH: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.

ENGLISH: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him, and prospered?

PAITE: Mualte a suana, a theikei ua, heha amaute a lumleh laiin.
ENGLISH: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.

PAITE: A mun akipanin lei a singa, huan huaia khuamte aling uh.

PAITE: Ni thu a piaa, huan a suak kei; aksite a bilhkhum ngiungeu hi.
ENGLISH: He commands the sun, and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.

PAITE: Amah kian vante a phalhkhiaa, tuipi kihawt tungah a pai hi.

ENGLISH: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.

PAITE: Aman sui theih vuallouh thil thupite a hiha; ahi, sim zohlouh thillamdangte.
ENGLISH: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.

PAITE: Ngaiin, ka kiangah a paia, amah ka mu kei: a pai lailaia, himahleh amah ka mu kei hi.
ENGLISH: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.

PAITE: Ngaiin, samat a mana, amah kuan a kham thei dia? Bang hih na hia? kuan a kiangah a chi dia.
ENGLISH: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’

PAITE: Pathianin a hehna a lakik kei ding; Rahab panpihmite amah nuaiah a kun petmah uhi.
ENGLISH: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.

PAITE: Bangchipheta tawm jawin amah ka dawngin, amah toh ngaihtuah dingin ka thute ka telkhe dia?
ENGLISH: How much less shall I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?

PAITE: Amah, diktatta zongleng, ka dawng kei ding hi; ka gal kiangah thilngetna ka bawl ding.
ENGLISH: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.

PAITE: Samta leng la, huan honna dawngta leh; himahleh ka aw a ngaikhia chih ka um kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.

PAITE: Huihpiin aman a honkitamsaka, a san omlouin ka liamnate a pungsak hi.
ENGLISH: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.

PAITE: Ka nak a honphal keia, himahleh thangpaihnain a hondimsak hi.
ENGLISH: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

PAITE: Hatna thu gen leng, ngaiin, Amah a hat hi: huan vaihawmna thu, kuan hun a pe dia?
ENGLISH: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’

PAITE: Diktatta zongleng, ka kamin a honmohpaih hi: hoihkim ta zongleng, hoihlouin a hontelsak ding hi.
ENGLISH: Though I am righteous, my own mouth shall condemn me. Though I am blameless, it shall prove me perverse.

PAITE: Hoih kim mahleng, ka kilimsak kei; ka hinna ka musit.
ENGLISH: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.

PAITE: Khat ahi veka; huaijiakin, Hoihkim leh gilou a hihse tuak, ka chi
ENGLISH: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.

PAITE: Jepnain thakhatin hihlum leh, mi hoih thuakna a nuihsan ding hi.
ENGLISH: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.

PAITE: Lei mi gilou khuta piakin a om: huaia vaihawmmite maitangte a tuama; amah ahihkeileh, kua a hita dia?
ENGLISH: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?

PAITE: Tuin ka nite laitaipihmi sangin a kinjaw: a tai mang ua, hoih a mu kei uh.

PAITE: Long kinte bangin a pai mang uhi: muvanlai samat tunga ngumkiak bangin.
ENGLISH: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.

PAITE: Ka phunna ka mang ngilh dia, ka mel lungkham ka pai dia, ka kipak ding, chi leng.

ENGLISH: I shall be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?

ENGLISH: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,

PAITE: Kei bangin, amah lah mihing ahi keia, amah ka dawn theihna dingin, vaihawmnaa ka hoh khawm theihna ding un.

PAITE: Ka kikal uah kou gel honmat theihna dingin, thulaigenmi a om kei hi.
ENGLISH: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.

PAITE: Kei akipanin achiang la meng henla a kihtakhuainain kei honlausak kei hen:Huaichiangin thu ka gen dia, amah ka lau kei ding: keimah ah lah huchibang ka hi ngal kei a.
ENGLISH: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;

PAITE: Amoz tapa Isaiin Judate kumpipa Uzzia te, Jothamte, Ahaz te, Hezekia te lal laia, Judate leh Jerusalem tugtang thu-a kilakna a muh thu.
ENGLISH: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

ENGLISH: Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for Yahweh “Yahweh” is God’s proper Name, sometimes rendered “LORD” (all caps) in other translations. has spoken: “I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.

PAITE: Bawngtalin a neitu a theia, sabengtungin leng a pu anpiakna a thei: Israelten bel a theikei uh, ka miten a ngaihtuah kei uh, chiin.
ENGLISH: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel doesn’t know, my people don’t consider.”

PAITE: Ah! nam gilou thulimlouhna gikpi pua mite, chi thil hoihlou hihte, ta hoihlou pi-a gamta sekte ahi ua: TOUPA a paisan ua, Israelte Mi Siangthou a musit ua, kihihtuamin a nungtolhta uh.
ENGLISH: Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken Yahweh. They have despised the Holy One of Israel. They are estranged and backward.

ENGLISH: Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

PAITE: Khepek nuaia kipana lutang phain damlai himhim a om kei; chikeh, vuak sidup ek, meima nai la ngen ahi: huaite lah a mek bing kei ua, tuam leng a tuam sam kei ua, sathau leng a nuh kei uh.
ENGLISH: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it: wounds, welts, and open sores. They haven’t been closed, neither bandaged, neither soothed with oil.

ENGLISH: Your country is desolate. Your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your land in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

ENGLISH: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.

ENGLISH: Unless Yahweh of Armies had left to us a very small remnant, we would have been as Sodom; we would have been like Gomorrah.

ENGLISH: Hear the word of Yahweh, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “Elohim.” , you people of Gomorrah!

PAITE: TOUPAN, Huzahzaha na kithoihna uh kei dinga bang ahia a thamatna om? Belamtal haltuma latte leh gan vakthaute thauin a honnimta; bawngpate leh belam noute leh kelpate sisan ah leng ka kipak kei, a chi.
ENGLISH: “What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?,” says Yahweh. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed animals. I don’t delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.

PAITE: Ka maa kilan dinga na hongpai un, ka biakin huangsuang intual sik kuan a honphuta?
ENGLISH: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts?

PAITE: Thilpiak bangmahloute hontawi nawn kei un; banghiam gimlim kei adingin thil kihhuaipi ahi; kha thakte, khawlnite, khawmpite na kichial khawmte mawkmawk uh ka iplah mahmah; thulimlouhna ahi, kikhopna thupitak leng.
ENGLISH: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me; new moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I can’t bear with evil assemblies.

ENGLISH: My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They are a burden to me. I am weary of bearing them.

ENGLISH: When you spread forth your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood.

PAITE: Kisil unla, kihihsiang un; ka mitmuh phaklouh din na thilhihte uh a gitouhna koih mang un; gilou hih tawpta uh:
ENGLISH: Wash yourselves, make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.

PAITE: Thil hoih hih kisinta unla; vaihawmna diktat zong un, nuaisiahna thuakte panpih unla, pa neiloute vaihawm sak unla, meithai thu gensak un, a chi hi.
ENGLISH: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Judge the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”

PAITE: TOUPAN, Hongpai un, ngaihtuah khawm dih ve ni! Na khelhnate uh san au bangin aom mahleh, vuk bangin a ngou ding; san dup bangin san khin mahleh belam mul bangin a om ding.
ENGLISH: “Come now, and let us reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

ENGLISH: If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land;

ENGLISH: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.

ENGLISH: Your silver has become dross, your wine mixed with water.

ENGLISH: Your princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves. Everyone loves bribes, and follows after rewards. They don’t judge the fatherless, neither does the cause of the widow come to them.

ENGLISH: Therefore the Lord, The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” Yahweh of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says: “Ah, I will get relief from my adversaries, and avenge myself of my enemies;

PAITE: Huan, na tungah ka khut ka kha dinga, na eksia siang sipsipin ka hihmang ding, na sikgawm tengteng ka la mang vek ding:
ENGLISH: and I will turn my hand on you, thoroughly purge away your dross, and will take away all your tin.

ENGLISH: I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called ‘The city of righteousness, a faithful town.’

ENGLISH: They will only bow down under the prisoners, and will fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

ENGLISH: Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!

ENGLISH: However he doesn’t mean so, neither does his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy, and to cut off not a few nations.

ENGLISH: For he says, “Aren’t all of my princes kings?

PAITE: Kalno khua Karkemis khua bang hita lou ahi maw? Hamath khua Arpad khua bang hita lou ahi maw? Samari khua Damaska khua bang hita lou ahi maw?
ENGLISH: Isn’t Calno like Carchemish? Isn’t Hamath like Arpad? Isn’t Samaria like Damascus?”

ENGLISH: As my hand has found the kingdoms of the idols, whose engraved images exceeded those of Jerusalem and of Samaria;

ENGLISH: shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?

PAITE: Huchi a hih jiakin hichi ahi dinga; TOUPAN Zion tang leh Jerusalem kho sunga a nasep ding tengteng a sep khit hun chiangin Asuria kumpipa lungsim kiotsakna gah leh a mit kisathei thupina ka gawt sin hi.
ENGLISH: Therefore it will happen that, when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the willful proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the insolence of his haughty looks.

PAITE: Aman, Ka khut hatnain ka hiht hi, ka pilna tohin; ka kizen ngala; chih chih gamgite khawng lah ka suana, a vaihawmna uh lah ka suta, laltutphaha tute lah mi hangsan hih bangin ka kai khia hi.
ENGLISH: For he has said, “By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I have understanding: and I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures. Like a valiant man I have brought down their rulers.

PAITE: Ka khutin chi chih hausaknate lah vasa bu bangin a zong khiaa; min vasa tuia pi loihsansa a la uh bangin lei tengteng ka la khinvekta hi; ka jap hiam, kam ka hiam ham hiamhim hiam leng a om kei uhi, a chi vial ngala.
ENGLISH: My hand has found the riches of the peoples like a nest, and like one gathers eggs that are abandoned, have I gathered all the earth. There was no one who moved their wing, or that opened their mouth, or chirped.”

PAITE: Heipiin thil ehna dinga a zangmi a kisaktheihsan dia hia? Singatnain a atmi a nuaisiah dia hia? Khetbukin a dommite a lik zosop diam aw, chiangin sing lah hi lou a lik zomah bang phet ahi.
ENGLISH: Should an axe brag against him who chops with it? Should a saw exalt itself above him who saws with it? As if a rod should lift those who lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up someone who is not wood.

PAITE: Huaijiakin TOUPA, Sepaihte, TOUPAN, a mi thaute lakah gawnna a sawl dinga; a thupina nuaiah mei kuang lai lel bangin mei tohin a om ding.
ENGLISH: Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory a burning will be kindled like the burning of fire.

PAITE: Huan, Israelte vakna mei a honghi dinga, a Mi Siangthou mah uleng meikuang ahi ding; huaiin ni khat thuin loulingneite leh khaulingneite a kangsakin a hihmangthang ding.
ENGLISH: The light of Israel will be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.

PAITE: A gammang leh a lei hoih mun thupina leng, kha leh sa nasanin, a hihmang ding; huchiin, chiamtehna tawipen kia hun lai bang ahi ding.
ENGLISH: He will consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body. It will be as when a standard bearer faints.

PAITE: A gammanga sing om sek laite naupang gelh tham pheta tawm a hita ding.
ENGLISH: The remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, so that a child could write their number.

PAITE: Huan, huainiin hichi ahi dinga, Israelte omzek laite leh Jakob inkuanpihte laka a damlaiten amaute thatpa a muang nawnta kei ding ua; TOUPA Israelte Mi Singthou, chihtaktakin a muang zota ding uhi.
ENGLISH: It will come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel, and those who have escaped from the house of Jacob will no more again lean on him who struck them, but shall lean on Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

PAITE: A om zek lai. Jakob om zeklaite, Pathian hattak kiang ah a kik nawn ding uh.
ENGLISH: A remnant will return, even the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.

PAITE: Na mi Israelte tuipi piaunel zahin om mah le uh, a om zek laite kia a kik nawn sin ngal ua; diktatna luan letna suksiatna lah tung dinga vaihawmpuk ahi.
ENGLISH: For though your people, Israel, are like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. A destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.

PAITE: TOUPA, Sepaihte TOUPAN, tawpna, tawpna tung ngei dinga vaihawmpuk lah, lei tengteng laizangah a bawl sin ngala.
ENGLISH: For the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will make a full end, and that determined, in the midst of all the earth.

PAITE: Huaijiakin, TOUPA, Sepaihte TOUPAN, hichiin a chi, Ziona om ka mite aw, Aigupta gama a hih bang un khetbuk a nou honvuain achiang na tunguah lik mah leh, Asuria mi jaw kihta kei un.
ENGLISH: Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, says “My people who dwell in Zion, don’t be afraid of the Assyrian, though he strike you with the rod, and lift up his staff against you, as Egypt did.

PAITE: Sawtlou chik nungin ka lungkimlouhna hongbei dia, ka hehna leng amaute hihmanthatna dia heiin a omta ding hi.
ENGLISH: For yet a very little while, and the indignation against you will be accomplished, and my anger will be directed to his destruction.”

PAITE: Ireb suangpia Midiante a thah lai bang un sepaihte tOUPAN amah sual dingin jepna a pei dinga; achiang lah tuipi tung lamah a om dinga Aigupta gama a pei bangin a pei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Yahweh of Armies will stir up a scourge against him, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb. His rod will be over the sea, and he will lift it up like he did against Egypt.

PAITE: Huai niin hi chi ahi dinga, puakgik na liangjanga kipana lakmangin a om dinga, a hakkol leng na ngawngnga kipana lakmangin a om lai ding hi; thau nilh jiakin hakkol lah hihsiatin a omta dinga, chiin.
ENGLISH: It will happen in that day, that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing oil.

PAITE: Rimon akipan Aiath khua a tungta Migron khuaah a pai suakta; Mikmas khuaah a van a koihta.
ENGLISH: He has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his baggage.

PAITE: Kuam ah a tumta uh; Geba khuaah a giakta uh; Ramah khuate a lingling ua; Saula, Gibeah khote a taimangta uhi.
ENGLISH: They have gone over the pass. They have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has fled.

PAITE: Gallim kho tanu aw! na awin ngaihtakin kikou in; Laishah khua aw! ngaikhiain; Anathoth aw, hehpihhuai na lawmlawm chia!
ENGLISH: Cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! You poor Anathoth!

PAITE: Madmenah khote taimangin a omta uh; Gebim khuaa omte taimang tumin a kidelh luailuai uh.
ENGLISH: Madmenah is a fugitive. The inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.

PAITE: tuni mahmahin Nob khuaah a tam sin; Zion tanu tang, Jerusalem mual pawng a khut a sin khum hi.
ENGLISH: This very day he will halt at Nob. He shakes his hand at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

PAITE: Ngai dih, TOUPA, sepahte TOUPAN, thil mulkimhuaitakin ahiangte a sat khe dinga, sang pipite lah phuk in a om dinga, a dawk tuamte leng gawi niamin a om ding.Sikin gamnuai sing sahte a phuk dinga, LEbanon sidar singte mi thupi pukin a puk juajua ding uh.
ENGLISH: Behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.

PAITE: Sikin gamnuai sing sahte a phuk dinga, LEbanon sidar singte mi thupi pukin a puk juajua ding uh.
ENGLISH: He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.

PAITE: Jesai bul akipanin selnou a hongpawt dinga, a zungtea kipanin ahiang a hongkhang khe ding;
ENGLISH: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.

PAITE: Huan TOUPA kha pilna leh theihtheihna kha, lemtheihna leh hatna kha theihna leh TOUPA launa kha a tungah a tu ding
ENGLISH: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.

PAITE: Huchiin a kipahna a TOUPA launaah ahi ding A mita a muh bangin vai a hawm kei dinga a bil a a jal bangin leng a taihilh sam kei ding
ENGLISH: His delight will be in the fear of Yahweh. He will not judge by the sight of his eyes, neither decide by the hearing of his ears;

PAITE: Gentheite diktat takin vai a hawm sak zo dinga, lei mi thunuailutte adingin khentuam neilouin a taihilh sak lai ding hi; a kama khetbukin lei a khen dinga, a muka huin mi gilousaloute a that ding.
ENGLISH: but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.

PAITE: Huan, diktatna a kawnggakna ahi dinga, ginomna a taigakna ahi ding hi.
ENGLISH: Righteousness will be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his waist.

PAITE: Huan, ngia lah belamnou toh a om khawmta ding ua, gialbem kelnou toh a bok khawm ta ding uh, bawng nou leh humpinelkai tuai lai leh gan vak thaute a om khawm ta ding ua; naupangnouin a pi zungzung ding hi.
ENGLISH: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; The calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them.

PAITE: Huan, bawng leh vompi a gamta khawm ding ua; a noute uh a bok khawm chiptep ta ding uh; huan humpinelkaiin bawngtal bangin buhpawl a neta ding.
ENGLISH: The cow and the bear will graze. Their young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.

PAITE: Huan, nau nawitui ne lai thangtom ko geiah a om hiathiat dinga, nau nawitui nek tawpsain guldekpak ko geiah a khut a nga ding
ENGLISH: The nursing child will play near a cobra’s hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper’s den.

PAITE: Ka tang siangthou mawngmawngah kihihnat a omta kei dinga, kihihsiat leng a om nawnta kei ding, tuitein tuipi a khuh gige bangin, lei TOUPA theihnain a dim khin vek sinta hi.
ENGLISH: They will not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain; for the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.

PAITE: Huan, huai niin hichi ahi dinga, Jesai zung mi chih chiamtehna dinga ding, amah mahmah nam chihin a dong ding ua, a khawlna mun lah thupi ding hi.
ENGLISH: It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.

PAITE: Huan, huai niin hichi ahi dinga, TOUPAN a si val om sun a mite, Asuria gam akipan bang, Aigupta gam akipan bang, Pathros gam akipan bang, Kus gam akipan bang, Elam gam akipan bang, Sinar gam akipan bang. Hamath khua akipan bang, tuipi tuikulhgam akipan bang, a la nawndinga a nihveina dingin a khut a jak nawn ding.
ENGLISH: It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.

PAITE: Huan nam chih adingin chiamtehna a takkhe dinga, Israel delhkhiakte a pikhawm dinga, Juda dalhte kawlmong li akipan a pikhawm ding
ENGLISH: He will set up a banner for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

PAITE: Huchiin, Ephraimte hajatna a beita dinga, Judate hihbuaimite hihmanthatin a omta ding uh; Ephraimten Judate a haza nawnta kei ding ua, Judaten leng Ephraimte a hihbuai nawn kei ding uh.
ENGLISH: The envy also of Ephraim will depart, and those who persecute Judah will be cut off. Ephraim won’t envy Judah, and Judah won’t persecute Ephraim.

PAITE: Huchiin, amaute tuh tumlamah Philistiate liangjangah leng suk in a va tuang ding ua; suahlam mite a lok khawm ding uh; Edom leh Moabte tungah a khut uh a kha ding ua, Ammon suanten a thu uh a mangta ding uh.
ENGLISH: They will fly down on the shoulders of the Philistines on the west. Together they will plunder the children of the east. They will extend their power over Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon will obey them.

PAITE: Huan, TOUPAN Aigupta tuipi lei a hihse vek dinga, Luipi leng a huih sa huthutin a khut a sin khum dinga, luita khepek leng kawt louin a pai galkah ding.Huchiin, Aigupta gam akipan a pattouh ni-ua adinga lamlian a hongom bangin, a sibang om sun a mite adingin Asuria gam akipanin lamlian a hongom ding hi.
ENGLISH: Yahweh will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind he will wave his hand over the River, and will split it into seven streams, and cause men to march over in sandals.

PAITE: Huchiin, Aigupta gam akipan a pattouh ni-ua adinga lamlian a hongom bangin, a sibang om sun a mite adingin Asuria gam akipanin lamlian a hongom ding hi.
ENGLISH: There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

PAITE: Huai ni chiangin hichi bangin na chi dinga. TOUPA aw, kipahthu ka hon hilh hi; ka tungah na hehta mah lechin, na hehna lah a daita, nang honkhamuante neive.
ENGLISH: In that day you will say, “I will give thanks to you, Yahweh; for though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away and you comfort me.

PAITE: Ngaiin, Pathian lah honhondampa ahi a; ka gingta dinga, lauin ka om kei ding; TOUPA Jehova lah ka hatna leh ka la ahi ngala, honhondampa leng ahi, chiin.
ENGLISH: Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust, and will not be afraid; for Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.”

PAITE: Huaijiakin hotdamna tuikhuk akipan nuamin tui na tai ding uh.
ENGLISH: Therefore with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.

PAITE: Huan, huai niin hichiin na chi ding. TOUPA kiangah kipahthu hilh unla, a min lou unla, a thilhihte mi chih lakah theisak unla, a min pahtawiin a om chih gen un.
ENGLISH: In that day you will say, “Give thanks to Yahweh! Call on his name. Declare his doings among the peoples. Proclaim that his name is exalted!

PAITE: TOUPA pahtawiin lasa un; aman lah thil hoihpente a nahihta ngala; huai tuh lei tengtengah theihin om hen.Ziona omte aw, ngaihtakin kikou unla, kikou vengvung un, Israelte Mi Siangthou na lak ua om lah a thupi ngala, chiin.
ENGLISH: Sing to Yahweh, for he has done excellent things! Let this be known in all the earth!

PAITE: Ziona omte aw, ngaihtakin kikou unla, kikou vengvung un, Israelte Mi Siangthou na lak ua om lah a thupi ngala, chiin.
ENGLISH: Cry aloud and shout, you inhabitant of Zion; for the Holy One of Israel is great in the midst of you!”

PAITE: Babulon kho puak gik Amoz tapa Isaiin a muh thu.
ENGLISH: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw:

PAITE: Mi liante kongpitea a lut theihna ding un tang mai velvul ah chiamtehna tak khia unla, ngaih takin amau sam unla, khutin hihdingdan hilh un.
ENGLISH: Set up a banner on the bare mountain! Lift up your voice to them! Wave your hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.

PAITE: Kei mahmahin ka mi sehte thu ka peta, ahi, ka mi hat tak, ka mi kinuamsakte, ka hehna tangtung sak dingin ka samta hi.
ENGLISH: I have commanded my consecrated ones; yes, I have called my mighty men for my anger, even my proudly exulting ones.

PAITE: Tua! tanga mipi husa, mipi a tamatam husa bang mahmah! Tua! nam chih gama mi om khawmte chiak vengvung husa! sepaihte TOUPAN gal sual dinga sepaihte kaikhawm eive.
ENGLISH: The noise of a multitude is in the mountains, as of a great people; the noise of an uproar of the kingdoms of the nations gathered together! Yahweh of Armies is mustering the army for the battle.

PAITE: Amaute, TOUPa leh a lungkumlouhna vanzat, gam gamlapi akipan, kawlmong tawpna mahmah akipanin gam tengteng hihse dingin a hong pai uhi.
ENGLISH: They come from a far country, from the uttermost part of heaven, even Yahweh, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.

PAITE: Mau tuaituai un; TOUPA ni lah a naita ngala, Bangkimhihtheia kipan a siatna a hongtung bangin a hongtung sin hi.
ENGLISH: Wail; for the day of Yahweh is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.

PAITE: Huaijiakin khut tengteng a hat kei ding a, mihing lungtang chiteng leng a zulmang ding:
ENGLISH: Therefore all hands will be feeble, and everyone’s heart will melt.

PAITE: Huan, a lau ding ua; damlouhna leh lungkumlouhnaten amaute a man dinga; numei nauvei bangmaiin a chi uh a na ding; lamdang kisa tuahin a om chiat ding uh; a melte uh meikuang mel bang ahi ding.
ENGLISH: They will be dismayed. Pangs and sorrows will seize them. They will be in pain like a woman in labor. They will look in amazement one at another. Their faces will be faces of flame.

ENGLISH: Behold, the day of Yahweh comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.

PAITE: Van aksite leh aksimunkipte un a vakna uh a suaksak kei ding ua; ni lah a suah laiin mialsakin a om dinga, khain leng a vakna a vaksak sinta kei ahi.
ENGLISH: For the stars of the sky and its constellations will not give their light. The sun will be darkened in its going forth, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.

PAITE: Huan, khovel a gitlouhna jiakin ka gawt ding a, mi gilousaloute a thulimlouhna jiak un ka gawt sam ding. Huan, mi kisathei paukhauh lah ka tawpsak dinga, mi kihtakhuai kisaktheinna lah ka niamsak lai ding hi.
ENGLISH: I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity. I will cause the arrogance of the proud to cease, and will humble the haughtiness of the terrible.

PAITE: Mi tuh dangkaeng siangthou sanga leng hak jawin ka bawl dinga, mihing mahmah lah Ophir dangkaeng siangthou sanga leng hak jawin ka bawl ding.
ENGLISH: I will make people more rare than fine gold, even a person than the pure gold of Ophir.

PAITE: Huchiin tunga van ka kisingsak dinga, sepaihte TOUPA hehna jiakin, a hehna ni thupi tak niin, lei leng a omna mun kisuan thamin linsakin a om ding.
ENGLISH: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken out of its place in the wrath of Yahweh of Armies, and in the day of his fierce anger.

ENGLISH: It will happen that like a hunted gazelle, and like sheep that no one gathers, they will each turn to their own people, and will each flee to their own land.

PAITE: Muha om peuhmah dawt pailetin a om dinga, huan, mata om peuhmah namsaua sat paihin a om ding.
ENGLISH: Everyone who is found will be thrust through. Everyone who is captured will fall by the sword.

PAITE: A naungekte uleng a mit muh un jan dimdem khopa lei satnaa zatin a om ding uh; a inte uh lohin a om dia, a jite uh leng mawksual tuakin a om ding uh.
ENGLISH: Their infants also will be dashed in pieces before their eyes. Their houses will be ransacked, and their wives raped.

PAITE: Ngaiin, Mediate amau sual dingin ka tokthou dinga, huaiten dangka a limsak kei ding ua, dangkaeng leng a kipahpih kei ding uh.
ENGLISH: Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, who will not value silver, and as for gold, they will not delight in it.

PAITE: A thalpeute un tangvalte a ansak dinga; mi gila gah hehpihna himhim a neikei ding uh; a mit un naupangte a hawi kei ding uh.
ENGLISH: Their bows will dash the young men in pieces; and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb. Their eyes will not spare children.

PAITE: Huan, Babulon, gam chih thupina, Kaldaite kisaktheihpih thil hoihtak, Pathianin Sodom leh Gomorra a sukman lai bangin a om ding uh.
ENGLISH: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride, will be like when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

PAITE: Chikchiang inleng huailaiah mi a om nawnta kei ding uh, suan om lai siah inleng a sunga om a om sam kei ding; Arab miten lah huailaiah a puaninte uh a kai sam kei ding ua; belam chingten lah huailaiah a belam honte uh a kualsak sam kei ding uh.
ENGLISH: It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from generation to generation. The Arabian will not pitch a tent there, neither will shepherds make their flocks lie down there.

ENGLISH: But wild animals of the desert will lie there, and their houses will be full of jackals. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will frolic there.

PAITE: Huan, ngaite a insangte uah a ham ding ua, sihalte leng a inpi nuam mahmahte uah a ham ding uh; huan, a gawt hun ding a tung sinta a, a nite leng a suksauin a om kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: Wolves will cry in their castles, and jackals in the pleasant palaces. Her time is near to come, and her days will not be prolonged.

PAITE: TOUPAN Jakobte a hehpih dinga, Israelte telin amau gam ngeingeiah lah a omsak sin ngala; Huan, gam dang miten amau a jui ding ua, Jakob inkuanpihte a lenkip ding uhi.
ENGLISH: For Yahweh will have compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land. The foreigner will join himself with them, and they will unite with the house of Jacob.

PAITE: Huan, mi chihin amaute a pi ding ua, a mun ding uh a tun ding uhi; huchiin Israel inkuanpihten TOUPA gamah amau salpa leh salnuin a nei ding ua; amau sala neimite salin a honman ding ua; amaute simmohte tungah vai a honhawm ding uhi.
ENGLISH: The peoples will take them, and bring them to their place. The house of Israel will possess them in Yahweh’s land for servants and for handmaids. They will take as captives those whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.

PAITE: Huan, na lungkhamnaa kipan bang, na buainaa kipan bang, nasep haksapipi a honsepsakna ua kipante bangin TOUPAN nang a honkhawlsak ni chiangin hichi ahi ding hi.
ENGLISH: It will happen in the day that Yahweh will give you rest from your sorrow, from your trouble, and from the hard service in which you were made to serve,

ENGLISH: that you will take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and say, “How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased!”

PAITE: TOUPAN mi gilousalou chiang a hihtanta, vaihawmmite lal chiang;
ENGLISH: Yahweh has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers,

ENGLISH: who struck the peoples in wrath with a continual stroke, who ruled the nations in anger, with a persecution that none restrained.

PAITE: Lei pumpi a khawla, a dai vungvunga; thakhatin la a sa khe guih uh.
ENGLISH: The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet. They break out song.

PAITE: A hi, na tungthu jiakin meilahte a nuam ua, Lebanon tanga sidar singte toh, Hihniama na om nungsiah phukpaitu ding himhim ka kiang uah a hongtou ngei nawn kei uh, chiin,
ENGLISH: Yes, the fir trees rejoice with you, with the cedars of Lebanon, saying, “Since you are humbled, no lumberjack has come up against us.”

PAITE: Nuailama kipan Sheol nang hongtung dawn dingin, nangmah jiakin a buai lutlut hi; misi, leia makai tengteng nangmah jiakin a tokthou a; nam chih kumpipa tengteng a laltutphah ua kipanin a kaidingta.
ENGLISH: Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. from beneath has moved for you to meet you at your coming. It stirs up the dead for you, even all the rulers of the earth. It has raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.

PAITE: Huai tengtengin nangmah biain, na kiangah hichiin a gen ding uh. Nang leng kou banga hatta lou na hi maw?
ENGLISH: They all will answer and ask you, “Have you also become as weak as we are? Have you become like us?”

PAITE: Na thupi mahmahna Sheola pi khiaksuk a hita, na kaihging lunglungte toh; tangtel na nuaiah a phah ua, thanin nang a honkhuhta uhi, chiin.
ENGLISH: Your pomp is brought down to Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. , with the sound of your stringed instruments. Maggots are spread out under you, and worms cover you.

PAITE: Sun Aksi aw, Jingsanglam tapa, bangchi dangin ahia vana kipan na kiaktak maimah! nam chih hihpukpa, bangchi danin ahia leia sat khiak suka na ommai mah.
ENGLISH: How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low!

PAITE: Na lungtangin, Van ah ka kah dinga, Pathian aksitetunglamah ka laltutphah ka tawisang ding; huan, kikhopna tang, mal tawpa omah, ka tu dinga;
ENGLISH: You said in your heart, “I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north!

PAITE: Meipi sanga sangah ka kah dinga; Tungnungpen bang maiin ka om ding, na chi nak viala.
ENGLISH: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!”

PAITE: Himahleh, Sheolah, kokhuk tawpah, pi khiak sukin lah na om sin ngala,
ENGLISH: Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol Sheol is the place of the dead. , to the depths of the pit.

PAITE: A honmu peuhin hon lim et ding ua, Hiai mi maw lei hihlinga, gam chih kisingsaka,
ENGLISH: Those who see you will stare at you. They will ponder you, saying, “Is this the man who made the earth to tremble, who shook kingdoms;

PAITE: Khovel gamdai banga bawla, a kho omte hihmanga, a salte a inlam ua pai dia pawtsak ngei lou? chiin, na tanchin a sut ding uh.
ENGLISH: who made the world like a wilderness, and overthrew its cities; who didn’t release his prisoners to their home?”

PAITE: Nam chih kumpipa tengteng, a vek un, amau in chiat uah thupi takin a ihmu ua,
ENGLISH: All the kings of the nations, sleep in glory, everyone in his own house.

PAITE: Nang bel a hunlou-a piang kihhuaitak bangin leh, gal thah, namsaua sut pailet, kokhuka thante laka pai sukte puansilh bangin na han in akipan gamlapi-a paihkhiakin na omzota hi; luang sikden bang maiin.
ENGLISH: But you are cast away from your tomb like an abominable branch, clothed with the slain, who are thrust through with the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit; like a dead body trodden under foot.

PAITE: Na gam na hihsiata, na khua na tuite na thah jiakin a lak ua vuiin nang jaw na om kei ding hi. Thil hoihlou hihmite suante min khantawnin a lou ngei kei ding uh.
ENGLISH: You will not join them in burial, because you have destroyed your land. You have killed your people. The seed of evildoers will not be named forever.

PAITE: A kisak ua, lei a neih ua, leitung khopia a dimsak louhna ding un, a pipute uh khelhna jiakin a tate uh thah ding ngaihtuah un, chiin.
ENGLISH: Prepare for slaughter of his children because of the iniquity of their fathers, that they not rise up and possess the earth, and fill the surface of the world with cities.

PAITE: Huan, amaute sual dingin ka kisa ding, sepaihte TOUPAN a chi, Babulon akipan min leh, a om zek sunte leh, tapa leh tapa tapa kahih mang ding, TOUPAN a chi.
ENGLISH: “I will rise up against them,” says Yahweh of Armies, “and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, and son and son’s son,” says Yahweh.

PAITE: Sakuh adingin gouin ka bawl dinga, dil khawngahte leng ka bawl ding; hihmanna munphiatin ka phiat lai ding, sepaihte TOUPAn a chi.
ENGLISH: “I will also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water. I will sweep it with the broom of destruction,” says Yahweh of Armies.

PAITE: Sepaihte TOUPAN hichi banga genin a kichiamta, Pellouin ka ngaihtuah bang takin a hongtung ding; ka seh bang takin leng a om ding;
ENGLISH: Yahweh of Armies has sworn, saying, “Surely, as I have thought, so shall it happen; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand:

PAITE: Ka gamah Asuria mi ka hihse dinga, ka tangte ah ka chil ek dinga, chih bangin; huai hun chiangin a hakkol uh amau akipan a mang ta dinga, a puakgik uh a liangjang ua kipanin a mang sam ding hi.
ENGLISH: that I will break the Assyrian in my land, and tread him under foot on my mountains. Then his yoke will leave them, and his burden leave their shoulders.

ENGLISH: This is the plan that is determined for the whole earth. This is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.

PAITE: Sepaihte TOUPAN a septa ngala, kuan a sut dia? a khut lah jakin a omta, kuan a lak nawn sak dia? chiin.
ENGLISH: For Yahweh of Armies has planned, and who can stop it? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?”

PAITE: Kumpipa Ahaz sih kumin hiai puakgik a hongomta.
ENGLISH: This burden was in the year that king Ahaz died.

PAITE: Philistia gam pumpi aw, nangmah vuakna chiang a kitantak jiakin kipak ken: gul zunga kipanin guldekpak a pawt sin ngala, a gah tuh gul kuang leng thei a honghi ding hi.
ENGLISH: Don’t rejoice, O Philistia, all of you, because the rod that struck you is broken; for out of the serpent’s root an adder will emerge, and his fruit will be a fiery flying serpent.

ENGLISH: The firstborn of the poor will eat, and the needy will lie down in safety; and I will kill your root with famine, and your remnant will be killed.

PAITE: Kongkhak aw, mau tuaituai in; khopi aw, kikouin; Philistia aw, na pumin na zulmang khinta; mal lama kipanin lah meikhu a hongpawt ngala, a hun seh uah tuantual himhim a om ngei kei uh.Philistia nam palaite bangchi bangin i dawng ding ua? ENGLISH: Howl, gate! Cry, city! You are melted away, Philistia, all of you; for smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.

ENGLISH: What will they answer the messengers of the nation? That Yahweh has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will take refuge.

PAITE: Moab gam puakgik. Jan khatin Moab gama Ar khua suksiatin a oma, bangmahlou-a bawlin lah a omta ngala; jan khat in Moab gama Kir khua suksiatin a oma, bangmahlou-a bawlin lah a omta ngala.
ENGLISH: The burden of Moab: for in a night, Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing; for in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing.

PAITE: Dibon tanu, mun sangtea, kap dingin a hohtoutaa; Moabten Nebo leh Medeba a kah khum ua, a lu tengteng uh a giau veka, a khamul teng uleng metin a om vekta hi.
ENGLISH: They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of their heads. Every beard is cut off.

PAITE: Huan, Heshbonte leng a kikou ua, Elealehte toh; Jahaz kho lamin leng a aw uh a ja uhi: huaijiakin Moabte galvana kivante ngaihtakin a kikou ua; a hinna uh a sung uah a ling hi.
ENGLISH: Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. Their voice is heard even to Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud. Their souls tremble within them.

PAITE: Moabte jiakin ka lungtang a kikou a; a mi hoihte uh Zoar khua leh Eglath-shelishijah ah a tai ua: Hornaim lampi ah siatna kikouin a kikou khia uhi.
ENGLISH: My heart cries out for Moab! Her nobles flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for in the way of Horonaim, they raise up a cry of destruction.

PAITE: Nimrim tuite lah hihsiatin a om sin ngal ua: loupa lah a vuai khina, loupa selnoute a vuaia, thil hing himhim lah a omta ngal kei hi.
ENGLISH: For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass fails, there is no green thing.

ENGLISH: Therefore they will carry away the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have stored up, over the brook of the willows.

PAITE: Kikou husa lah Moab gamgi kim khawngah a thang ngala; a mau tuaituai husa Eglaim khua a tungta hi.Dimon tuite lah sisanin a dim vek ngala: Dimon tungah thil thupi diak ka tungsak sin ngala, Moabte laka taikhiate tungah leh, huai gama om sunte tungah humpinelkai ka tungsak ding hi.
ENGLISH: For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.

PAITE: Dimon tuite lah sisanin a dim vek ngala: Dimon tungah thil thupi diak ka tungsak sin ngala, Moabte laka taikhiate tungah leh, huai gama om sunte tungah humpinelkai ka tungsak ding hi.
ENGLISH: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more on Dimon, a lion on those of Moab who escape, and on the remnant of the land.

PAITE: Gam vaihawmmi adingin belam noute Sela khua gamdai lama om akipanin Zion tanu tang ah khak un.

ENGLISH: For it will be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.

PAITE: Moab laka mi delhkhiaka omte na kiang ah om uhen; amau adingin hihsemi mela kipan bukna mun hi hen: lepgumi lah bangmahlou-a- bawlin a omta ngala, hihsiatna a daitaa, nuaisiahnate gama kipana hihmanthatin a omta uh.
ENGLISH: Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortioner is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.

PAITE: Huchiin laltutphah hehpihnaa hihkipin a om dinga, huai tungah, David puanin ah, mi khat, vaihawmin, vaihawmna diktat zongin, thil diktat kin taka hih pahin, chih taktakin a tu ding hi.
ENGLISH: A throne will be established in loving kindness. One will sit on it in truth, in the tent of David, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.

PAITE: Moabte kisaktheihna thu, a kisathei mahmah uh chih, ka naja ua: a suahngal dan uleh, a kisaktheih dan ulah, a hehdan thu uh; a kiotsaknate uh bangmah ahi kei hi.
ENGLISH: We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; even of his arrogance, his pride, and his wrath. His boastings are nothing.

PAITE: Hesbon loute lah a tul khinta ngala, Sibmah grep gui toh: nam chih kumpipaten a kung hoih tata akitansak phengphung ua: Jazer kho tantanin a jam ua, gamdai ah a jam lut ua; ahiangte a jam dalh sengsunga, tuipi ah a jam galkah ta.
ENGLISH: For the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have broken down its choice branches, which reached even to Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness. Its shoots were spread abroad. They passed over the sea.

ENGLISH: Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. I will water you with my tears, Heshbon, and Elealeh: for on your summer fruits and on your harvest the battle shout has fallen.

PAITE: Kipahna laksakin a omta, lou hoih taka kipanin leng nopna laksakin a omta a; grep huanah lasak himhim a omta kei dinga, husa noptuak himhim leng a om nawn sam kei ding: grep sukna khukte ah chila sukmi mi himhimin uain a chilkhe ta kei ding uh; grep laa kikou ka daisak ta.
ENGLISH: Gladness is taken away, and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there will be no singing, neither joyful noise. Nobody will tread out wine in the presses. I have made the shouting stop.

ENGLISH: This is the word that Yahweh spoke concerning Moab in time past.

ENGLISH: It will be like when the harvester gathers the wheat, and his arm reaps the grain. Yes, it will be like when one gleans grain in the valley of Rephaim.

PAITE: himahleh, oliv sing sin khita a jikpi sangpen dawna gah nihtou thumtou hiam, singgah mahmah hiang saupentea litou ngathou hiam a om sek bangin, huaiah maihkhak top ding a om laiding, Toupa Pathian in a chi hi.

ENGLISH: In that day, people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will have respect for the Holy One of Israel.

PAITE: Nang honhondampa Pathian na mangngilha, na hatna Suangpi lah na theigige ngal keia; huaijiakin kung kilawm taktakte na suan seka, a sungah hiang tuamte na vut tang niaunuau seka:
ENGLISH: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not remembered the rock of your strength. Therefore you plant pleasant plants, and set out foreign seedlings.

ENGLISH: In the day of your planting, you hedge it in. In the morning, you make your seed blossom, but the harvest flees away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.

ENGLISH: Ah, the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters!

PAITE: Nam chih lah tuipi tam pi ging hawhaw bangin a ging hawhaw ding ua; himahleh aman a taihilh dinga, huchiin gamla pi-ah a taimang ding ua, tanga buhsi huih mut bang leh leivui huihpi mut leng lunglung bang in delhin a om ding uh.Nitaklamin, ngaiin, thil mulkimhuai tak a om a; huan, khovak main lah a om nawn kei uh. ENGLISH: The nations will rush like the rushing of many waters: but he will rebuke them, and they will flee far off, and will be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.

PAITE: A, kha jap ging hawhaw gam, Ethiopia gama luite gala om,

PAITE: Tuipi ah, tui tunga tolh longte ah palaite sawlpa! Misawl hattak te aw, nam sang zehzoh mam hehot kiangah, a pawt tung ua kipan tutana mi kihtakhuai takte kiangah, hoh un; namin gam a hawm sek ua, a palpuk sek uhi, a gam uh luiten a hawmjak hi.

ENGLISH: For Yahweh said to me, “I will be still, and I will see in my dwelling place, like clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.”

PAITE: Grep loh hun maa, a pak a beia, a pak grep puama a hongom chiangin, ahiang noute theikung attanna temtain a attan sin ngala, ahiang jam dalhte a la mangin a sattan lai ding hi.
ENGLISH: For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and he will cut down and take away the spreading branches.

ENGLISH: They will be left together for the ravenous birds of the mountains, and for the animals of the earth. The ravenous birds will summer on them, and all the animals of the earth will winter on them.

PAITE: Huai hun chiangin, sepaihte TOUPA min omna mun, Zion tangah, sepaihte TOUPA kianga piak dingin Mi sang zehzoh nam pepokte kianga kipan a pawt tung ua kipan tutana mi kihtakhuai takte kianga kipan, kipahman a hontawi ding ua; huai namin gam a hawm jel ua, a palpuk behlap lai ua, a gam u lah luiten a hawmjak hi.
ENGLISH: In that time, a present will be brought to Yahweh of Armies from a people tall and smooth, even from a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of Yahweh of Armies, Mount Zion.

PAITE: Aigupta gam puakgik, Ngaiin, TOUPA meipi hattak tunga tuangin, Aigupta gam a hongtungta, Aigupta gam millimte a maah a ling vonvon ding ua, Aiguptate lungtang lah a sung uah a zulmang mai ding.
ENGLISH: The burden of Egypt: “Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble at his presence; and the heart of Egypt will melt in its midst.

ENGLISH: I will stir up the Egyptians against the Egyptians, and they will fight everyone against his brother, and everyone against his neighbor; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.

ENGLISH: The spirit of Egypt will fail in its midst. I will destroy its counsel. They will seek the idols, the charmers, those who have familiar spirits, and the wizards.

ENGLISH: I will give over the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord. A fierce king will rule over them,” says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies.

PAITE: Huan, tuipi tuite a kang ding ua, lui lah a luang mangin a kangtat ta ding.
ENGLISH: The waters will fail from the sea, and the river will be wasted and become dry.

PAITE: Luite lah a namsia uh a; Aigupta gam tuiluangte lah a kiam hiaihiai ding uh, a kang tat mai ding a; phailuangte leh tui loupate a vuai khin ding hi.
ENGLISH: The rivers will become foul. The streams of Egypt will be diminished and dried up. The reeds and flags will wither away.

PAITE: Nile lui kianga Nile lui gei mahmaha, gan tatna pawnte leh, Nile lui kianga thil chin tengtengte a hongkeu vek dinga, taihmangin a om dinga, a om nawn kei ding hi.
ENGLISH: The meadows by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile, will become dry, be driven away, and be no more.
